h

that God mentioned in this place.
Some of them said: It is
h
the spoils of war

. They said: The meaning of the statement is: Your companions ask you, O Muhammad, about the spoils that you and your companions captured on the day of Badr. To whom do they belong? Say: It belongs to God and His Messenger.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid bin Amr told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: h
They ask you about the spoils of war
, he said:
h

are the booty.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h

, he said:
h

h

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,

the spoils of war

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,

m: h

The spoils of war

, he said:

the spoils of war

h

h

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ali bin Saleh bin Hayy told us, he said:
m: It reached me regarding his statement:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
, he said: The raids.

x: Others said:
h
The spoils of war
are what the polytheists took from the Muslims, such as a slave, an animal, or the like.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war

, he said: It is what the polytheists took from the Muslims without fighting, whether it was an animal, a slave, or property. That is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do with it as he wishes.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’:
m: h
They ask you about the spoils of war

. He said: It is what the polytheists took from the Muslims without fighting, whether a male or female slave, or goods or luggage, so it is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do with it as he wishes. ...He said, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri: Ibn Abbas was asked about
h
the spoils of war
, and he said: the spoils and the horse.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: It is said:
h
The spoils of war
are what is taken from what fell from the goods after the spoils are divided, so they are a gift from God and His Messenger.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Uthman bin Abi Sulayman told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Shihab: That a man said to Ibn Abbas: What is
h
the spoils of war
? He said: The horse, the shield, and the spear.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abdul Warith bin Saeed told us, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ata’ said: Al-Anfal means the strange horse, the armor, and the garment.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: A man would give away the spoils of another man and his horse.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Malik ibn Anas told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, he said:
m: I heard a man ask Ibn Abbas about al-Anfal, and Ibn Abbas said: The horse is from
h
the spoils of war
, and
h
the spoils of war
are from
h
the spoils of war
. Then he returned to his question, and Ibn Abbas said that too. Then the man said:
h
The spoils of war

, which God said in His Book, what are they? Al-Qasim said: He kept asking him until he almost made him embarrassed, and Ibn Abbas said: Do you know what is like this? Like Subaygh, who was struck by Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of al-Qasim bin Muhammad, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Whenever Umar may God be pleased with him was asked about something, he would say: I neither command you nor forbid you. Then Ibn Abbas said: By God, God did not send His Prophet (peace be upon him) except to forbid and command, to permit and prohibit. Al-Qasim said: So he sent Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him to ask him about
h
the spoils of war

. Ibn Abbas said: A man would give a man spoils of war and his weapon. The man repeated it to him, and he said the same thing to him, then he repeated it to him until he became angry. Ibn Abbas said: Do you know what this is like? It is like Subaygh, whom Umar beat until the blood ran down his heels - or: his feet - so the man said: As for you, God has avenged Umar from you!

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’:
m: h
They ask you about the spoils of war

, he said: They ask you about what the polytheists have given to the Muslims, other than fighting, of an animal or a slave, and it is a voluntary gift to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said: The voluntary charity is the fifth that God has made for the people of the fifth.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abdul Warith bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
They ask you about the spoils of war
, he said: It is the fifth. The Muhajireen said: Why has this fifth not been lifted from us? Has it not been taken from us? God said: It is for God and the Messenger.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: That they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the fifth after the four fifths, so the following verse was revealed:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war

x: The most correct of these sayings about the meaning of
h
the spoils of war
is the saying of the one who said: They are additions that the Imam adds to some or all of the army, either from his share over their rights from the division, or from what he has attained through
h
the spoils of war

or some of its causes, as an encouragement for him and an incitement for those with him from his army to do what is in their best interest and the best interest of the Muslims, or the best interest of one of the two parties. What Ibn ʿAbbas said, that it is a horse, a shield, and the like, may be included in that, and what ʿAta’ said, that it is whatever the polytheists returned to the Muslims of a slave or a horse, may be included in that, because that is the matter of the Imam, if what they attained was not by force and coercion, he does what is in the best interest of the people of Islam, and what the army has been conquered by force may be included in that.

We said that this is the most correct statement, because nafl in Arabic speech is an addition to something. It is said: nafltk so-and-so and anfaltk if you give him more. And al-Anfal is the plural of nafl, and from it is the saying of Labid bin Rabi’ah: Fearing our Lord is the best voluntary act, and God willing, I will make it easy for you. If its meaning is what we have mentioned, then whoever is given more than his share of the spoils from the fighting army - whether that was due to a calamity he had suffered, or to his being independent of the Muslims - by the governor granting him that, then the ruling on that for him is like the spoils that the killer takes away, so what is given more than that is a voluntary gift, because the increase is a voluntary gift, and the voluntary gift, even if it is due in some cases to the rightful owner, is not from the spoils that are divided. Likewise, everything that is given to someone who does not have a share in the spoils is a voluntary gift, because even if he was overcome by it, it is not from what was divided.

The difference - if the matter is as we have described - between booty and voluntary charity is that booty is what God bestowed upon the Muslims from the wealth of the polytheists through force and subjugation, whether it was given as a gift or not, and voluntary charity is what a person was given in order to survive and make up for the army without division. Since this is the meaning of an-Nafl, the interpretation of the statement is: Your companions ask you, O Muhammad, about the surplus of the money that is divided from the spoils of the infidels of Quraysh who were killed at Badr, to whom does it belong? Say to them, O Muhammad: It belongs to God and His Messenger, not to you, and He places it where He wills. There is a difference of opinion about the reason for which this verse was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed about the spoils of Badr, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave spoils to some people who had been afflicted, and some people excelled, while others stayed behind with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they disagreed about it after the war had ended, so God revealed this verse to His Messenger, teaching them that what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did about it was permissible and permissible.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us,
m: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrating, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever comes to such and such a place will have such and such, or he does such and such, he will have such and such.’ So the young men hastened to it, and the old men remained with the banners. When God granted them victory, they came seeking what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given them, but the old men said to them: ‘Do not go with it without us!’ So God revealed to him the verse: ‘So fear God and amend that which is between you.’”

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does such and such, will have such and such. The young men hastened to do so, and the old men remained under the banners. When the spoils came, they came seeking what had been made for them, and the old men said: Do not monopolize it from us, for we were a support for you, and we were under the banners, and if you were to flee, you would flee to us! So they disputed, and God revealed: ‘
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say, “The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.
h
So fear God and amend that which is between you and obey God and His Messenger
h
if you are believers

c: Ishaq bin Shahin told me, he said, Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does such and such will have such and such of the voluntary reward. So the young men advanced, and the elders stuck to the banners, and they did not move. Then when they were victorious, the elders said: We were a support for you, so if you were defeated, you would join us, do not take the spoils without us! But the young men refused and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made it ours! So God revealed: ‘
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger. ’” He said: So that was better for them, and likewise also: Obey me, for I know best.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding this verse: “
h
They ask you about the spoils of war

. Say: ‘The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.’” He said: “When the day of Badr came, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever does such-and-such will have such-and-such of
h
the spoils of war

!’ So the young men went out and began to do it. When it was time to divide the spoils, the old men said: ‘We are the bearers of the banners, and we were a support for you!’ So God revealed regarding that: ‘Say: ‘The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.’
h
So fear God and amend that which is between you and obey God and His Messenger
h
if you are believers

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yaqub Al-Zuhri told us, he said,
m: Al-Mughira bin Abd Surat al-Anfal 8:1
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say, "
h
The spoils of war
belong to God and the Messenger.
h
So fear God and amend that which is between you and obey God and His Messenger
h
if you are believers

c: Al-Rahman told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sulayman bin Musa, on the authority of Makhul,
m: the client of Hudhayl, on the authority of Abu Salam, on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said: God revealed when the people differed over the spoils on the day of Badr:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
until His saying:
h
If you are believers
, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among them, on the authority of Buwa.

c: Ibn Humayq told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith and others of our companions told me, on the authority of Sulayman al-Ashdaq, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili, he said:
m: I asked Ubadah ibn al-Samit about al-Anfal, and he said: It was revealed about us, the companions of Badr, when we differed about the voluntary spoils and our morals deteriorated in them, so God took it out of our hands and gave it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among the Muslims equally - he said: equally - so in that was fear of God, obedience to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and reconciliation between us.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed because some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him for something from the spoils before dividing them, but he did not give it to him, as it was a share among the army, so God made all of that for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Ismail bin Musa al-Suddi told me, he said, Abu al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Musʿab bin Saʿd,
m: “On the authority of Saʿd, he said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr with a sword and said: O Messenger of God, with this sword God has cured the polytheists! So I asked him for it, and he said: This is neither for me nor for you! He said: When I turned away, I said: I am afraid that someone who has not experienced my affliction will give it to me! Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was behind me. He said: I am afraid that something has been revealed concerning me! He said: The sword has become mine! He said: So he gave it to me, and the verse, “
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
” was revealed.”

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Abu Bakr narrated to us, he said, Asim narrated to us, on the authority of Musʿab bin Saʿd,
m: “On the authority of Saʿd bin Malik, he said: When the day of Badr came, I came with a sword. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, God has healed my chest from the polytheists - or something like that - so give me this sword! He said to me: This is neither for me nor for you! So I went back and said: Perhaps this will be given to someone who has not suffered as I have! So the messenger came to me, and I said: Tell me something! When I finished, he said: O Saʿd, you asked me for the sword, and it was not mine, and now it is mine, so it is yours! And the verse was revealed: “
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I obtained a sword on the day of Badr and I liked it, so I said: O Messenger of God, give it to me! So God revealed: “
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna and Ban Wakee’ told us
m: - Ibn Al-Muthanna said: Abu Mu’awiyah told me, and Ibn Wakee’ said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us - he said: Al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Ubayd God, “on the authority of Sa’d Ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: When the day of Badr came, my brother Umair was killed, and I killed Sa’id Ibn Al-’As and took his sword, which was called “Dhu Al-Katifah,” and I brought it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Go and throw it in the fist! So I threw it and returned, and I had what only God knows about the killing of my brother and the taking of my spoils! He said: I had not gone far, until Surat Al-Anfal was revealed to him, and he said: Go and take your sword!” The wording of the hadith is from Ibn Al-Muthanna.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us,
m: all on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Bakir told me, on the authority of some of the Banu Sa’idah, he said: “I heard Abu Asid Malik bin Rabi’ah say: I obtained the sword of the Banu A’idh on the day of Badr, and the sword was called “al-Marzban.” When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to return what was in their hands of the voluntary offerings, I brought it and threw it among the voluntary offerings, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not refuse anything that he asked for, so al-Arqam bin Abi al-Arqam al-Makhzumi saw it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him and he gave it to him.”

c: Yahya bin Jaʿfar told me, he said, Ahmad bin Abi Bakr told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Imran, on the authority of his grandfather Uthman bin Al-Arqam, and on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of his grandfather, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Badr: ‘Return what was taken from the spoils!’ So Abu Usaid Al-Saʿidi put down the sword of Ibn ʿAʿidh, the satrap, and Al-Arqam recognized it and said: ‘Give it to me, O Messenger of God!’ He said: ‘So he gave it to him.’”

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shaʿbah narrated to us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Musʿab ibn Saʿd, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I obtained a sword, he said: It was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O Messenger of God, give it to me as a gift! He said: Put it down! Then he stood up and said: O Messenger of God, give it to me as a gift! He said: Put it down! Then he stood up and said: O Messenger of God, give it to me as a gift! Shall I be treated like one who has no means of support? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Put it down from where you took it! Then this verse was revealed: “
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.”

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Musʿab bin Saʿd,
m: “On the authority of Saʿd, he said: I took a sword from
h
the spoils of war
and said: O Messenger of God, give me this! So this verse was revealed: ‘
h
They ask you about the spoils of war

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war

, he said: “Saad said: I had taken the sword of Saeed bin Al-Aas bin Umayya, so I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: Give me this sword, O Messenger of God! He remained silent, then the following was revealed: “
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
,” up to His statement:
h
If you are believers
, he said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave it to me.”

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed because the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked to divide the spoils among themselves on the day of Badr, and God informed them that it was for God and His Messenger, not them, and they had no share in it. They said: The meaning of about in this place is from, and the meaning of the statement is:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. They said: Ibn Masoud used to read it:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
, according to this interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said:
m: The companions of Abdullah used to recite it:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: It is in the reading of Ibn Masoud: (They ask you for
h
the spoils of war

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: “
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say, ‘The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.’” He said:
h
The spoils of war

are the booty, and they were exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one had a share of them. Whatever the Muslim armies took of something they brought to him, so whoever withheld a needle or a thread from it, it was theft. So they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give them some of it. God said:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say, ‘The spoils are mine; I have given them to My Messenger. You have no share in them.’
h
So fear God and amend that which is between you and obey God and His Messenger
h
if you are believers

.’ Then God revealed: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils - indeed, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger. (al-Anfal 8:41) Then that fifth was divided for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for those named in the verse.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. He said: It was revealed about the Muhajireen and Ansar who were present at Badr. He said: They differed and were divided into thirds. He said: So the following was revealed: “
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.” And God gave it to His Messenger, who divided it as God showed him.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather:
m: The people asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about
h
the spoils of war
on the day of Badr, so this verse was revealed:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. ... He said, Abbad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
, he said: They ask you to give them spoils of war.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
, he said:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is that God Almighty informed us in this verse about a people who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give them
h
the spoils of war

, so God informed them that they belonged to God, and that He had made them for His Messenger. If that is what it means, then it is possible that it was revealed because of the disagreement of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and it is possible that it was because of a question from someone who asked him about the sword that we mentioned about Saad asking him about it, and it is possible that it was because of a question from someone who asked him about dividing it among the army. They differed about it: Is it abrogated or not?
Some of them said: It is abrogated. They said: It was abrogated by His statement:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of anything - a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger (al-Anfal 8
:41), the verse. Surat al-Anfal 8:1
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say, "
h
The spoils of war
belong to God and the Messenger.
h
So fear God and amend that which is between you and obey God and His Messenger
h
if you are believers
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah, they said:
m: h
The spoils of war
were for God and for the Messenger, but they were abrogated by:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of anything - a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger (al-Anfal 8

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
They ask you about the spoils of war

. He said: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas was struck by a sword on the day of Badr, and he and some people argued over it. They asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from them, and God said: “
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
. Say, ‘The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.’” The verse, so
h
the spoils of war
were specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God abrogated it with a fifth.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Salim Musa Umm Muhammad told me, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
, he said: It was abrogated by: And know that whatever you obtain of anything - a fifth of it is for God (al-Anfal 8:41).

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah - or:
m: Ikrimah and Amel - they said: Al-Anfal abrogated: And know that whatever you obtain of anything, a fifth of it is for God (al-Anfal 8:41).

x: Others said: It is decisive, and not abrogated. Rather, the meaning of that is: “Say: The spoils belong to God,” and they are undoubtedly God’s, along with the world and what is in it, and the Hereafter, and the Messenger, who places them in the places in which God commanded him to place them.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
They ask you about the spoils of war
, so he recited until he reached:
h
If you are believers

, so submit to God and His Messenger to judge over it as they wish, and to place it wherever they want, so they said: Yes! Then after forty came: And know that whatever you obtain of anything, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger (al-Anfal 8:41), and you have four-fifths. And “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Khaybar: This fifth is returned to your poor,” God and His Messenger do what they like with that fifth, and place it wherever they like.

c: Then God informed us
m: of what He likes from that. Then He recited the verse: For the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, so that it will not circulate among the rich among you (al-Hashr 59:7).

x: The correct statement in this regard is that God, the Most High, has informed us that He made
h
the spoils of war
for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give as a gift to whomever he wishes. He gave
h
the spoils of war

to the murderer as a gift, and gave the army a quarter at the beginning, and a third after a fifth upon returning. He gave a people a gift after their shares, one camel at a time, in some of the battles. So God, the Most High, made the ruling on
h
the spoils of war

for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give as a gift according to what he sees is in the best interest of the Muslims, and for the imams who come after him to follow his example in this regard. There is no evidence in the verse that its ruling has been abrogated, because it is likely to have the meaning that I mentioned and described. It is not permissible to rule that a ruling that was revealed in the Qur’an has been abrogated, except with an argument that must be accepted.

We have shown in more than one place in our books that nothing has been abrogated except that which has been invalidated by an event that has ruled otherwise, negating all of its meanings, or a report comes that requires the argument that one of them abrogates the other. It was mentioned on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab that he denied that
h
the spoils of war
were for anyone after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an interpretation of the words of God Almighty: “Say:
h
The spoils of war
belong to God and the Messenger.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, he said:
m: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab sent his slave to some people who asked him about something, and he said: You sent to me asking me about
h
the spoils of war

. There is no voluntary charity after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. We have shown that the imams may follow the example of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their battles by his actions, and they may perform voluntary acts of worship in the same way that he performed voluntary acts of worship, if the voluntary acts of worship are good for the Muslims.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
So fear God and amend that which is between you and obey God and His Messenger
h
if you are believers
A[or Jaafar said: God Almighty says: So fear God, O people, and be pious to Him by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience, and reform the situation among yourselves.
The people of interpretation differed about what was meant by his saying: And reconcile your differences.

Some of them said: It is an order from God to those who took the spoils on the day of Badr, and witnessed the battle with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they disagreed about the spoils: to return what they took from it to one another.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So fear God and amend that which is between you, he said: The Prophet of God would give a believer the spoils of a disbeliever if he killed him, then God revealed: So fear God and amend that which is between you, He commanded them to return them to one another.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: It has reached me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would give a man spoils of war according to his wealth and his ability, as he saw fit, until the day of Badr came, and the people had filled their hands with spoils of war, and the weak among the people said: The strong took the spoils! So they mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse was revealed: “Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger. So fear God and amend that which is between you,” so that the strong would respond to the weak.

x: Others said: This is a warning from God to the people, and a prohibition for them from differing in what they differed about regarding the matter of spoils and other things.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said, Khalid bin Yazid told us, and Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, they said, Abu Israel told us, on the authority of Fadil, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: So fear God and amend that which is between you, he said: It is difficult for them.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So fear God and amend that which is between you, he said: This is an encouragement from God to the believers, to fear God and amend that which is between them. Ibad said, Sufyan said: This was when they disagreed over the spoils on the day of Badr.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So fear God and amend that which is between you, meaning do not quarrel. The Arab scholars differed on the feminization of al-bayn.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He added (that) to (between), and made it (that), because some things are given a feminine noun, and some are masculine, like (the house) and (the wall), he made (the house) feminine and made (the wall)) masculine.

Some of them said: What he meant by his saying: between you is the state of the time between, so he said: And likewise at the time of the evening, meaning the time in which the evening prayer is. He said: And they did not put a masculine for the feminine, nor a feminine for the masculine, except for a meaning.
This statement is the more correct of the two statements, for the reason I mentioned for it.
As for his saying:
h
And obey God and His Messenger

, its meaning is: And, O people seeking spoils, abide by the command of God and the command of His Messenger regarding what God has bestowed upon you, for He has made clear to you its aspects and ways,
h
if you are believers
, meaning: If you believe in the Messenger of God in what he has given you from your Lord, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
So fear God and amend that which is between you and obey God and His Messenger
h
if you are believers
, so submit to God and His Messenger, so that they may rule in it as they wish, and place it where they want.

evidence.text: They said: Ibn Masoud used to read it: They ask you about the spoils of war, according to this interpretation.
Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said: The companions of Abdullah used to recite it: They ask you about the spoils of war.
Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: It is in the reading of Ibn Masoud: (They ask you for the spoils of war).
Then He recited the verse: For the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, so that it will not circulate among the rich among you (al-Hashr 59:7).

x: God Almighty says: The believer is not the one who disobeys God and His Messenger, and abandons following what He has revealed to him in His Book in His limits and obligations, and submitting to His judgment, but the believer is the one who, when God is mentioned, his heart becomes fearful, and he submits to His command, and submits to His remembrance, out of fear of Him, and fear of His punishment, and when the verses of His Book are recited to him, he believes in them, and is certain that they are from God, so his belief in that increases to his belief in what he had previously received from Him, in belief. And that is the increase in their faith in what is recited to them from God’s verses, And upon their Lord they rely, meaning: And in God they are certain, that His judgment concerning them will be carried out, so they do not hope for anyone other than Him, and they do not fear anyone other than Him.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The believers are only those who

, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, he said: The hypocrites, nothing of the remembrance of God enters their hearts when performing His obligations, and they do not believe in any of the signs of God, nor do they put their trust in God, nor do they pray when they are absent, nor do they pay the zakat on their wealth. So God, the Exalted, informed us that they are not believers, then He described the believers, saying:
h
The believers are only those who

, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, so they perform His obligations, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith, meaning belief, and upon their Lord they rely, meaning they do not hope for anyone other than Him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Those whose hearts, when God is mentioned, become fearful, he said: They become afraid. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi: Those whose hearts become fearful when God is mentioned, he said: When God is mentioned at something, his heart becomes fearful.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
The believers are only those who
, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, he said: When God is mentioned, his heart becomes fearful.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Their hearts were terrified, he said: They were afraid.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Their hearts were fearful, they were afraid. ... He said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: I heard al-Suddi say regarding His statement:
h
The believers are only those who
, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, he said: He is the man who wants to wrong - or he said: He intends to commit a sin - I think he said: So he is deterred from it.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The believers are only those who

, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, he said: Fear in the heart is like the burning of a palm branch. Do you not find it making you shiver? He said: Yes! He said: If you find that in your heart, then supplicate to God, for supplication removes that.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The believers are only those who
, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, he said: Out of fear of God, the Blessed and Exalted, and in awe of God, and in fear of God, the Blessed and Exalted. As for his saying:
h
It increased their faith
, I mentioned what Ibn Abbas said about it. And another said about it:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
m: And when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith, he said: fear.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith, and upon their Lord they rely. He said: This is a description of the people of faith, so he confirmed their description and description, so he confirmed their attribute. Surat al-Anfal 8:2
h
The believers are only those who
, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith; and upon their Lord they rely.

evidence.text: And that is the increase in their faith in what is recited to them from God’s verses, And upon their Lord they rely, meaning: And in God they are certain, that His judgment concerning them will be carried out, so they do not hope for anyone other than Him, and they do not fear anyone other than Him.

x: God Almighty says: Those who perform the obligatory prayer within its limits, and spend from the wealth that God has provided them in what God has commanded them to spend in it, from zakat, jihad, Hajj, Umrah, and spending on those whose expenses they are obligated to spend, so they fulfill their rights, those, he says: those who do these actions, are the believers, not those who say with their tongues: We have believed, while their hearts are filled with the opposite of that, hypocritically, they do not establish prayer, nor do they pay zakat. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Those who establish prayer, he says: the five daily prayers, and spend from what We have provided them, he says: the zakat of their wealth.

x: Those are the true believers, meaning: they are innocent of disbelief. Then God described hypocrisy and its people, saying: Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His messengers and wish to make distinction between God and His messengers, until His saying:
h
Those are the true disbelievers

. (al-Nisa 4:150-151), so God made the believer a true believer, and made the disbeliever a true disbeliever, which is His saying, the Most High: It is He who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer. (al-Taghabun 64:2).

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Those are the true believers, he said: They deserved faith in truth, so God made it true for them.

x: The statement in the interpretation of His saying:
h
They will have degrees with their Lord and forgiveness and generous provision

By His saying, For them are degrees, He, the Most High, means for these believers whose characteristics He, the Most High, described, degrees, which are high ranks. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding these degrees that God mentioned that they have with Him. What are they?
Some of them said: These are noble deeds and virtues that they performed during their lives.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told me, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya al-Qattat, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They will have degrees with their Lord, he said: high deeds.

x: Others said: Rather, these are ranks in Paradise.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Jabalah, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Muhairiz:
m: They will have degrees with their Lord, he said: The degrees are seventy degrees, each degree is the age of a well-trained, noble horse for seventy years. His saying: And forgiveness, meaning: pardon for their sins, and covering them up, and generous provision, it was said: Paradise. In my opinion, it is: what God has prepared for them in Paradise of more food and drink and a pleasant life.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And forgiveness, he said: for their sins, and generous provision, he said: Paradise.

x: The people of interpretation differed about the reason for this kaf in His statement: as He brought you out, and what is similar to God bringing out His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his home with the truth.

Some of them said: It is likened to it in terms of righteousness for the believers, their fear of their Lord, their reconciliation between them, and their obedience to God and His Messenger. They said: The meaning of that is that God says: And reconcile yourselves, for that is better for you, just as God brought Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of his house with the truth, and that was better for him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: So fear God and amend that which is between you and obey God and His Messenger, if you are believers, “
h
just as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth
,” the verse, meaning: This is better for you, just as bringing you out from your home with truth was better for you.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Just as your Lord, O Muhammad, brought you out of your home with the truth against the will of a group of believers, so they hate fighting, so they argue with you about it after it has become clear to them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Just as your Lord brought you out of your home with the truth, he said: Thus they argue with you about the truth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Just as your Lord brought you out of your home with the truth, so they argue with you about the truth, fighting. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
Just as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth
, he said: Thus did your Lord bring you out.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: God revealed regarding his departure - meaning the departure of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - to Badr, and their argument with him, saying: Just as your Lord brought you out from your home with the truth, although a party of the believers were averse, to the polytheists’ request,
h
They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear
, The Arabs differed on this.

x: Some of the Kufi grammarians said: This is a command from God to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to carry out his command regarding the spoils, despite the unwillingness of his companions, just as he carried out his command regarding his leaving his house to seek the caravan, and they were unwilling.

Others among them said: The meaning of this is: They ask you about the spoils of war, arguing, as they argued with you on the day of Badr, saying: You sent us out on the caravan, and you did not teach us fighting so that we could prepare for it. Some Basra grammarians said: It is possible that this kaf is in kama khuraka as He brought you out, based on his saying:
h
Those are the true believers

, “as your Lord brought you out from your home in truth.” He said: Kaaf means ala. Surat al-Anfal 8:5 Just as your Lord brought you out from your home in truth, while indeed a party of the believers were averse to it. Another of them said: It means an oath. He said: The meaning of the statement is: And the one who brought you out is your Lord.

The most correct of these sayings, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said the same thing about it as Mujahid, and he said: Its meaning is: Just as your Lord brought you forth with the truth against the will of a group of the believers, so they will argue with you about the truth after it has become clear, because both matters had happened, I mean the exit of some of those who left the city against their will, and their argument when meeting the enemy and when the people were close to each other, so likening some of that to others, with one of them being close to the other, is more appropriate to liken it to what is far from it. Mujahed said in The Truth that he mentioned that they were arguing with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after they had made it clear: It is fighting.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They argue with you about the truth, he said: fighting.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. As for his saying: From your house, some of them said: It means: From the city.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Bazza:
m: As your Lord brought you out of your home, Medina, to Badr.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Jaʿfar told me
m: regarding his statement:
h
As your Lord brought you out from your home with truth
, he said: From Medina to Badr. As for his saying: And indeed, a party of the believers are averse, their aversion was as follows:

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said,
m: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, and Yazid ibn Ruman told me, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and other scholars of ours, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, they said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of Abu Sufyan coming from the Levant, he called upon the Muslims to go to them and said: ‘This is the caravan of Quraysh with their wealth in it, so go out to it, perhaps God will give it to you!’ So the people volunteered, some of them lightly and some of them heavily, because they did not think that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would encounter war.”

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Sayyid:
m: And indeed, a party of the believers are averse, to the polytheists’ pursuit. Then the people of interpretation differed about those meant by his saying:
h
They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear

x: Some of them said: He meant by that the people of faith from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who were with him when he went to Badr to meet the polytheists.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted him about meeting the people, and Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah said to him what he said, and that was on the day of Badr, he ordered the people to get ready for the fight, and he ordered them to use force, and the people of faith hated that, so God revealed: “Just as your Lord brought you out of your home with the truth, although a party of the believers were averse. They dispute with you about the truth after it had become clear as if they were being driven to death while they were looking on.”

c: Ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Then he mentioned the people - meaning the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - and their march with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the people knew that Quraysh had marched against them, and that they had only gone out seeking the caravan in the hope of spoils, so he said:
h
As your Lord brought you out from your home with truth
, until his saying: unwillingly, meaning out of hatred for meeting the people, and in denial of Quraysh’s march when they mentioned it to them.

x: Others said: He meant the polytheists.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear as if they were being driven to death while they are looking on

, he said: These are the polytheists, they argued with him about the truth, as if they were being driven to death when they were called to Islam, while they are looking on, he said: This is not a description of the others, this is a description that was introduced for the people of disbelief.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yaqub bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told me, on the authority of my nephew Al-Zuhri, on the authority of his uncle, he said:
m: A man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to interpret: As if they were being driven to death while they were looking on, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, going out to the caravan.

x: The correct statement about that is what Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Ishaq said, that it is report from God about a group of believers who hated to meet the enemy, and their argument with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was that they said: (He did not teach us that we would meet the enemy and prepare to fight them, but we went out for the caravan). And what indicates its correctness is his statement: And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours, and you wished that the one without the power would be yours, so in that is clear evidence for whoever understands from God, that the people hated the power, and that their argument was about fighting, as Mujahid said, out of their hatred for it, and that what Ibn Zayd said has no meaning, because what preceded his statement:
h
They argue with you about the truth
, is report about the people of faith, and what follows it is report about them, so it is more appropriate for it to be report about them than it is report about someone who was not mentioned.
As for his saying:
h
After it became clear
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.
Some of them said: It means:
h
After it became clear
to them that you do nothing but what God has commanded you.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
After it became clear
that you do nothing except what God has commanded you to do.

x: Others said: It means: They argue with you about fighting after you were ordered to do so.
Who said that? Al-Kalbi narrated, on the authority of Abu Saleh, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. As for his saying:
h
As if they are being driven to death while they are looking on

, its meaning is: As if these people who argue with you about meeting the enemy, out of their hatred of meeting them if they are called to meet them for fighting, are being driven to death. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq said:
m: As if they were being led to death while they were watching, meaning out of aversion to meeting the people, and denial of the Quraysh’s march when they were told about it to them.

x: God Almighty says: And remember, O people,
h
And when God promised you one of the two parties
, meaning one of the two groups, the group of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and the caravan, and the group of the polytheists who fled from Mecca to prevent their caravan. And his saying:
h
It is yours

, meaning: that what they have is spoils for you. And you would like that the one without power should be yours, meaning: and you would like that group that has no power - meaning: it has no limits, and there is no fighting in it - to be yours. He says: you would like that the caravans in which there is no fighting should be yours, without the group of Quraysh who came to protect their caravan, who would fight and war against them. The origin of the word thorn is from thorns. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Nasr and Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad narrated to us, they said: Abdul Samad bin Abdul Warith narrated to us, he said: Aban Al-Attar narrated to us, he said: Hisham bin Urwah narrated to us, on the authority of Urwah:
m: Abu Sufyan and the Quraysh riders who were with him came from Ash-Sham, and they took the coastal route. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of them, he called his companions and told them about the wealth they had and how few they were in number. So they went out, intending none but Abu Sufyan and the riders with him, seeing them as nothing but booty for them, not thinking that there would be a great fight if they saw them. And this is what God revealed about it:
h
And you wish that the one without power should be yours

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri,
m: and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, and Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, and Yazid ibn Ruman, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others of our scholars, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, each of whom narrated to me some of this hadith, and their hadiths were gathered in what I have cited of the hadith of Badr. They said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of Abu Sufyan coming from Syria, he summoned the Muslims to them and said: ‘This is the caravan of Quraysh, in which is their wealth, so go out to it, for God’s sake, do not let them take it from you!’ So the people volunteered, some of them lightly and some of them were heavy, because they did not think that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would encounter war. Abu Sufyan was certain when he approached the Hijaz and was looking for report, and asking whoever he met of the riders, fearing for the people’s wealth, until he received report from one of the riders: ‘Muhammad has mobilized his companions for you and your caravan!’ So he was cautious at that time, and hired Damdam ibn Amr.” Al-Ghafari, so he sent him to Mecca, and ordered him to go to the Quraysh and mobilize them to defend their wealth, and to inform them that Muhammad had attacked it with his companions. So Damdam bin Amr quickly set out for Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with his companions until he reached a valley called Dhafran, so he went out from it, until he was in some part of it, and the report came to him from the Quraysh about their march to prevent their caravan, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted the people, and informed them about the Quraysh. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said, Good. Then Umar, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said, Good. Then Al-Miqdad bin Amr stood up and said, “O Messenger of God, go where God has commanded you, for we are with you. By God, we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Moses, ‘Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.’” (al-Ma’idah 5:24), but rather, “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are with you, fighting!” By Him Who sent you with the truth, if you march with us to Bark al-Ghamad - meaning: the city of Abyssinia - we will fight with you until you reach it! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said something good to him, then he prayed for good for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Advise me, O people! He only wants the Ansar, because they were the number of people, and when they pledged allegiance to him at al-Aqabah, they said: O Messenger of God, we are free from your protection until you reach our homes, and when you reach us, then you are under our protection, and we will protect you as we protect our sons and women. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was afraid that the Ansar would not see it as their duty to support him except to those of his enemy who attacked him in Medina, and that it would not be their duty to march with them to an enemy from their country. He said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that, Saʿd ibn Muʿadh said to him: It seems that you want us, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes! He said: We have believed in you and confirmed your truth, and we testify that what you have brought is the truth, and we have given you our pledges and covenants to hear and obey. So go, O Messenger of God, to what you wish. By Him Who sent you with the truth, if you were to parade us across this sea and cross it, we would cross with you. Not a single man of us would stay behind. We would not mind if you were to meet our enemy tomorrow. We are patient in war and truthful when we meet. Perhaps God will show you from us something that will please your eyes. So go with us with God’s blessing! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with Saʿd’s words and it encouraged him. Then he said: Go with God’s blessing and be glad, for God has promised me one of the two groups. By God, it is as if I am now seeing the place where the people will be killed tomorrow.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: “Abu Sufyan came with a caravan from the Levant in which there was a Quraysh trade, and it was al-Latimah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed that it had come, so he mobilized the people, and three hundred and a few men went out with him. So he sent a spy from Juhaynah, an ally of the Ansar, called Ibn Urayqit, and he brought him report of the people. Abu Sufyan was informed of the departure of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he sent to the people of Mecca to ask for their help, so he sent a man from Banu Ghafar called Damdam ibn Amr, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out without knowing about the departure of Quraysh, so God informed him of their departure, so he feared that the Ansar would abandon him and say: We promised to protect you if anyone wanted to attack you in our country! So he went to his companions and consulted them about seeking the caravan, and Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, said to him: I have taken this road, so I know it, and the man left them at such and such a place.” And so. The Prophet (peace be upon him) remained silent, then he returned to consult them, and they began to advise him about the caravan. When he had consulted them more, Saʿd ibn Muʿadh spoke and said: O Messenger of God, I see that you consult your companions and they advise you, and you return to consult them, as if you are not satisfied with what they advise you, and as if you fear that the Ansar will stay behind you! You are the Messenger of God, and the Book was revealed to you, and God has commanded you to fight, and promised you victory, and God does not break His promise. Proceed with what you have been commanded to do, for by He who sent you with the truth, not a single one of the Ansar will stay behind you! Then Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad Al-Kindi stood up and said: O Messenger of God, we do not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Moses: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here” (Al-Maʿidah: 24), but we say: Go forward and fight, we are fighting with you! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was pleased with that and said: My Lord has promised me the people, and they have come out, so go to them! So they went.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours

, and you wished that the one without power would be yours, he said: The two parties, one of them: Abu Sufyan bin Harb when he came with the caravan from Ash-Sham, and the other party: Abu Jahl with him a group of Quraysh. So the Muslims hated the power and the fighting, and they wanted to meet the caravan, and God willed what He willed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when God promised you one of the two parties

, he said: The caravan of the people of Mecca came - meaning: from Ash-Sham - and the people of Medina heard about that, so they went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intending to meet the caravan. The people of Mecca heard about that, so they hastened to travel to it, so that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions would not be defeated. The caravan outran the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God had promised them one of the two parties, so it was more pleasing to them to meet the caravan, and it was easier to prevent a thorn, and it brought more booty. When the caravan outran and missed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with the Muslims intending to meet the people, but the people disliked their travel because of a thorn in the people.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours

, and you wished that the one without power would be yours, he said: They meant the caravan. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Medina in the month of Rabi’ al-Awwal, and Kurz bin Jabir al-Fihri raided, intending to raid Medina until he reached al-Safra’. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about it and rode after him, but Kurz bin Jabir outran him. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and established his tradition. Then Abu Sufyan headed to the Levant with a caravan of Quraysh, and when he was close to Badr, Gabriel came down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and revealed to him:
h
And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours

, and you wished that the one without power Surat al-Anfal 8:7 And when God promised you that one of the two parties would be yours, and you wished that the one without power would be yours. And God intended to establish the truth by His words and to eliminate the disbelievers. would be yours, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with all the Muslims, and they were at that time three hundred and thirteen men, two hundred and seventy of them from the Ansar, and the rest from the Muhajirun. The report reached Abu Sufyan while he was in Al-Batam, so he sent to all of Quraysh who were in Mecca, and Quraysh were frightened and angry.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours

, and you wished that the one without power would be yours, he said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, had come down and informed him of the march of the Quraysh and they were going to take their caravan, and he promised him either the caravan or the Quraysh, and that was at Badr, and they took the water-carriers and asked them, and they informed them, so that is what His saying: and you wished that the one without power would be yours, they are the people of Mecca.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And you wish that the one without power should be yours

, to the end of the verse, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Badr and they wanted to intercept a caravan of Quraysh. He said: Satan came out in the form of Suraqah ibn Ju’sham, until he came to the people of Mecca and seduced them, and said: Muhammad and his companions have intercepted your caravan! And he said: No one among the people like you can overcome you today, and I will protect you from being on what God hates! So they went out and called out that none of us should stay behind except that we will demolish his house and take it as a ransom! And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions took al-Ruha’, a spring for the people, and he informed him about them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has promised you the caravan or the people! So the caravan was more beloved to the people than the people, the fighting was over the power, and the caravan is not about fighting.” And that is the statement of God Almighty:
h
And you wish that the one without power should be yours
. He said: (The thorn), the fight, and (other than the thorn), the donkey.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yaqub bin Muhammad al-Zuhri told us, he said, Abdullah bin Wahb told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Abi Imran, on the authority of Abi Ayoub, who said:
m: God Almighty revealed:
h
And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours
, so when we promised one of the two parties that it would be ours, our souls were at peace. And the two parties is the caravan of Abi Sufyan, or the Quraysh.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Aslam Abu Imran al-Ansari - I think he
m: said: Abu Ayoub said -
h
And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours

, and you wished that the one without the power would be yours, they said: The one without the power is the people, and the one without the power is the caravan. So when God promised us one of the two parties, either the caravan or the people, our souls were at peace.
b.via: Aslam Abu Imran al-Ansari - I think he

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yaqub bin Muhammad told me, he said, more than one person told me
m: regarding his statement: And you would like that you have those who have no power, that the power is Quraysh.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And you wish that the one without power should be yours

, that it was the caravan of Abu Sufyan. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wished that the caravan was theirs and that the fighting had been diverted from them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And you would like that the one without the power be yours, meaning: the spoils without the war. As for his saying:
h
It is yours
, it was opened with the repetition of promises, and that is because his saying: God promises you, has worked on one of the two groups. The interpretation of the statement:
h
And when God promised you one of the two parties
, He promised you that one of the two parties would be yours, as He said: Do they await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly?
r
(Muhammad 47:18)

. He said: And you would like the one without power to be yours, so he made with feminine because it refers to the group. The meaning of the statement is: And you would like the group that is not powerful to be yours, rather than the group with power.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And God wants to establish the truth with His words and to eradicate the disbelievers

God Almighty says: And God wants to establish Islam and make it supreme, with His words, meaning: by His command to you, O believers, to fight the infidels, while you want the spoils and money. And His saying: And to cut off the root of the infidels, meaning: He wants to destroy the root of those who deny the oneness of God. We have previously explained the meaning of daber and that it is the last, and that the meaning of cut it off is to come upon all of them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the statement of God: And God intends to establish the truth with His words, that he should kill those whom he wanted to eradicate. This is better for you than the caravan.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And God wants to establish the truth with His words and to cut off the roots of the disbelievers, meaning: the battle that He inflicted on the leaders and chiefs of Quraysh on the day of Badr.

x: God Almighty says: And God wants to cut off the roots of the disbelievers, so that the truth may be established, so that God alone may be worshipped without gods and idols, and Islam may be widespread, and that is (the establishment of the truth), and falsehood may be nullified, meaning: and the worship of gods and idols and disbelief may be nullified, even if those who committed crimes and acquired sins and burdens from the disbelievers hate that.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So that the truth may be established and falsehood may be abolished, even though the criminals may hate it, meaning the polytheists. It was said: The truth in this place is God Almighty.

x: God Almighty says: And falsehood is nullified, when
h
you seek help from your Lord
, so when is a connection to nullifies. The meaning of his saying:
h
You seek help from your Lord

, is that you seek refuge in Him from your enemy, and you call upon Him for victory over them, and He answered you, meaning: He answered your prayer, that I will support you with a thousand angels, one following the other, and one following the other.
The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that, and the narration came from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
The report mentioned that:

c: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Maharibi told me, he said, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ikrimah ibn Ammar, he said, Samak al-Hanafi told me, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, told me, he said: “When the day of Badr came, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at the polytheists and their number, and looked at his companions, who numbered more than three hundred, he faced the qiblah and began to supplicate, saying: O God, fulfill for me what You promised me. O God, if You destroy this group of the people of Islam, You will not be worshipped on earth! He continued like that until his cloak fell off, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, took him and put his cloak over him, then embraced him from behind, then said: It is sufficient for you, O Prophet of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, to implore your Lord, for He will fulfill for you what He promised you! So God revealed: ‘When you called upon your Lord, and He answered you, “
h
I will reinforce you with a thousand angels
, following one another.”’”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “When the people lined up, Abu Jahl said: O God, give us the right, so support him! And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hand and said: O Lord, if this group is destroyed, you will never be worshipped on earth!”

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said: O God, our Lord, You have sent down the Book to me, and You have commanded me to fight, and You have promised me victory, and You do not break Your promise! So Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him, and God revealed: ‘Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come to you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks. ’”
r
Abu Al-Sa’ib narrated to me, saying:

c: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zaid bin Yathi’, who said:
m: “Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hut, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to supplicate, saying: O God, support this group, for if you do not do so, you will not be worshipped on earth!” Abu Bakr said: Some of your entreats will fulfill what he promised you.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to call upon God, seeking His help and seeking His victory, so God sent down the angels upon him.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When you called upon your Lord for help
, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: When you sought help from your Lord, meaning: with your supplications, when they saw the great number of their enemy and their small number, and He answered you, with the supplication of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and your supplication with him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said:
m: “When the day of Badr came, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to implore his Lord with the most intense entreaty, so Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, came to him and said: O Messenger of God, some of your entreaties, by God, God will fulfill to you what He promised you!” As for his saying:
h
I will reinforce you with a thousand angels
