, one after the other, we have explained its meaning. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
I will reinforce you with a thousand angels
, one after the other, he says: more, as you say: Go to the man and give him more such and such.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ahmad bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Harun bin Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: In succession, he said: in succession. ... He said, my father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us, he said: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He will reinforce you with a thousand angels, one after the other, he said: Behind every angel is an angel.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Kadina Yahya bin Al-Muhallab, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: In succession, he said: in succession. ... He said, Hani’ bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Arta’ah, on the authority of Qabus, who said: I heard Abu Dhibyan say: In succession, he said: The angels, one after the other. ... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: In succession, he said: one after the other.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his saying: Murdifin, he said: Extended. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Katheer, he said: Murdifin, (Irdaaf) means providing them with support.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told me, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
With a thousand angels in succession
meaning: in succession.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
With a thousand angels in succession
, one following the other.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: in succession, he said: in succession, one after the other, following one another.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein
m: that he said, I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
With a thousand angels in succession
, he said: in succession, on the day of Badr. The Qur’an differed in reading this. So I read it as most of the people of Medina read: mardafin two pairs, with the dāl in the accusative case.

x: Some of the Meccans, the majority of the Kufi reciters, and the majority of the Kufi and Basri reciters read it as mardafin. Abu Amr used to read it in this way, and he said, as was reported from him: It is from some of them followed each other.

Some scholars of Arabic speech denied this statement of Abu Amr and said: Al-Irdaaf means that a man carries his companion behind him. He said: This was not heard in the description of the angels on the day of Badr. Scholars of Arabic speech differed about the meaning of that if it is read with a fatha on the dal or a kasra on it.

Some of the Basrans and Kufians said: The meaning of this, if it is read with the kasra, is that the angels came following one another, in the language of those who say: (I rode behind him). They said: The Arabs say: (I rode behind him) and (I rode behind him), meaning (I followed him) and (I followed him).

i: And the evidence for the validity of their saying that is what the poet said:
x: If Gemini follows the Pleiades, I will have bad thoughts about the family of Fatima.

They said: So the poet said: I followed it, but he meant I followed it, meaning it came after it, because Gemini comes after the Pleiades. They said: Its meaning, if it is read mardafin in Surat al-Anfal 8:9 When you sought help from your Lord, and He responded to you, "
h
I will reinforce you with a thousand angels
, following one another." succession, is that it is the object of the verb, as if its meaning is: with a thousand angels, God sends some of them behind others.
Others said: The meaning of this, if the dal is broken, is: the angels followed one another, and if it is read with a fatha, it is: God followed the Muslims with them.

The correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read: with a thousand angels following one another, with a kasra on the dal, because the people of interpretation have agreed upon what I mentioned of their interpretation, that its meaning is: some of them follow one another, and in succession. So in their consensus on this interpretation, there is clear evidence that the correct reading is what we have chosen in this regard, with a kasra on the dal, meaning: some of the angels followed one another. And it is heard from the Arabs: (I came riding behind so-and-so), meaning: I came after him. As for the statement of those who said: The meaning of that, if it is read mardafin with the opening of the dal, is that God sent the Muslims behind them, then this statement has no meaning, since the mention in mardafin is from the angels, not the believers.

Rather, the meaning of the statement is: that He will support you with a thousand angels, some of them following others. Then the mention of the agent was deleted, and the report was brought out without naming its agent, so it was said: mardafin, meaning some angels following others. If the matter were as the one we mentioned said, then those who ride behind each other would have to mention Muslims, not angels. This is contrary to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the Qur’an.
Another reading has been mentioned, which is:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said,
m: Abdullah bin Yazid said, Mardafin and Mardafin and Mardafin are heavy with the meaning: Mardafin riding on two backs.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yaqub bin Muhammad al-Zuhri told us, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Imran told me, on the authority of al-Zumai, on the authority of Abu al-Huwayrith, on the authority of Muhammad bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: Gabriel descended with a thousand angels on the right side of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was in it, and Michael, peace be upon him, descended with a thousand angels on the left side of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was in it.

evidence.text: So I read it as most of the people of Medina read: mardafin two pairs, with the dāl in the accusative case.
Some of the Meccans, the majority of the Kufi reciters, and the majority of the Kufi and Basri reciters read it as mardafin.
Abu Amr used to read it in this way, and he said, as was reported from him: It is from some of them followed each other.
Scholars of Arabic speech differed about the meaning of that if it is read with a fatha on the dal or a kasra on it.
Some of the Basrans and Kufians said: The meaning of this, if it is read with the kasra, is that the angels came following one another, in the language of those who say: (I rode behind him).

They said: Its meaning, if it is read mardafin in Surat al-Anfal 8:9 When you sought help from your Lord, and He responded to you, "I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another." succession, is that it is the object of the verb, as if its meaning is: with a thousand angels, God sends some of them behind others.
Others said: The meaning of this, if the dal is broken, is: the angels followed one another, and if it is read with a fatha, it is: God followed the Muslims with them.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read: with a thousand angels following one another, with a kasra on the dal, because the people of interpretation have agreed upon what I mentioned of their interpretation, that its meaning is: some of them follow one another, and in succession.

So in their consensus on this interpretation, there is clear evidence that the correct reading is what we have chosen in this regard, with a kasra on the dal, meaning: some of the angels followed one another.

As for the statement of those who said: The meaning of that, if it is read mardafin with the opening of the dal, is that God sent the Muslims behind them, then this statement has no meaning, since the mention in mardafin is from the angels, not the believers.

x: God Almighty says: God did not make the angels following one another and following one another in coming to you, O believers, as support for you, except as good tidings, for you, meaning: good tidings for you, giving you good report of God’s victory for you over your enemies, and that your hearts may be reassured thereby, meaning: and that your hearts may be reassured by its coming to you, and be certain of God’s victory for you, and victory is only from God, meaning: and you are not victorious over your enemy, O believers, except that God grants you victory over them, not by the strength of your power and strength, but by God’s victory for you, because that is in His hand and to Him, He grants victory to whomever He wills of His creation, Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise, meaning: God is the One who grants you victory, and in His hand is the victory of whomever He wills of His creation, Exalted in Might, nothing can subdue Him, and no one can overcome Him, rather He subdues and overcomes everything, because He created it, Wise, meaning: He is wise in His management, and He supports those He supports, and He lets down those He lets down among His creation. There is no weakness or defect in His management.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer on the authority of Mujahid
m: regarding this, what: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Kathir told me that he heard Mujahid say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not extend more than a thousand angels in succession from what God mentioned, and he mentioned the three and the five as good report. They did not extend more than this thousand that God Almighty mentioned in Al-Anfal. As for the three and the five, they were good report. We have discussed this in Surah Al Imran, sufficiently.
b.via: Abdullah bin Katheer on the authority of Mujahid

x: God Almighty says: And that your hearts may be reassured thereby, “When drowsiness overtakes you,” and what He means by His statement: overtakes you, is that He casts drowsiness upon you. A security, meaning: a security from God for you from your enemy overpowering you. Likewise, drowsiness in war is a security from God Almighty.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: Drowsiness in battle is a security from God Almighty, and in prayer it is from Satan.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us
m: regarding his statement: (Drowsiness overtakes you as a security from Him), on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Abdullah, something similar, he said: Abdullah said, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razeen, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: something similar. Security is a noun derived from the saying: I am safe from such-and-such, security, and safety, and all of these have the same meaning. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Safety from Him, safety from God Almighty. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Amenah, he said: A security from God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement:
h
When drowsiness overcame you as a security from Him
, he said: God Almighty sent down drowsiness as a security from the fear that afflicted them on the day of Uhud. Then he recited: Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security, drowsiness
r
(Al Imran 3:154)
. There is a difference in the reading of His statement:
h
When drowsiness overtakes you as a security from Him

. The majority of the people of Medina read it as: (Nausea overwhelms you), with a damma on the ya’ and a light shin, and the accusative of (na’as), from (God has covered them with drowsiness, so He covers them). The majority of the Kufians read it as: yaghshikum, with a damma on the ya’ and a shaddah on the shin, from: (God covered them with drowsiness, so He covers them). Some Meccans and Basrans read it as: (Naa’s overwhelms you), with the opening of the ya’ and raising of (na’as), meaning: (Naa’s overwhelms them, so it overwhelms them). They also cited as evidence for the correctness of their reading the words of God in Al Imran 3:A group will be covered
r
(Al Imran 3:154)

x: The most correct of these is: When He covers you, according to what I mentioned from the reading of the Kufians, because all the reciters agree on the reading of His statement:
h
And He sends down upon you water from the sky
, by directing that to the fact that it is from the action of God Almighty. So it is also necessary that He covers you be like this, since His statement:
h
And He sends down
, is in apposition to He covers, so that the speech is consistent in one way. As for the words of God Almighty:
h
And He sends down
upon you from the sky
h
water to purify you thereby

, this is rain that God sent down from the sky on the day of Badr to purify the believers for their prayer, because they had become ritually impure that day without water. So when God sent down water upon them, they washed themselves and purified themselves. Satan had whispered to them what had saddened them about their becoming ritually impure without water, so God removed that from their hearts with the rain.

This is how He bound their hearts together, strengthened their reasons, and made their feet firm with that rain, because they had met their enemy on the sand of Mithaa, and the rain covered it until the feet were firm on it and did not sink in it, as a preparation from God Almighty for His Prophet, peace be upon him, and his friends, the reasons for being able to defeat their enemy and triumph over them. And similar to what we said, the report continued from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God Surat al-Anfal 8:11 When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him and sent down upon you from the sky
h
water to purify you thereby
and remove from you the defilement of Satan that He might strengthen your hearts and make firm thereby your feet. bless him and grant him peace, and other people of knowledge.
Mentioning the report reported about that:

c: Harun ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Musʿab ibn al-Muqaddam narrated to us, Israʿil narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Haritha, on the authority of ʿAli,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: We were struck by a heavy downpour of rain at night - meaning the night in the morning of which the Battle of Badr took place - so we went under a tree and a rock to seek shade from the rain. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spent the night supplicating to his Lord: O God, if this group is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on earth! When dawn broke, he called out: Prayer, servants of God! So the people came from under the trees and rocks, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in prayer and urged people to fight.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath and Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab:
m: Water to purify you with it, he said: He was drowned on the day of Badr.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yazid told me, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Saeed,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Uday and Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of al-Sha’bi and Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, they said:
m: He was struck on the day of Badr.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab regarding this verse:
h
And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby
and remove from you the impurity of Satan, they said: Tash was on the day of Badr, and God made the feet firm with it.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: (
h
When drowsiness overtakes you as a security from Him

) the verse, he mentioned to us that they had rain on that day until the valley flowed with water, and they fought on a dusty dune, so God covered it with water, and the Muslims drank and performed ablution and gave others to drink, and God removed from them the whisperings of Satan.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped - meaning: when he marched to Badr - and there was a flat sand between the Muslims and the water, so the Muslims were severely weakened, and Satan cast rage into their hearts, and whispered among them: You claim that you are the friends of God and that His Messenger is among you, and the polytheists have defeated you at the water, and you are praying in a state of ritual impurity! So God rained down heavy rain upon them, so the Muslims drank and purified themselves, and God removed from them the impurity of Satan, and the sand stood firm when the rain fell upon it, and people and animals walked on it, so they marched to the people, and God reinforced His Prophet with a thousand angels, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, was with five hundred angels, and Michael was with five hundred angels, and Michael was with five hundred.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: (
h
When drowsiness overtakes you as a security from Him

) until His statement: And makes the feet firm thereby, that is because when the polytheists of Quraysh went out to support the caravan and fight on its behalf, they stopped at the water on the day of Badr, and they overpowered the believers there, so the believers became thirsty, so they began to pray while ritually impure and in a state of minor ritual impurity, until that became great in the hearts of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God sent down water from the sky until the valley overflowed, so the Muslims were filled with joy, and they filled their water skins and gave water to the riders, and they washed themselves from major ritual impurity, so God made that a means of purification and made the feet firm. That is because there was sand between them and the people, so God sent rain upon it, and it struck it until it became strong, and the feet were firm upon it.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims were at the water of Badr, the polytheists preceded them and they camped there, and Abu Sufyan and his companions turned towards the sea, and they set out. He said: They camped at the top of the valley, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, camped at the bottom. A man from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, would become ritually impure and not be able to reach the water, so he would pray while ritually impure. Satan cast his thoughts into their hearts and said: How do you hope to prevail over them, while one of you stands up to pray while ritually impure and without performing ablution? He said: So God sent rain upon them, so they washed themselves, performed ablution, and drank, and the ground became hard for them, and it was a flat plain in which their feet could enter, so it became hard for them from the rain, and they struggled on it.”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: The polytheists defeated the Muslims in the beginning of their affair in terms of water, so the Muslims became thirsty and prayed in a state of ritual impurity and minor ritual impurity, and there was sand between them. So Satan cast sadness into the hearts of the believers and said: You claim that there is a prophet among you and that you are the friends of God, yet you have defeated them in terms of water, and you pray in a state of ritual impurity and minor ritual impurity! He said: So God, the Almighty, sent down water from the sky, and it flowed in every valley, so the Muslims drank and purified themselves, and their feet became firm, and the whisperings of Satan went away.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Water to purify you thereby

, he said: The rain, He sent it down upon them before drowsiness, The filth of Satan, he said: His whisperings. He said: So the rain extinguished the dust, and the earth was covered with it, and their souls were content with it, and their feet were firm with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Water to purify you thereby
, He sent it down upon them before drowsiness, the rain covered the dust, and the earth was covered with it, and their souls were pleased with it, and their feet were firm with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Water to purify you thereby

, he said: rain, and remove from you the defilement of Satan, his whisperings. He extinguished the dust with the rain, covered the earth with it, and their souls were content with it and their feet were firm with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The devil’s filth and his whispering.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby

, he said: This is on the day of Badr, He sent down rain upon them, and to remove from you the defilement of Satan, which he cast into your hearts: You have no power over these people!, and to strengthen your hearts and plant firmly thereby your feet.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
When drowsiness overtakes you as a security from Him

, until His statement: And makes firm thereby the feet, that the polytheists camped at the water on the day of Badr and defeated the Muslims there. The Muslims became thirsty and prayed while in a state of ritual impurity and ritual impurity. Satan cast sadness into the hearts of the believers and whispered in them: You claim that you are the friends of God and that Muhammad is the Prophet of God, and you have defeated them at the water, and you pray while in a state of ritual impurity and ritual impurity! So God rained rain until every valley overflowed. The Muslims drank and filled their water skins, watered their animals, and washed themselves from ritual impurity, and God made firm thereby their feet. This is because there was a sand dune between them and their enemy that animals could not cross and a pedestrian could only walk with difficulty. So God struck it with rain until it became intense and their feet became firm there.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
When drowsiness overcame you as a security from Him

), meaning: He sent down security upon you so that you slept without fear, and He sent down upon you water from the sky, for the rain that fell upon them that night, so the polytheists were prevented from getting to the water before them, and He left the way for the believers to it, that He may purify you thereby and remove from you the defilement of Satan and strengthen your hearts and make firm thereby your feet, so that Satan’s doubts may be removed from them, by frightening them with their enemy, and making the earth smooth for them, until they reached their home to which they had been before their enemy.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: Then he mentioned what Satan had cast into their hearts regarding major ritual impurity and their standing up to pray without performing ablution, and he said: “When He causes drowsiness to overtake you as a security from Him and sends down upon you from the sky
h
water to purify you thereby
and remove from you the impurity of Satan and to strengthen your hearts and make firm thereby your feet,” when you are struggling on the sand, which is like the form of the earth.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, he said: A man said
m: in the presence of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab - and he said once: he recited -
h
And He sends down
upon you from the sky
h
water to purify you thereby
, so Saeed said: It is:
h
And He sends down
upon you from the sky
h
water to purify you thereby
. He said: Al-Sha’bi said: That was a great storm on the day of Badr.

x: Some of the people of Basra who are knowledgeable about the strange have claimed that the metaphor of his saying:
h
And He makes the feet firm thereby means that He pours patience upon them and sends it down upon them

, so that they become firm against their enemy. This is a statement that contradicts the statement of all the people of interpretation from the Companions and the Followers, and it is enough for the statement to be wrong to be contrary to the statement of those we mentioned, and we have explained their statements about it, and that its meaning is: And He makes firm the feet of the believers by covering the sand with rain so that their feet and the hooves of their animals do not sink into it.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of His statement: When drowsiness overtakes you as a security from Him.

The majority of the people of Medina read it as: (Nausea overwhelms you), with a damma on the ya’ and a light shin, and the accusative of (na’as), from (God has covered them with drowsiness, so He covers them).
The majority of the Kufians read it as: yaghshikum, with a damma on the ya’ and a shaddah on the shin, from: (God covered them with drowsiness, so He covers them).
Some Meccans and Basrans read it as: (Naa’s overwhelms you), with the opening of the ya’ and raising of (na’as), meaning: (Naa’s overwhelms them, so it overwhelms them).
They also cited as evidence for the correctness of their reading the words of God in Al Imran 3:A group will be covered (Al Imran 3:154).

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these is: When He covers you, according to what I mentioned from the reading of the Kufians, because all the reciters agree on the reading of His statement: And He sends down upon you water from the sky, by directing that to the fact that it is from the action of God Almighty.

x: As for his saying:
h
When your Lord inspired to the angels

, ‘I am with you,’ I will support you, ‘so strengthen those who believe,’ he says: strengthen their resolve and correct their intention in what their enemy among the polytheists said. It has been said that the angels’ confirmation of the believers was their presence during their war with them. It was said: This was their assistance to them in fighting their enemies. It was also said: This was when the angel came to a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I heard these people - meaning the polytheists - say: By God, if they attack us, we will be defeated! So the Muslims would tell each other about this, and their souls would be strengthened. They said: This was God’s revelation to His angels.
As for Ibn Ishaq, he said:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: So strengthen those who believe, meaning: support those who believe.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve
, so strike upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip.
God Almighty says: I will terrify the hearts of those who disbelieve in Me, O believers, among you, and fill them with fear until they flee from you, So strike above the necks.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying: above the necks.
Some of them said: It means: Strike the necks.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
Then strike above the necks

, he said: Strike the necks. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Al-Qasim, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was not sent to punish with the punishment of God. I was only sent to strike necks and tighten bonds.”

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Then strike above the necks

, meaning: Strike the necks. The authors of this article argued that the Arabs say: I saw the soul of so-and-so, meaning: I saw him. They said: Likewise, his saying: strike above the necks, means: strike the necks.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is, hit the heads.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
Then strike above the necks

, he said: the heads. The proponents of this article argued that what is above the necks is the heads. They said: It is not permissible to say above the necks, so that its meaning is the necks. They said: Even if that were permissible, it would be permissible to say under the necks, so that its meaning would be the necks. They said: That is contrary to what is reasonable in speech, and a reversal of the meanings of the speech.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Strike on the necks. They said: On and above have similar meanings, so it is permissible for one of them to be placed in place of the other.

The correct statement in this regard is that God commanded the believers, teaching them how to kill the polytheists and strike them with the sword: to strike above their necks, hands and feet. His statement, above their necks, may mean the heads, or it may mean above the skin of the necks, in which case it means: on the necks. If this is possible, then the statement of those who say that it means: the necks is correct. If the matter is possible in what we have mentioned of interpretation, then we cannot direct it to some of its meanings and not others, except with an argument that must be accepted. And there is no argument that indicates its specificity, so it must be said: God commanded striking the heads, necks, hands and feet of the polytheists, the companions of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who witnessed Badr with him. As for his saying:
h
And strike off every fingertip of theirs
, its meaning is: O believers, strike off every limb and joint of your enemy’s hands and feet.
Al-Banan is the plural of Bananah, which are the tips of the fingers and toes.

i: This is what the poet said:
x: I wish I had cut off a fingertip and found him awake and alert in the house.
It means one banana. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: And strike off every fingertip of them, he said: every joint.

c: Ibn Wakiʿiq al-Ali narrated to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: And strike off every fingertip of them, he said: the joints. ... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: And strike off every fingertip of them, he said: every joint.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And strike off from them every fingertip
, he said: the extremities. And it is said: every joint.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And strike off from them every fingertip
, meaning by fingertip: the extremities.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And strike off from them every fingertip
, he said: the extremities.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And strike off from them every fingertip
, meaning: the extremities.

x: God Almighty means by His saying: That is because they, this action of striking these infidels above the necks and striking every fingertip of theirs, as a punishment for their dissent against God and His Messenger, and as a punishment for it. The meaning of his saying:
h
They opposed God and His Messenger
, is that they abandoned the command of God and His Messenger and disobeyed them, and obeyed the command of Satan. The meaning of his statement:
h
And whoever contradicts God and His Messenger

, and whoever disobeys the command of God and the command of His Messenger and abandons their obedience, then indeed, God is severe in penalty, is for him. And the severity of His punishment for him: in this world, He will bring upon him what he used to bring upon his enemies of punishments, and in the Hereafter, eternity in the fire of Hell. And the deletion of for him from the statement is because the statement indicates it.

God Almighty says: This is the punishment that I have hastened for you, O disbelievers who have caused trouble for God and His Messenger in this world, of being struck above your necks and every fingertip by the hands of My faithful friends, so taste it soon, and know that in the Hereafter and the Hereafter you will have the torment of the Fire. As for the opening of an in his saying:
h
And that for the disbelievers

, there are two aspects of parsing: One of them is: raising and the other is: lowering. As for the nominative, it means: That is it, so taste it, that is it, and for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire, with the intention of repeating that is it, as if it was said: That is the matter, and this. As for the accusative case: it has two aspects: One of them is: That is it, so taste it, and know, or: And be certain that it is for the disbelievers, so its accusative case is with the intention of an implied verb.
I saw your husband in the battlefield, carrying a sword and a spear.
Meaning: carrying a spear. The other: meaning: that, so taste it, and that the disbelievers will have the punishment of the Fire, then the ba was deleted, so it was placed in the accusative case.

God Almighty means: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, When you meet those who disbelieve in battle, advancing, meaning: advancing towards one another, and advancing means drawing near and coming close, then do not turn your backs to them, meaning: do not turn your backs to them and be defeated by them, but stand firm against them, for God is with you against them.

And whoever turns his back to them on that Day, meaning: And whoever among you turns his back to them, except turning aside for the sake of fighting, meaning: Except diverting himself to fight his enemy, seeking a vulnerable spot that he can hit so he can attack him, or withdrawing to a company, or: Except that he turns his back to them withdrawing to a company, meaning: Going to the area of the believers who will bring him back with them to fight them, and will return with him to them with them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ narrated, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Except for one who is evading battle or withdrawing to a group. He said: The one who is evading is the one who goes ahead of his companions to see an enemy surprise and capture it. He said: “And the one who is evading is the one who flees to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. And likewise the one who flees today to his leader and his companions.” Ad-Dahhak said: This is a warning from God to the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they should not flee. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were their group.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And whoever turns his back to them that day

, unless he turns aside for battle or withdraws to a company, as for turning aside, he says: unless he is diverting, meaning to return, or withdrawing to a company, he said: The one who withdraws, to the Imam and his soldiers if he attacks and he is unable to deal with them, and the people are not excused, even if they are many, for turning away from the Imam. Scholars differed regarding the ruling on the words of God Almighty:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day

, unless he turns aside for fighting or withdraws to a company, he has certainly drawn upon himself the wrath of God, and his refuge is Hell. Is it specific to the people of Badr, or does it apply to all believers?

x: Some people said: It is specifically for the people of Badr, because it was not for them to leave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his enemy and flee from him, but today there is no reason to flee.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah,
m: regarding the words of God Almighty:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, he said: That was the day of Badr, and they were not allowed to withdraw, and if anyone had withdrawn, he would not have withdrawn except to… Abu Musa said: He means: to the polytheists.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed,
m: the Almighty’s saying:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: If they had withdrawn, they would have withdrawn to the polytheists, and there were no Muslims on earth that day other than them.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Bishr ibn Mufaddal told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Saʿid, who said:
m: The following was revealed on the day of Badr:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna and Ali Ibn Muslim Al-Tusi told us
m: - Ibn Al-Muthanna said: Abd Al-Samad told me, and Ali said: Abd Al-Samad told us - he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Dawud, meaning Ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, he said: The day of Badr. Abu Musa said: I was told that in the book of Ghundar this hadith: On the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abu Sa’id.
b.via: Ibn Al-Muthanna and Ali Ibn Muslim Al-Tusi

c: Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Tusi told us, he said, Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, who said:
m: That was only on the day of Badr, when the Muslims had no group except the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. But after that, the Muslims were groups for one another.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah:
m: h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, he said: This was revealed about the people of Badr.

c: Yaqub told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said:
m: I wrote to Nafi’ asking him about his statement:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day

, was that day or later? He said: And he wrote to me: (That was only on the day of Badr). Surat al-Anfal 8:16 And whoever turns his back to them that Day, unless he turns aside to fight or withdraws to a company, has certainly drawn upon himself the wrath of God, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Zaid told us, on the authority of Sufban, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said:
m: The flight was only on the day of Badr, and they had no refuge to which they could turn. As for today, there is no flight.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And whoever turns his back to them that day

, he said: This was on the day of Badr specifically. Fleeing from battle is not one of the major sins. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, he said: This was specifically on the day of Badr. ... He said, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, on the authority of Habib bin Al-Shaheed, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, he said: It was revealed about the people of Badr.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, he said: That was the day of Badr.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Mubarak ibn Fadala, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, he said: That was on the day of Badr. As for today, if he withdraws to a group or a country, I think he said: There is nothing wrong with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said:
m: I wrote to Nafi’:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, he said: This is only on the day of Badr.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, who said, Yazid bin Abi Habib told me:
m: God made Hell obligatory for those who fled on the day of Badr. He said:
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day

, unless he turns aside for the sake of fighting or withdraws to a company, he has certainly drawn upon himself the wrath of God. Then when the day of Uhud came after that, He said: “It was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. But God has pardoned them.”
r
(Al Imran 3:155)
. Then came Hunayn, seven years after that, and He said: Then you turned back, fleeing. (al-Tawbah 9:25). Then after that, God will turn in mercy to whom He wills. (al-Tawbah 9:7).

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad:
m: That Umar, may God have mercy on him, was informed of the killing of Abu Ubayd, so he said: If only he would come to me! If I were one of the factions!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, who said, Qais bin Saad told me:
m: I asked Ata bin Abi Rabah about the statement of God, And whoever turns his back to them that Day, he said: This was abrogated by the verse in al-Anfal 8:“Now God has lightened your burden, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are among you a hundred, patient, they will overcome two hundred” (al-Anfal 8:66). He said: And it is not for a people to flee from two times their number. He said: That was abrogated except for this number.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, he said:
m: When Abu Ubayd was killed, the report came to Umar, and he said: O people, I am your group. ...Ibn al-Mubarak said, on the authority of Muammar, Sufyan al-Thawri, and Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: I am the group of every Muslim.

x: Others said: Rather, the ruling of this verse is general for everyone who turns his back on the enemy in defeat.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The greatest of the major sins is associating partners with God and fleeing from battle, because God Almighty says: “
h
And whoever turns his back to them that day
, unless he turns aside for the sake of fighting or withdraws to a company, he has certainly drawn upon himself the wrath of God, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.”

x: The most correct of the two interpretations of this verse, in my opinion, is the statement of the one who said: Its ruling is decisive, and that it was revealed about the people of Badr, and its ruling is established for all believers, and that God has forbidden the believers, when they meet the enemy, to turn their backs to them in defeat except to turn away for fighting, or to join a group of believers wherever they are in the land of Islam, and that whoever turns his back to them after the march to fight in defeat without intending one of the two characteristics that God has permitted turning away, has deserved God’s threat, unless He bestows His pardon upon him. We said that it is a decisive and not abrogated ruling because we have explained in more than one place in this book and others: that it is not permissible to rule that a ruling of a verse is abrogated, and it has a reason for not being abrogated, except with an argument that must be accepted, from a report that eliminates the excuse, or an argument of reason.

And there is no argument from these two meanings that indicates the abrogation of the ruling of the statement of God Almighty: And whoever turns his back to them that Day, unless he turns aside for the sake of fighting or withdraws to a company. As for his saying:
h
He has incurred the wrath of God

, he says: he has returned with the wrath of God. And his abode is Hell, he says: and his destination that he will go to in his return on the Day of Resurrection is Hell. And an evil destination, he says: and an evil place to which that destination will go.

God Almighty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger, who witnessed Badr with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and fought with him the enemies of his religion from the infidels of Quraysh 106:You did not kill the polytheists, O believers, but God killed them. And He, the Most High, attributed their killing to Himself, and denied it to the believers in Him who fought the polytheists, since He, the Most High, was the cause of their killing, and the believers’ fighting against them was due to His command. In that is the clearest evidence of the corruption of the deniers’ claim that God has a hand in the actions of His creation and they have attained it. Likewise, His saying to His Prophet, peace be upon him:
h
And you did not throw when you threw

, but God threw, so He attributed the throwing to the Prophet of God, then denied it from him, and informed about Himself that He was the thrower, since He, may His praise be glorified, was the one who conveyed what was thrown to those who threw it from the polytheists, and the one who caused the throwing to His Messenger.

It will be said to those who deny what we have mentioned: You know that God attributed the throwing of the polytheists by His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Himself, after describing His Prophet with it and attributing it to Himself. This is one action, the causation of which was from God and its direction, and the deletion and sending from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So why do you deny that the rest of the acquired actions of creation are like this: from God is creation and accomplishment through causation, and from creation is acquisition through powers? They will not say a statement about one of them without obligating the same about the other. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Umar told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And why did you not kill them?, regarding the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when this one said: I killed, and this one: I killed, “
h
and you did not throw when you threw
,” he said: to Muhammad when he threw stones at the infidels.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Surat al-Anfal 8:
m: 17 So you did not kill them, but it was God who killed them.
h
And you did not throw when you threw

, but it was God who threw, that He might test the believers with a good test. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. Qatada: And it was not you who threw when you threw, but God threw, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threw pebbles at them on the day of Badr.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Nothing of it fell except into a man’s eye.

c: Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad bin Abdul Warith told us, my father told us, Aban Al-Attar told us, Hisham bin Urwa told us:
m: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived at Badr, he said: ‘This is where they will fall!’ The polytheists found that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had preceded them to it and had descended upon him. When they came upon him, they claimed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said: ‘This is Quraysh who have come with their noise and pride, challenging You and denying Your Messenger. O God, I ask You for what You promised me!’ So when they came, he faced them and threw stones in their faces, and God Almighty defeated them.”

c: Ahmad bin Mansour told us, he said, Yaqoub bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Imran told us, he said, Musa bin Yaqoub bin Abdullah bin Zama’a told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Sulayman bin Abi Hathma, on the authority of Hakim bin Hizam, he said:
m: When the day of Badr came, we heard a sound falling from the sky like the sound of a pebble falling into a basin, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threw that shot and we were defeated.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais and Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi, they said:
m: “When the people drew near to one another, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a handful of dirt and threw it in the faces of the people, and said: ‘May your faces be disfigured!’ It entered their eyes, all of them, and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came forward, and God revealed: ‘
h
And you did not throw when you threw
, but it was God who threw,’ the verse, until: ‘Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.’”
b.via: Muhammad bin Qais and Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you did not throw when you threw

, the verse, he told us that on the day of Badr the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took three stones and threw them at the faces of the infidels, and they were defeated at the third stone.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: “When the two armies met on the day of Badr, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: Give me a pebble from the ground. So he gave him a pebble with dirt on it, and he threw it in the faces of the people. There was not a single polytheist who did not get some dirt in his eyes. Then the believers followed them, killing them and taking them captive. Then he mentioned the throw of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘You did not kill them, but God killed them. You did not throw when you threw, but God threw.’”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And you did not throw when you threw

, but it was God who threw, he said: “This was on the day of Badr. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took three pebbles and threw one pebble to the right flank of the people, one pebble to the left flank of the people, and one pebble in their midst, and he said: Disgrace the faces! And they fled.” So that is the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
And you did not throw when you threw
, but it was God who threw.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hand on the day of Badr and said: O Lord, if this group is destroyed, You will never be worshipped on earth again! Gabriel said to him: Take a handful of dirt! So he took a handful of dirt and threw it in their faces. There was not one of the polytheists who did not get dirt from that handful in his eyes, nostrils and mouth, so they turned and fled.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: God Almighty said
m: about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, throwing pebbles from his hand at the polytheists when he threw them:
h
And you did not throw when you threw
, but God threw, meaning: That was not your throw, were it not for what God put in it of your victory, and what He cast into the hearts of your enemy of it when God defeated them.

c: It was narrated from Al-Zuhri
m: that he said something that contradicts these sayings, which is: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri: And what did you throw when you threw? He said: “Abi bin Khalaf al-Jumahi came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a rotten bone, and he said: ‘Will God revive this, O Muhammad, when it has rotted away?’ And he was crumbling the bone, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God will revive it, then cause you to die, then cause you to enter the Fire!’ He said: So when the day of Uhud came, he said: ‘By God, I will kill Muhammad when I see him!’ That reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘Rather, I will kill him, God willing.’” As for his saying:
h
And that He may test the believers with a good test

, its meaning is: So that He may bestow upon the believers in God and His Messenger victory over their enemies, and give them what they have as booty, and write for them the rewards of their deeds and their struggle with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the good trial that God has afflicted upon these polytheists. By good trial he means the beautiful, good blessing, which is what was described and what is similar to it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And that He may test the believers with a good test from Him

, meaning: So that the believers may know of His blessings upon them, in their victory over their enemy despite their large numbers and their small numbers, so that they may know His right thereby, and so that they may thank Him for His blessings thereby. And His saying: Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, means: Indeed, God is All-Hearing, O believers, of the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his supplication to his Lord, and his asking Him to destroy the enemy and your enemy, and of your saying and the saying of all of His creation. He is All-Knowing, of all of that, including what is good for you and the good of His servants, and other things, encompassing it, so fear Him and obey His command and the command of His Messenger.

x: By His saying, That, He, the Most High, means this action, of killing the polytheists, and shooting them until they were defeated, and testing the believers with a good test by defeating them, and enabling them to kill them and take them captive, we did what we did, and that God weakens the plot of the disbelievers, meaning: And know that God, in addition to that, weakens the plot of the disbelievers, meaning: their treachery, until they are humiliated and submit to the truth, or they perish. In the opening of that there are aspects that are in His saying: That is it, so taste it, and indeed for the disbelievers (al-Anfal 8:14), and I have explained it there. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: weakened. The majority of the people of Medina and some of the Meccans and Basrans read it as muhan with emphasis, from wahant al-shay’ I weakened something, meaning I weakened it. The majority of the Kufians read it as muhan, from awhantuhu, ana muhanna, meaning: I weakened him.

The severity in this is more pleasing to me, because God Almighty used to nullify what the polytheists had concluded for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, contract after contract, and thing after thing. Even if the other aspect is correct.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: weakened.
The majority of the people of Medina and some of the Meccans and Basrans read it as muhan with emphasis, from wahant al-shay’ I weakened something, meaning I weakened it.
The majority of the Kufians read it as muhan, from awhantuhu, ana muhanna, meaning: I weakened him.

x: God Almighty says to the polytheists who fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Badr:
h
If you ask for victory

, victory has already come to you, meaning: If you ask God to rule over the most severe of the two parties to kinship ties, and the most unjust of the two groups, and you ask Him for victory over him, then God’s judgment has come to you, and His victory has made the oppressed victorious over the oppressor, and the truth victorious over the false. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
If you seek victory

, then victory has come to you. He said: If you seek justice, then justice has come to you. ... He said, Suwaid bin Amr Al-Kalbi told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah:
h
If you ask for victory
, then victory has come to you. He said: If you ask for justice, then justice has come to you.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you seek victory
, then victory has come to you, meaning the polytheists:
h
If you seek victory
, then help has come to you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Abdullah bin Kathir told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you seek victory
, he said: If you seek a final judgment. And he used to say: “
h
And if you desist
, it is better for you. But if you return, We will return,
h
and your company will not avail you at all
,” I said: For the polytheists? He said: We do not know anything other than that.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you ask for victory
, victory has already come to you, he said: The infidels of Quraysh said: Our Lord, decide between us and Muhammad and his companions! So victory was granted between them on the day of Badr.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri:
m: h
If you ask for victory

, then victory has come to you. He said: Abu Jahl asked for victory and said: O God - meaning Muhammad and himself - Which of us was more wicked to You, O God, and more severing of family ties, then destroy him today! God said:
h
If you ask for victory
, then victory has come to you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you ask for victory

, victory has already come to you, he said: Abu Jahl bin Hisham asked for victory and said: O God, which of us was the most wicked towards You and the most severed of family ties, then punish him today! meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and himself. God the Almighty said:
h
If you ask for victory
, victory has already come to you, so the two sons of Afra’: Awf and Muadh struck him, and Ibn Masoud finished him off.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said:
m: Abdullah bin Tha’laba bin Sa’eer Al-Adawi, an ally of Banu Zuhra, informed me: The one who sought victory that day was Abu Jahl, and that he said when the people met: Which of us will sever ties of kinship and bring us what we do not know, so that we may defeat him this morning! So that was his seeking victory, so God revealed concerning that:
h
If you seek victory
, victory has already come to you, the verse. Surat al-Anfal 8:19
h
If you ask for victory
, victory has already come to you. But if you desist, it is better for you. But if you return, We will return.
h
And your company will not avail you at all
, even if it is large.
h
And that God is with the believers

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you ask for victory
, victory has already come to you, the verse, he says: Badr was a fate and a lesson for those who take heed.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: When the polytheists came out to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca, they took hold of the curtains of the Kaaba and sought God’s help and said: O God, support the more powerful of the two armies, the more honorable of the two groups, and the better of the two tribes! Then God said:
h
If you ask for victory
, victory has already come to you, meaning: I have supported what you said, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj told us, he said,
m: I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, he heard al-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
If you seek victory
, victory has already come to you, until His statement,
h
And that God is with the believers

, that was when the polytheists went out to look at their caravan, and the people of the caravan, Abu Sufyan and his companions, sent to the polytheists in Mecca asking for their support, so Abu Jahl said: Whichever of us is best in your opinion, support him! And His statement,
h
If you seek victory
, means: seek support.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
If you ask for victory

, victory has already come to you, he said: If you ask for punishment, then they were punished on the day of Badr. He said: Their opening prayer was in Mecca, they said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment, (al-Anfal 8:32). He said: So the punishment came to them on the day of Badr.

c: And He informed us
m: about the day of UHud 11:“
h
And if you return
[to battle], We will return [to battle],
h
and your company will not avail you at all
, even if it were many. And indeed, God is with the believers.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah, he said:
m: Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: O God, support the more guided of the two groups, and the better of the two groups and the more excellent. So the following was revealed:
h
If you ask for victory

, victory has already come to you. ... He said, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri: That Abu Jahl was the one who asked for victory on the day of Badr and said: O God, whoever among us was the most wicked and severed his ties of kinship, then punish him today! So God revealed:
h
If you ask for victory

, victory has already come to you. ... He said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Tha’laba bin Su’air: Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: O God, He has severed our ties of kinship and brought us what we do not know, so defeat him this morning! That was an opening from him, so the verse was revealed:
h
If you ask for victory

, victory has already come to you, the verse. ... He said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Saad, on the authority of Salih bin Kaysan, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Tha’laba bin Su’air, who said: The one who sought victory on the day of Badr was Abu Jahl. He said: O God, He has severed our ties of kinship and brought us what we do not know, so destroy him this morning! So God revealed:
h
If you seek victory
, victory has already come to you.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Tha’labah ibn Su’ayr,
m: an ally of Banu Zuhrah, he said: When the people met and drew near to each other, Abu Jahl said: O God, we have severed our ties of kinship and brought to us what we do not know, so destroy it this morning! So he was the one who sought to open the door for himself. Ibn Ishaq said: So God said: If you seek to open the door, then victory has come to you, because of Abu Jahl’s saying: O God, we have severed our ties of kinship and brought to us what we do not know, so destroy it this morning! He said: The opening is fairness in supplication.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ma’shar told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ruman and others,
m: Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: O God, support the one which is more beloved to You of the two religions, our ancient religion or their new religion! So God revealed:
h
If you ask for victory
, victory has already come to you, until His saying:
h
And that God is with the believers
. As for his statement:
h
And if you desist
, it is better for you, he is saying:
h
And if you desist

, O people of Quraysh and the group of unbelievers, from disbelieving in God and His Messenger, and fighting His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him, it is better for you, in your worldly life and your afterlife.
h
And if you return
, We will return, he says:
h
And if you return
to fighting him and fighting him and fighting his believing followers, We will return, meaning: with something similar to the incident that befell you on the day of Badr. And His statement:
h
And your company will not avail you at all

, even if it were large, meaning: If you return, We will prepare to destroy you at the hands of My allies and defeat you, and your company will not avail you at My return to kill you at their hands and take you captive and defeat you,
h
and your company will not avail you at all

, even if it were large, meaning: their soldiers and their group of polytheists, just as they did not avail them at all on the day of Badr, despite their large number and the small number of believers,
h
and that God is with the believers

, meaning: And that God is with those of His servants who believe in Him against those of them who disbelieve in Him, He will grant them victory over them, or He will make them victorious as He made them victorious on the day of Badr over the polytheists. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if you desist
, it is better for you, he said: He is saying to the Quraysh 106:
h
And if you return
, We will return, for a similar incident that befell you on the day of Badr, “
h
And your company will not avail you at all

, even if it were many. And indeed, God is with the believers,” meaning: Even if your numbers are many in yourselves, it will not avail you at all. And indeed, I am with the believers, I will support them against those who oppose them. It has been said that the meaning of his saying:
h
And if you return
, We will return,
h
and if you return

to the opening, We will return to the opening of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This statement is meaningless, because God Almighty had guaranteed to His Prophet, peace be upon him, when He permitted him to fight his enemies, the manifestation of His religion and the elevation of His word, before Abu Jahl and his party sought victory. So there is no reason to say, while the matter is thus: If you desist from seeking victory, it is better for you; but if you return [to victory], We will return [to victory], because God had promised His Prophet, peace be upon him, victory by saying: “Permission to fight has been given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged. And indeed, God is competent to give them victory” (al-Hajj 22:39), whether the polytheists sought victory or not.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And if you return
, We will return, if you ask for the second opening, We will open for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
And your company will not avail you at all
, even if it were large, and indeed, God is with the believers, Muhammad and his companions. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
And that God is with the believers

. The opening of it is generally read by the people of Medina, meaning: And your group will not avail you at all, even if it is many, and God is with the believers. So he connected with that the place of even if it is many, as if he said: because of its great number, and because God is with the believers, and the place of that then would be accusative according to this statement. Some Arabists claimed that if it is opened, it is like: And God weakens the plot of the disbelievers, and And God is with the believers, in apposition of the latter to the first. The majority of the Kufians and Basrans read it as: And God, with a kasra on the alif, as a beginning, and they argued that it is in Abdullah’s reading: And God is with the believers.

x: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who broke in for the beginning, to complete the report before that about what is required by his saying:
h
And that God is with the believers

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And that God is with the believers.
The majority of the Kufians and Basrans read it as: And God, with a kasra on the alif, as a beginning, and they argued that it is in Abdullah’s reading: And God is with the believers.

Abu Jaafar said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who broke in for the beginning, to complete the report before that about what is required by his saying: And that God is with the believers.

x: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, Obey God and His Messenger, in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you, and do not turn away from him, meaning: do not turn away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disobeying his commands and prohibitions, while you hear, his commands and prohibitions to you, and you are believers in him, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: O you who have believed, obey God and His Messenger and do not turn away from him while you hear, meaning: Do not disobey his command while you hear his words and claim that you are from him.

x: God Almighty says to the believers in God and His Messenger from the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not be, O believers, in opposing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, like the polytheists who, when they hear the Book of God recited to them, say: (We have heard), with our ears, while they do not hear, meaning: They do not consider what they hear with their ears nor benefit from it, because they turn away from it and fail to absorb it in their hearts and ponder it. So God made them, since they did not benefit from the admonitions of the Qur'an, even though they heard them with their ears, in the position of those who did not hear them. God Almighty says to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not be like those polytheists who hear the sermons of the Book of God with their ears, and say: We have heard, while they are turning away from listening to them and learning from them, like those who do not hear them.
Ibn Ishaq used to say about this:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And do not be like those who said
, ‘We hear,’ while they do not hear, meaning: like the hypocrites who appear to obey him, but conceal their disobedience.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And they do not hear, he said: They are disobedient.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: What Ibn Ishaq said has a point, but his statement:
h
And do not be like those who said

, ‘We hear,’ while they do not hear, is in the context of stories about the polytheists, and is followed by the report about them with their condemnation, which is his statement: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason, so what is between them is more appropriate for it to be report about them than report about others.

God Almighty says: The worst of God’s creations that have crawled on the earth are those who listen to the truth so that they do not hear it, and learn from it and are admonished by it, and turn away from it if they speak it. They are those who do not understand God’s commands and prohibitions, and use their bodies for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God, he said: Live creatures means people.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: And they used to say: ((We are deaf and dumb regarding what Muhammad calls us to. We do not hear it from him, nor do we respond to him with belief!)) So they were all killed at Uhud, and they were the bearers of the banner.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The deaf and dumb who do not understand
, he said: those who do not follow the truth.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason, not deaf in this world nor dumb, but deafness of hearts, dumbness and blindness! And he recited: For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts which are within the breasts (al-Hajj 22:46). There is a difference of opinion about who this verse refers to.

x: Some of them said: He meant a group of polytheists.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
The deaf and dumb who do not understand

, a group of Banu Abd al-Dar who do not follow the truth. ... He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
The deaf and dumb who do not understand
, he said: They do not follow the truth. He said, Ibn Abbas said: They are a group of Banu Abd al-Dar.
