c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: It refers to the hypocrites.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason, meaning: the hypocrites whom I forbade you from being like, dumb to goodness, deaf to the truth, not using reason, not knowing what punishment and consequences will be upon them for that.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said what Ibn Abbas said: And that he meant by this verse the polytheists of Quraysh, because it is in the context of the report about them.
The people of interpretation differed about who this verse refers to, and about its meaning.

Some of them said: It refers to the polytheists. He said: Its meaning is that if God had granted them understanding of what He revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would not have believed in it, because God has decreed that they will not believe.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: His statement, “
h
And if God had known any good in them
, He would have made them hear.
h
And if He had made them hear
,” they would have said, Bring a Qur’an other than this,
r
(Yunus 10:15)
, and they would have said, Why did you not choose it? (al-A’raf 7:203), and if He had brought them a Qur’an other than it, they would have turned away while they were averse.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And if He had made them hear

, they would have turned away, averse, he said: If He had made them hear after He knew that there was no good in them, they would not have benefited from that, and they would have turned away, averse. He told me about it again and said: “If God knew any good in them, He would have made them hear. If He made them hear,” after He knew that there was no good in them, it would not have benefited them after He had realized that they would not benefit from it.

x: Others said: Rather, it refers to the hypocrites.
They said: Its meaning is what:

c: Ibn Hamid told us that Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And if God had known any good in them

, He would have made them hear, meaning He would have carried out what they said with their tongues, but their hearts contradicted that from them. And if they had gone out with you, they would have turned away, turning away. They would not have fulfilled for you anything for which they went out.

x: The more correct of the two opinions in interpreting this, in my opinion, is what Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said, because of the reason we mentioned before, and that this is not a characteristic of hypocrites.

The interpretation of the verse is: If God had known any good in these speakers, He would have made them hear the admonitions and lessons of the Qur’an, so that they would understand the arguments of God, the Almighty and Majestic, from it. But He knew that there was no good in them, and that they were among those destined for misery, so they would not believe. If He had made them understand that, so that they would know and understand, they would have turned away from God and His Messenger, turning away from believing in what God’s admonitions, lessons, and arguments had shown them to be true, opposing the truth after knowing it.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his statement:
h
When He calls you to that which gives you life
Some of them said: It means: Respond to God and the Messenger if he calls you to faith.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life
. He said: As for that which gives you life, it is Islam, I feel them after their death, after their disbelief.

x: Others said: For the truth.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding God’s statement:
h
When He gives you life
, he said: The truth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When He calls you to that which gives you life
, he said: The truth.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, he said, Anbasa told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life
, he said: to the truth.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: If he calls you to what is in the Qur’an.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life
, he said: It is this Qur’an, in it is life, trust, salvation, and protection in this world and the next.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: If he calls you to war and jihad against the enemy.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life
, meaning: to the war by which God has honored you after humiliation, strengthened you after weakness, and protected you from your enemy after they had subdued you.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: Its meaning is: Respond to God and the Messenger with obedience, if the Messenger calls you to what gives you life from the truth. That is because if that is its meaning, then it includes the command to respond to fighting the enemy and jihad, and to respond if he calls them to the rule of the Qur’an, and in responding to all of that is the life of the respondent. As for in this world, it is the continuation of the beautiful memory, and that is life for him in it. As for in the Hereafter, it is eternal life in Paradise and eternity therein. As for the statement of those who said: It means: Islam, this statement has no meaning. Because God described them as believers in His saying:
h
O you who have believed
h
respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life
. So there is no reason to say to the believer: Respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to Islam and faith.
And then, in what: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam al-Ajli narrated to us, saying:

c: Yazid ibn Zari’ narrated to us, saying: Ruh ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to my father while he was praying and called him: ‘O my father!’ My father turned to him and did not answer him. Then my father shortened the prayer, then turned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God!’ He said: ‘And upon you, what prevented you from answering me when I called you?’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, I was praying!’ He said: ‘Did you not find in what was revealed to me: “Respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life”?’ He said: ‘Yes, O Messenger of God! I will not do it again.’” Abu Kuraib narrated that Khalid bin Mukhallad narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-ʿAlaʿ, on the authority of his father, Surat al-Anfal 8:24
h
O you who have believed
h
respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life
h
And know that God comes between a man and his heart

and that to Him you will be gathered. on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by my father while he was standing praying, and he shouted at him but he did not answer him. Then he came and said: O my father, what prevented you from answering me when I called you? Didn’t God say: ‘
h
O you who have believed
h
respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life

’? My father said: No wonder, O Messenger of God, do not call me unless I answer, even if I am praying!” What is clear about the meaning of the verse are those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calls to what is in their life by their response to him from the truth after their conversion to Islam, because there is no doubt that Ubayy was a Muslim at the time when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him what we mentioned in these two reports.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And know that God comes between a man and his heart
, and that to Him you will be gathered.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: It stands between the disbeliever and faith, and between the believer and disbelief.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Aʿmash, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abdullah al-Razi, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr:
m: It comes between a person and his heart, he said: between the disbeliever believing, and the believer disbelieving.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, they said, Sufyan told us, and Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdullah Al-Razi, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: something similar.

c: Abu Zaydah Zakariya bin Abi Zaydah told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: the same.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: It comes between a person and his heart, he said: It comes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abdullah Al-Razi, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: It comes between a person and his heart, it comes between the disbeliever and faith and obedience to God. ... He said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It comes between a person and his heart, he said: It comes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubaid bin Sulayman and Abdul Aziz bin Abi Rawad told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He comes between a man and his heart
, he said: He comes between the disbeliever and his obedience, and between the believer and his disobedience.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim,
m: something similar. ... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: It stands between a person and disbelief, and between a disbeliever and belief.

c: Al-Hasan bin Hayya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Abd al-Aziz bin Abi Rawad told us, on the authority of al-Dahhak bin Muzahim:
m: It comes between a person and his heart, he said: It comes between the disbeliever and the obedience of God, and between the believer and the disobedience of God.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Ibn Abi Rawad told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: something similar. And it was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say:

c: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us:
m: I heard Al-Dahhak bin Muzayqam say: And he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I heard Abdul Aziz bin Abi Rawad narrating, on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, regarding his statement:
h
He comes between a man and his heart
, he said: He comes between the believer and his disobedience.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And know that God comes between a person and his heart, meaning: He comes between the believer and disbelief, and He comes between the disbeliever and faith.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And know that God comes between a man and his heart
, meaning: He comes between the disbeliever and his obedience, and He comes between the believer and his disobedience.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: It comes between a person and his heart, he said: It comes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Rawad, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
h
He comes between a person and his heart

, meaning: He comes between the disbeliever and his obedience, and between the believer and his disobedience. ... He said, Ishaq bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Yaqub al-Qummi, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr,
h
He comes between a person and his heart
, he comes between the believer and sins, and between the disbeliever and faith. ... He said, Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih:
h
He comes between a person and his heart
, he said: He comes between him and sins.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: It comes between a person and his mind, so he does not know what he is doing.
Who said that?

c: Ubayd God bin Muhammad Al-Faryabi told us, he said, Abdul Majeed told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He comes between a person and his heart
, he said: He comes between a person and his mind.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: It comes between a person and his heart, until it leaves him without reason.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He comes between a man and his heart
, he said: It is like his statement: (a state), until he left it and he does not understand.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Maqal bin Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
He comes between a person and his heart

. He said: If something comes between you and your heart, what do you do? ... He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: It comes between a person and his heart, he said: It comes between the heart of the unbeliever and doing good.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: It prevents a person from believing or disbelieving except with his permission.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And know that God comes between a person and his heart, he said:
h
He comes between a person and his heart
, so he cannot believe or disbelieve except with His permission.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that it is close to his heart, and nothing he reveals or keeps secret is hidden from him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It comes between a man and his heart
, he said: It is like his statement:
h
Nearer to him than his jugular vein
r

x: The most correct statement in my opinion is that it is said: This is report from God, the Almighty, that He has more control over the hearts of His servants than they do, and that He intervenes between them and them if He wills, so that no one with a heart is able to perceive anything of faith or disbelief, or to comprehend anything, or to understand, except with His permission and will. This is because the intervention between a thing and another thing is only a barrier between them, and if He, the Most High, intervenes between a servant and his heart in something, so that he does not perceive it or understand it, then the servant will not be able to perceive what God has prevented his heart from perceiving. If that is what it means, then it includes the statement of the one who said: He stands between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith, and the statement of the one who said: He stands between him and his mind, and the statement of the one who said: He stands between him and his heart so that he cannot believe or disbelieve except with His permission, because if God Almighty stands between a servant and his heart, the servant will not understand with his heart, which has been stood between it and that which prevented him from perceiving it, as I have explained.
However, it should be said: God, in His saying:
h
And know that God comes between a man and his heart

, is general in meaning, the report that He comes between the servant and his heart, and He did not specify one of the meanings that we mentioned over another, and the speech is open to all of these meanings, so the report is general until it specifies what must be accepted. As for His statement: And to Him you will be gathered, its meaning is: Know, O believers, also, along with the knowledge that God comes between a person and his heart: that God is the One who has power over your hearts, and He has more control over them than you do, to Him is your destination and your return on the Day of Resurrection, and He will give you the reward for your deeds, the good among you for his goodness, and the evildoer for his evil, so fear Him and be mindful of what He and His Messenger have commanded you and forbidden you to waste, and not to respond to His Messenger when he calls you to that which will give you life, for that will cause His wrath, and you will deserve His painful punishment when you are gathered to Him.
Surat al-Anfal 8:24
h
O you who have believed
h
respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life
h
And know that God comes between a man and his heart
and that to Him you will be gathered.

God Almighty says to those who believe in Him and His Messenger: (Fear God), O believers, a trial, meaning: a test from God that tests you, and a trial that He tests you, do not afflict, this trial that I warned you about, those who have wronged, and they are those who did what they had no right to do, either crimes that they committed, or sins between them and God that they committed. God Almighty warns them not to commit a sin for Him, or to commit a sin that would deserve punishment from Him. It was said: This verse was revealed about a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are the ones meant by it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim told us, al-Hasan ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
And fear a trial which will not strike only those who have wronged among you
, he said: It was revealed about Ali, Uthman, Talhah, and al-Zubayr, may God have mercy on them.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar:
m: h
And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively
, Qatada said: Az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: It was revealed, and we do not see any of us falling into it. Then he left us, in that it will strike us exclusively.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Zaid bin Auf Abu Rabia told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan: that Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam said:
m: This verse was revealed:
h
And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively

, and we do not think we are its people, and we are the ones meant by it. ... He said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Samit ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Sahban, who said: I heard al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam say: I read this verse for a long time, and I did not see that we were among its people, but we were the ones meant by it:
h
And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively
h
and know that God is severe in penalty

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively
, he said: This was revealed about the people of Badr specifically, and it struck them on the Day of the Camel, so they fought.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively
h
and know that God is severe in penalty
. He said: The people of the camel.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively

, he said: God commanded the believers not to allow evil to be practiced among them, lest God punish them all. ... He said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nahih, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively
, he said: It is also for you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And fear a trial which will not strike only those who have wronged among you
, he said: The trial means misguidance.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Al-Qasim, he said: Abdullah said:
m: There is not one of you who is not covered with a trial. God says: And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial (al-Anfal 8:28), so let him seek refuge in God from the misleading trials.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Al-Zubayr said:
m: He frightened us with it, meaning with his saying:
h
And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively
. The Arabs differed in their interpretation of this.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: And fear a trial that will not afflict those who do wrong. His saying: will not afflict is not an answer, but rather a prohibition after a command. If it were an answer, the letter nun would not have been included.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said that his statement, And fear a trial which will not strike those who do wrong, is a command to them and then a prohibition. And in it is a part of the recompense, even though it is a prohibition. He said: And similar to it is his statement, O ants, enter your dwellings lest Solomon crush you (al-Naml 27:18), a command to them and then a prohibition, and in the interpretation of the recompense. As if the meaning of the words to him was: Beware of a trial, if you do not beware of it, it will befall you. As for His statement:
h
And know that God is severe in penalty

, it is a warning from God and a threat to whoever falls into the trial that He warned him of by saying: And fear trial. He says: Know, O believers, that your Lord is severe in punishment for whoever is tempted by the injustice of his soul, and disobeys His command and sins thereby.

evidence.text: He said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Samit ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Sahban, who said: I heard al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam say: I read this verse for a long time, and I did not see that we were among its people, but we were the ones meant by it: And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively, and know that God is severe in penalty.

x: This is a reminder from God Almighty to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and advice. He says: Obey God and His Messenger, O believers, and respond to Him when He calls you to that which gives you life, and do not disobey His command even if He commands you to do that which is difficult and harsh for you, for God will make it easy for you by your obedience to Him, and will hasten for you from Him what you love, as He did with you when you believed in Him and followed Him while you were few, and the disbelievers would weaken you and tempt you away from your religion, and they would afflict you with harm in your souls and your honor, and you feared that they would kidnap you and kill you and destroy you all. So
h
He gave you shelter
, meaning: He made for you a refuge to which you could take refuge from them,
h
and supported you with His victory

, meaning: He strengthened you with His victory over them until you killed from them those whom you killed at Badr, and provided you with good things, meaning: And He fed you their spoils, lawful and good, that you might be grateful, meaning: so that you might be grateful for what He provided you with and bestowed upon you from that and other blessings of His with you.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the people who were meant by his saying: that people might snatch you away.
Some of them said: The infidels of Quraish.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land

, fearing that people would snatch you away, he said: He meant in Mecca, with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who followed him from Quraysh and their allies and clients before the migration.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Kalbi - or Qatada,
m: or both of them - And remember when you were few and oppressed, that it was revealed on the day of Badr, when they were afraid that people would snatch them away, so God sheltered them and supported them with His victory.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant other than Quraysh.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, my father told me, he said,
m: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say regarding the words of God Almighty: You fear that people will snatch you away, he said: Faris. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, Abdul Samad told me: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say, and he recited:
h
And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land
, fearing that people would snatch you away: and people at that time were the Persians and the Romans. ... He said, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land

, he said: This tribe of Arabs was the most humiliated of people, the most miserable in life, the hungriest in stomachs, the most naked in skin, and the most clearly astray, on the top of a rock, between the two lions, Persia and Rome. By God, there was nothing in their land at that time for which they could be envied. Whoever lived among them lived miserably, and whoever died among them was thrown into the Fire, they were eaten but did not eat. By God, we do not know of a tribe among the people of the earth at that time who were worse in status than them, until God brought Islam, and established you in the land through it, and expanded your provision through it, and made you kings over the necks of the people. So through Islam, God gave what you have seen, so thank God for His blessings, for your Lord is a benefactor who loves thanks, and the thankful will have more from God, the Blessed and Exalted.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: He meant the polytheists of Quraysh, because the Muslims did not fear for themselves before the migration from others, because they were the closest of the infidels to them, and the most severe on them at that time, despite their large number and the small number of Muslims. As for his saying:
h
He gave you shelter
, he means:
h
He gave you shelter
in Medina, and likewise his saying:
h
And supported you with His victory
, with the Ansar. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
He gave you shelter
, he said: to the Ansar in Medina,
h
and supported you with His victory
, and these are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He supported them with His victory on the day of Badr.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: So
h
He gave you shelter
h
and supported you with His victory
and provided you with good things, meaning Medina.

x: God Almighty says to the believers in God and His Messenger from the companions of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
O you who have believed

in God and His Messenger, Do not betray God. Their betrayal of God and His Messenger was by those of them who showed faith to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers outwardly and sincerely, while they concealed their disbelief and deceit for them inwardly, showing the polytheists their weaknesses and informing them of what was hidden from them of their report.
The interpreters differed about who this verse was revealed to, and the reason for it.
Some of them said: It was revealed about a hypocrite who wrote to Abu Sufyan, revealing to him the secret of the Muslims.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim bin Bishr Maruf narrated to us, saying: Shababah bin Suwar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad Al-Muharram narrated to us, saying:
m: I met Ata bin Abi Rabah, and he narrated to me, saying: Jabir bin Abdullah narrated to me: Abu Sufyan left Mecca, and Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Abu Sufyan is in such and such a place! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: Abu Sufyan is in such and such a place, so go out to him and keep it secret! He said: So a man from the hypocrites wrote to Abu Sufyan: (Muhammad wants you, so be on your guard)! So God Almighty revealed:
h
Do not betray God and the Messenger
or betray your trusts.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about Abu Lubaba, regarding what happened to him and the Banu Qurayzah. Mention those who said that. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Abu Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, regarding his statement:
h
Do not betray God and the Messenger

, nor betray your trusts, he said: It was revealed about Abu Lubabah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him, and he pointed to his throat: it is slaughtering. Al-Zuhri said: Abu Lubabah said: No, by God, I will not taste food or drink until I die or God accepts my repentance! So he remained for seven days without tasting food or drink until he fell unconscious, then God accepted his repentance. It was said to him: O Abu Lubabah, you have accepted your repentance! He said: By God, I will not absolve myself until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the one who absolves me.

So he came to him and absolved him with his hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: Part of my repentance is that I leave the home of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I give up my wealth! He said: A third is sufficient for you if you give it in charity.

c: Al-Muntha told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, he said:
m: I heard Abdullah bin Abi Qatada say:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not betray God and the Messenger
or betray your trusts while you know, was revealed about Abu Lubaba.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed regarding Uthman, may God have mercy on him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Yunus bin Al-Harith Al-Ta’ifi told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ubaid God bin Awn Al-Thaqafi told us, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah, he said:
m: This verse was revealed regarding the killing of Uthman, may God have mercy on him:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not betray God and the Messenger
, the verse.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is that God forbade the believers from Surat al-Anfal 8:27
h
O you who have believed
h
do not betray God and the Messenger

or betray your trusts while you know. betraying Him and His Messenger, and betraying His trust. It is possible that it was revealed about Abu Lubaba, and it is possible that it was revealed about someone else, and we do not have any information about which of them should be accepted as correct. The meaning and interpretation of the verse is what we have mentioned above. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not betray God and the Messenger
, he said: He forbade you from betraying God and the Messenger, as the hypocrites did.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Do not betray God and the Messenger

the verse, he said: They used to hear the hadith from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they would spread it until it reached the polytheists. They differed in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And you betray your trusts while you know

x: Some of them said:
h
Do not betray God and the Messenger
, for that would be a betrayal of your trusts and would destroy them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
do not betray God and the Messenger
or betray your trusts, for if they betray God and the Messenger, then they have betrayed their trusts.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
do not betray God and the Messenger

or betray your trusts while you know, meaning: Do not show God the truth that He is pleased with from you, then secretly contradict Him for something else, for that is the destruction of your trusts and a betrayal of yourselves.

x: According to this interpretation, his saying:
h
And betray your trusts
, is in the accusative case as a declension, as the poet said: Do not forbid a behavior and then do the same. Shame on you if you do it. It is narrated: (And the same will come).
Others said: Its meaning is:
h
Do not betray God and the Messenger
, and do not betray your trusts while you know.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not betray God and the Messenger
or betray your trusts, he says: Do not betray, meaning: do not diminish them.

x: According to this, the interpretation is:
h
Do not betray God and the Messenger
, and do not betray your trusts.
The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of trust, which God mentioned in His saying:
h
And betray your trusts
Some of them said: It is what is hidden from people’s eyes of God’s obligations.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And betray your trusts
, and trusts are the deeds that God has entrusted the servants with, meaning the obligatory duty. He says: Do not betray, meaning: do not diminish them.

c: Ali bin Dawud told us, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
, do not betray God, meaning: by abandoning His obligations, and the Messenger, meaning: by abandoning His Sunnah and committing disobedience to Him. He said: And he said another time:
h
Do not betray God and the Messenger
and do not betray your trusts, and trust means deeds, then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Al-Muthanna.

x: Others said: The meaning of trusts here is religion.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And betray your trusts

, your religion, while you know, he said: The hypocrites did that while they knew that they were disbelievers who outwardly showed faith. And he recited: And when they stand for prayer, they stand with laziness
r
(An-Nisa’: 142)
. He said: These are the hypocrites, God and His Messenger entrusted them with His religion, but they betrayed, and outwardly showed faith but concealed disbelief.

x: The interpretation of the statement is: O you who believe, do not diminish God’s rights over you from His obligations, nor His Messenger from the obligation to obey him, but obey them in what they command you and forbid you from, do not diminish them,
h
and betray your trusts

, and diminish your religions and the obligation of your actions and their necessity for you, while you know, that they are necessary for you, obligatory by the proofs that God has established for you.

God Almighty says to the believers: Know, O believers, that your wealth which God has given you, and your children which God has given you, are a test and a trial. He gave them to you to test you and try you, to see how you act in fulfilling God's right over you in them, and adhering to His commands and prohibitions in them, and that God has a great reward. He says: Know that God has goodness and a great reward for your obedience to Him in what He has commanded you and prohibited you in your wealth and children with which He has tested you in this world. Obey God in what He has charged you with in them, and you will attain a great reward in your afterlife.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Masoud,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Your wealth and your children are but a trial
, he said: There is not one of you who is not covered by a trial, so whoever among you seeks refuge, let him seek refuge with God from the misleading trials.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial
, he said, Trial means the test, their test. And he recited: And We test you with evil and with good as trial, and to Us you will be returned
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 35)

x: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, if you fear God by obeying Him and performing His obligations, avoiding His disobedience, and abandoning betraying Him and His Messenger and betraying your trusts,
h
He will make for you a criterion

, meaning: He will make for you a separation and distinction between your right and the falsehood of those of your polytheist enemies who seek to harm you, by giving you victory over them, and will remove from you your misdeeds, meaning: He will erase from you what has passed of your sins between you and Him, and will forgive you, meaning: He will cover them and conceal them from you, so He will not hold you accountable for them, and God is the possessor of great bounty, meaning: God who does that to you, has great bounty over you and over others of His creation by doing that and doing similar things. And his action is a reward from Him to His servant for his obedience to Him, because He is the One who guides His servant to the obedience that he has acquired, so that he deserves from his Lord the reward that He promised him for it.
The people of interpretation differed in the expression of the interpretation of His saying:
h
He will make for you a criterion
Some of them said: A way out.
Some of them said: Salvation.

Some of them said: A chapter. All of this is close in meaning, even if the expressions differ. I have explained the correctness of this previously, so there is no need to repeat it. It was mentioned that it means: the exit.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: If you fear God, He will grant you a criterion, he said: a way out. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: If you fear God, He will grant you a criterion, he said: A way out.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Furqana, with a chain of transmission.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Our two criters, he said: a way out in this world and the hereafter.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hani’ bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Furqan, he said: Furqan is the way out.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: A criterion, meaning: a way out.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Furqana, with a chain of transmission.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Raja’ al-Basri told us, he said, Zaydah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: Furqana, he said: a way out.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: I heard Ubayd say: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Furqana, as a way out.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Al-Furqan is the way out. It was mentioned that it means salvation.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: If you fear God, He will grant you a criterion, he said: Salvation.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah and Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He will make for you a criterion
, Ikrimah said: the way out, and Mujahid said: salvation.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
He will make for you a criterion

, he said: salvation. Surat al-Anfal 8:29 O you who have believed, if you fear God, He will grant you a criterion and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And God is the possessor of great bounty.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He will make for you a criterion
, meaning: He will make for you salvation.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
He will make for you a criterion

, meaning: salvation. Mention who said a chapter. ... O you who have believed, if you fear God, He will grant you a criterion. He said: A criterion that distinguishes in their hearts between truth and falsehood, so that they may know and be guided by that criterion.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: O you who have believed, if you fear God, He will grant you a criterion, meaning: a distinction between truth and falsehood, so that your truth may be revealed and the falsehood of those who oppose you may be hidden. In Arabic speech, al-Furqan is a noun derived from their saying: I differentiated between one thing and another, I differentiate between them, a difference and a difference.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reminding him of His blessings upon him: And remember, O Muhammad, when those who disbelieved among the polytheists of your people plotted against you to imprison you.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement, that they may establish you.
Some of them said: It means to tie you up.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you
, meaning: to tie you up. ... He said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: To make you firm, to bind you.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you
, the verse, to bind you tightly. And by that they meant the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca at that time.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Muqsim, they said:
m: Tie him up with the ties.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So that they may establish you, he said: Establishment means imprisonment and shackles.

x: Others said: Rather, it means imprisonment.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: I asked Ata’ about his statement: that they may imprison you. He said: They may imprison you, and Abdullah Ibn Kathir said it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: They said: (Prison him).

x: Others said: Rather, it means: to bewitch you.

Who said that? Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Basri, known as Al-Wasawsi, told me that Abdul Majeed bin Abi Rawad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, on the authority of Al-Muttalib bin Abi Wada’ah: “Abu Talib said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: What do your people follow? He said: They want to bewitch me, kill me, and expel me! He said: Who told you this? He said: My Lord! He said: Yes, your Lord is your Lord, so treat him well! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Should I treat him well? Rather, he treats me well! Then this verse was revealed: ‘
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you or kill you
or expel you’, the verse.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ata’ said: I heard Ubayd ibn Umair say: “When they plotted against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill him, or to imprison him, or to expel him, Abu Talib said to him: Do you know what they plotted against you? He said: So tell him. He said: Who told you? He said: My Lord! He said: Yes, your Lord is a good Lord, so treat him well! He said: Should I treat him well, or should he treat me well?” As if the meaning of the people’s plot against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was to prove him wrong, as: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi narrated, my father narrated, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Al-Kalbi narrated, on the authority of Zadin, the freed slave of Umm Hani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A group of Quraysh, from the nobles of each tribe, gathered to enter the House of Assembly, and Satan intercepted them in the form of a venerable old man. When they saw him, they said: Who are you? He said: An old man from Najd. I heard that you have gathered, so I wanted to bring you, and you will not be deprived of my advice and counsel. They said: Yes, enter! So he entered with them and said: Look at the matter of this man, by God, he is about to attack you in your affairs with his command. Then someone said: Lock him up in chains, then await the vicissitudes of fate for him, until he perishes as those poets who came before him perished, Zuhair and Al-Nabigha. He is only like one of them! He said: Then the enemy of God, the Najdi sheikh, cried out and said: By God, this is not an opinion for you! By God, his Lord will surely release him from his prison to his companions, and they will soon be able to seize him until they seize him from your hands and prevent him from you, for it is not safe for you that they will expel you from your country! They said: Then look for something other than this. He said: Then someone said: Then expel him from your midst and you will be relieved of him, for when he is released, what he has done and wherever he has fallen will not harm you, if his harm is absent from you and you are relieved, and his affair is with others. The Najdi sheikh said: By God, this is not an opinion for you. Have you not seen the sweetness of his speech, the fluency of his tongue, and the gripping of hearts when you hear his talk? By God, if you do that, then he reviews the Arabs, they will unite against you and come to you until he expels you from your country and kills your nobles! They said: By God, he is right! So look for an opinion other than this! Abu Jahl said: By God, I will advise you with an opinion that I do not think you have seen yet, I do not see anything else! They said: What is it? He said: We will take from each tribe a young, average, strong boy, then give each boy a sharp sword, then strike him with one blow, and when they kill him his blood will be distributed among all the tribes. I do not think that this tribe of Banu Ha'im will be able to fight all of Quraysh, for if they see that, they will accept reason, and we will be at ease and his harm will be cut off from us. The Najdi sheikh said: This, by God, is the opinion, the statement is what the young man said, I see no other! He said: So they dispersed on that and they were gathered for him. He said: So Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ordered him not to spend the night in the bed in which he had been spending that night. And God gave him permission at that time to go out, and after his arrival in Medina, He revealed to him Al-Anfal, reminding him of His blessings upon him and his affliction with Him: “
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you

to confine you or kill you or expel you. And they plotted, and God plotted. And God is the best of plotters.” And He revealed regarding their saying: Wait for him for a misfortune of time, until he perished as those poets before him perished. Or do they say, He is a poet; we are waiting for him to be struck by a misfortune of time? (al-Tur 52:30). That day was called the Day of the Crowd because of the opinion they had agreed upon.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Muqsim,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you
, they said: They consulted with each other about him one night while they were in Mecca.

x: Some of them said: When morning comes, bind him tightly.
Some of them said: Rather, kill him.
Some of them said: Rather, take him out. So when morning came, they saw Ali, may Surat al-Anfal 8:30
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you or kill you
or expel you. And they planned, and God planned. And God is the best of planners. God have mercy on him, and God repelled their plot.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr went out to the cave, he ordered Ali bin Abi Talib to sleep in his bed. The polytheists spent the night guarding him, and when they saw him sleeping, they thought he was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they left him. When morning came, they rushed to him, thinking he was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and suddenly they saw Ali. They said: Where is your companion? He said: I do not know! He said: So they rode on difficult and easy horses in search of him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Uthman Al-Jazari told me:
m: that Muqsim, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words:
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you
, he said: The Quraysh consulted one night in Mecca, and some of them said: When morning comes, then imprison him with chains, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Some of them said: Rather, kill him.

Some of them said: Rather, take him out. So God informed His Prophet of that, so Ali, may God have mercy on him, spent the night in the bed of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until he reached the cave, and the polytheists spent the night guarding Ali, thinking that he was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So when morning came, they rushed to him, and when they saw Ali, may God have mercy on him, God repelled their plot, so they said: Where is your companion? He said: I do not know! They followed his tracks, and when they reached the mountain and passed by the cave, they saw a spider's web over its entrance. They said: If he had entered here, he would not have woven a web over its entrance! So he stayed in it for three days.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you

to confine you or kill you or expel you - and they planned, and God planned. And God is the best of planners.” He said: The elders of Quraysh gathered to consult about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the Ansar had converted to Islam. They feared that his status would rise if he found a refuge to which he could flee. Then Satan came in the form of a man from Najd and entered the House of Assembly with them. When they denied him, they said: Who are you? By God, not all of our people have been informed of our gathering here! He said: I am a man from Najd, I listen to your talk and advise you! They felt shy, so they left him.

x: Some of them said: Take Muhammad when he lies down on his bed and put him in a house where we can await the vicissitudes of fate - and vicissitudes means death, and deaths means time - Satan said: What a bad thing you have said! You put him in a house, then his companions come and bring him out, and there will be fighting between you! They said: The old man has spoken the truth! He said: Expel him from your village! Iblis said: What a bad thing you have said! You expel him from your village, and he has corrupted your fools, then he comes to another village and corrupts their fools, so he brings horses and men! They said: The old man has spoken the truth! Abu Jahl - who was the first of them to obey Iblis - said: Rather, we will go to every clan of Quraysh, and bring out a man from them, and give them weapons, so they will attack Muhammad all together and strike him with one blow, and the sons of Abdul Muttalib will not be able to kill Quraysh, so they will have nothing but blood money!

Iblis said: He has spoken the truth, and this young man is the best of you in opinion! So they stood up and did that. And God informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he slept on the bed, and they put spies over him. When it was part of the night, he and Abu Bakr went to the cave, and Ali bin Abi Talib slept on the bed, and that is when God says: To confine you or kill you or expel you, and confinement means confinement and bondage, and it is His saying: And they almost forced you from the land to expel you from it, but then they would not remain behind you except a little (al-Isra’ 17:76), meaning: to destroy them. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, Umar met him and said to him: What did the people do? He saw that they had been destroyed when the Prophet left their midst, and this is what was done with the nations, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Delay the fighting.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: To imprison you or kill you, he said: The infidels of Quraysh wanted that for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he left Mecca.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hani’ bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar, except that he said: They did that to Muhammad.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you or kill you
, the verse, he is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they plotted against him while he was in Mecca.

c: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you
to the end of the verse, he said: “They gathered and consulted about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: Kill this man.

x: Some of them said: No man will kill him except that he will be killed by him! They said: Take him and imprison him, and put iron on him. They said: Let his family not leave you alone! They said: Take him out. They said: Then he will seduce the people against you. He said: And Satan was with them in the form of a man from Najd, and their opinion was that when he came to circumambulate the House and touch it, they would gather around him and cover him up and kill him, because his family would not know who killed him, so they would be satisfied with the blood money, so we would kill him and rest and cover him up! So when he came to circumambulate the House, they gathered around him and covered him up, so Abu Bakr came and was told that, so he came but did not find a way in. When he did not find a way in, he said:
“Do you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God,’ and he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord?”

He said: Then God relieved him of it. When night fell, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said, Who are your companions? He said, So-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so. He said, “No, we know them better than you, O Muhammad. They are the night watchmen!” He said: And those people were taken from their beds while they were asleep, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought to them. One of them was brought to Gabriel, who applied kohl to his eyes, then he let him go. He said, What is his appearance, O Gabriel? He said, I have taken care of him, O Prophet of God! Then another was brought, and he tapped his head with a stick, then he let him go. He said, What is his appearance, O Gabriel? He said, I have taken care of him, O Prophet of God! Then another was brought, and he tapped his knee. He said, What is his appearance, O Gabriel? He said, I have taken care of him!

Then another was brought, and he gave him a sip. He said, What is his appearance, O Gabriel? He said, I have taken care of him, O Prophet of God! The fifth was brought, and when he came home in the morning, he passed by an arrow, and a sharp pointer caught on his cloak, and it twisted and cut off the black part of his leg. As for the one whose eyes were blackened, he became blind. As for the one who was given a sip, he became sick with his stomach. As for the one whose head was pierced, a hole - a hole is a great sore - took hold of his head. As for the one whose knee was stabbed, he became crippled. This is what God said:
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you or kill you
or expel you - and they plotted, and God plotted - and God is the best of plotters.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: his saying:
h
And they plot
, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters, meaning: So I plotted against them with My mighty plot, until I saved you from them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when those who disbelieved plotted against you
, he said: This is Meccan. Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: This is Meccan.

x: The interpretation of the statement then is: And remember, O Muhammad, My favor with you, by My plotting against those of the polytheists of your people who tried to plot against you, by keeping you, killing you, or expelling you from your homeland, until I rescued you from them and destroyed them. So carry out My command in warring against those of the polytheists who fought you, and turn away from responding to what I sent you with of the upright religion, and do not be terrified by their great number, for your Lord is the best of plotters against those who disbelieve in Him, worship other than Him, and disobey His commands and prohibitions. We have explained the meaning of deceit previously, so there is no need to repeat it here.

God Almighty says: And when the clear verses of God’s Book are recited to those who disbelieve, for those whose breasts God has opened to understand it, they say, out of ignorance and stubbornness towards the truth, and they know that they are lying in what they say, If we willed, we could say the like of this, which is recited to us, This is nothing but legends of the ancients, meaning: that they say: This Qur’an that is recited to them is nothing but legends of the ancients. And (myths) is the plural of (lines), which is the plural of the plural, because the singular of (lines) is (line), then (line) is pluralized as (lines) and (lines), then (lines) is pluralized as (myths) and (myths). Some Arabs used to say: One of the words myths is myth. The polytheists meant by their statement, This is nothing but legends of the ancients, that this Qur’an that you recite to us, O Muhammad, is nothing but what the ancients wrote and transcribed of the report of the nations!
It is as if they added to it that it was taken from the children of Adam, and that God did not direct it to him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: His statement, “
h
And when Our verses are recited to them

, they say, ‘We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this,’” he said: Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith used to go on a trade trip to Persia, and he would pass by the worshippers while they were reading the Gospel, bowing, and prostrating. So he came to Mecca and found Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, having received revelation while he was bowing and prostrating. So Al-Nadr said, “We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this!”, to the one who had heard from the worshippers. So the statement, “
h
And when Our verses are recited to them

, they say, ‘We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this,’” was revealed. He said: So our Lord related what they had said in Mecca, and related what they had said when they said, O God, if this is the truth from You, the verse.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Alqamah, the brother of Banu Abd al-Dar, used to go to al-Hirah and listen to the rhyming prose of its people and their speech. When he arrived in Mecca, he heard the speech of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an, and he said: “We have heard it, if we wished, we could say the same. This is nothing but legends of the ancients,” meaning the rhyming prose of the people of al-Hirah.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: “On the day of Badr, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed with patience: ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt, Tuʿaymah ibn ʿAdi, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Al-Miqdad had taken al-Nadr prisoner, and when he ordered him to be killed, al-Miqdad said: O Messenger of God, my prisoner! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He used to say what he said about the Book of God! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to be killed. Al-Miqdad said: My prisoner! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, enrich al-Miqdad from Your bounty! Al-Miqdad said: This is what I intended! And this verse was revealed about him: ‘
h
And when Our verses are recited to them
’, the verse.”

“Yaqoub told me, Hisham told us, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed three men from the Quraysh on the day of Badr, with patience: Al-Mut’am bin Adi, Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt. He said: When he ordered the killing of Al-Nadr, Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad said: My prisoner, O Messenger of God! He said: He used to say about the Book of God and about His Messenger what he used to say! He said: He said that two or three times, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, enrich Al-Miqdad from Your bounty! And Al-Miqdad had taken Al-Nadr prisoner.”

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: God Almighty says: And when the clear verses of God’s Book are recited to those who disbelieve, for those whose breasts God has opened to understand it, they say, out of ignorance and stubbornness towards the truth, and they know that they are lying in what they say, If we willed, we could say the like of this, which is recited to us, This is nothing but legends of the ancients, meaning: that they say: This Qur’an that is recited to them is nothing but legends of the ancients.

x: God Almighty says: And remember, O Muhammad, also what happened to the one who said: O God,
h
if this is the truth from You

, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment, when You plotted against them and brought them a painful punishment, and that punishment was killing them with the sword on the day of Badr. This verse was also mentioned to have been revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when they said
, ‘O God,
h
if this is the truth from You
, then rain down upon us stones from the sky,’ he said: It was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If this is the truth from you
, he said: the statement of Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, or: Ibn Al-Harith bin Kalda.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: O God,
h
if this is the truth from You

, the words of Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith bin Alqamah bin Kalda, from Banu Abd Al-Dar. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
If this is the truth from You
, he said: He is Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith ibn Kaldah.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Talha ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Ata’
m: who said: A man from Banu Abd al-Dar called al-Nadr ibn Kalda said: O God,
h
if this is the truth from You
, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. So God said: And they said, ‘Our Lord, hasten for us our portion before the Day of Reckoning.’
r

, and He said: And indeed, you have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time. (al-An’am 6:94), and He said: A questioner asked about a punishment to befall the disbelievers. (al-Ma’arij 70:1-2) Ata’ said: About a dozen verses from the Book of God were revealed about it.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: He said - meaning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith - : O God, if what Muhammad says is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment! God said: A questioner asked about a punishment to come to pass (al-Ma’arij 70:1).

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If this is the truth from You
, the verse, he said: A questioner asked about a punishment to befall the disbelievers (al-Ma’arij 70:1-2).

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And when they said
, ‘O God,
h
if this is the truth from You
’ the verse, he said: That was said by the foolishness and ignorance of this nation, so God returned with His return and mercy to the foolishness and ignorance of this nation.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Then he mentioned the surprise of the Quraysh and their afflictions upon themselves, when they said: O God,
h
if this is the truth from You

, meaning: what Muhammad brought, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, as You rained them down upon the people of Lot, or bring us a painful punishment, meaning: some of what You punished the nations before us with. The Arab scholars differed on the reason for the inclusion of he in the speech.

x: Some of the Basrans said: The truth is in the accusative case because he - and God knows best - is an extra particle in the sentence that is a connection of emphasis, like the extra particle what - and it is only added to every verb that cannot do without a predicate, and he is not an adjective, like this, because if you had said: I saw this is him, it would not have been a sentence. And this is not the implicit particle, like His statement: But they were the wrongdoers (al-Zukhruf 43:76) and You will find it with God, better and greater in reward (al-Muzzammil 73:20). Because you say: ((I found him and me)), then (he) is an adjective. It may also be in this meaning other than an adjective, but it is redundant, as it was in the first. And it may in all of this run the course of a noun, raising what comes after it, if what comes after it is apparent or implied in the language of Banu Tamim.
They say in His statement:
h
If this is the truth from you

, “But they were the wrongdoers” (al-Zukhruf 43:76), and You will find it with God, better and greater in reward (al-Muzzammil 73:20), just as you say: (Their fathers were the wrongdoers), they made this implied like (he) and (they) and (you) redundant in this place, and they did not make the places of the adjective, because it is a separation by which he wanted to clarify that what comes after it is not an adjective for what came before it, and he did not need this in the place where it does not have a predicate.

Some of the Kufians used to say: “He huwa which is a pillar in speech is not used except for a correct meaning. He said: It is as if he said: “Zayd is standing,” and you said: Rather, Amr is the one standing. So huwa is for the known noun, and alif lam is for the known verb, and alif lam which is a connection in speech, is contrary to the meaning of huwa, because its entry and exit are the same in speech. huwa is not like that. As for what is used as a connection in speech, it is an emphasis similar to their saying: I found him himself, you say that, and it is not a description of like the elegant and the wise.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: And God would not punish them while you are among them, meaning: while you are residing among them. He said: This was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was residing in Mecca. He said: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out from among them and asked forgiveness for those Muslims who were there. Then, after he went out to him, when those Muslims asked forgiveness for them, it was revealed: And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. He said: Then those remaining Muslims went out from among them and punished the disbelievers.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibn Abza, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca, and God revealed to him: And God would not punish them while you are among them. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Medina, and God revealed: And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness.

x: He said: So those remaining Muslims who remained there were seeking forgiveness - meaning in Mecca - and when they left, God revealed to him:
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them
while they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque, and they were not its guardians? He said: So God gave him permission to conquer Mecca, and this is the punishment that He promised them.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, meaning: those Muslims who were in it,
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them
, meaning Mecca, and among them were the infidels.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding the statement of God: And God would not punish them, meaning the people of Mecca, and God would not punish them, and among them are the believers who seek forgiveness, and He forgives those Muslims among them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq bin Ismail Al-Razi and Abu Dawud Al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Ibn Abzi:
m: h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, he said: The remainder of the Muslims who remained among them. So when they left, he said:
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them
? ... He said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, he said: The people of Mecca. ...And my father told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, he said: The believers from the people of Mecca,
h
And why should God not punish them
while they prevent people from the Sacred Mosque, he said: The polytheists from the people of Mecca. ... He said, Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, he said: The believers seek forgiveness among themselves.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, meaning: Those who believed with you seek forgiveness in Mecca, until He expelled you and those who believed with you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: He did not punish a village until the Prophet and those who believed with him left it, and he joined him where he was commanded,
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
