, meaning the believers. Then he returned to the polytheists and said:
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, he said: He means the people of Mecca.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And God would not punish these polytheists of Quraysh in Mecca while you were among them, O Muhammad, until He brought you out from among them, And God would not punish them, and these polytheists say: (O Lord, Your forgiveness!), and similar meanings of seeking forgiveness by words. They said: And His statement:
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them
, in the Hereafter.

Who said that? Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ramadi narrated that Abu Hudhayfah narrated that Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Abu Zamil on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The polytheists used to circumambulate the House saying: ‘Here I am, here I am, you have no partner. ’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say: ‘Yes, yes! ’ They would say: ‘Except for a partner who is yours, you own him and what he owns. ’ They would say: ‘Your forgiveness, your forgiveness! ’ So God revealed: ‘
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them

, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness. ’” Ibn Abbas said: There were two things of security among them: the Prophet of God and seeking forgiveness. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, left, and seeking forgiveness remained. ‘
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them
while they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque, while they are not its guardians?
Its guardians are only the righteous. ’ He said: This is the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: And that is the punishment of this world.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ruman and Muhammad bin Qais, they said:
m: The Quraysh said to one another: Muhammad, may God honor him, is from among us: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us the verse. When evening came, they regretted what they had said, and they said: Your forgiveness, O God! So God revealed:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
until His saying:
h
They do not know
b.via: Yazid bin Ruman and Muhammad bin Qais

c: Ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: They used to say - meaning the polytheists -: By God, God will not punish us while we seek forgiveness, nor will He punish a nation while its Prophet is with it until He expels him from it! This was from what they said, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among them. So God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioning to him their ignorance, their deception, and their opening up to themselves, when they said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, just as You rained them down on the people of Lot. And He said, when He criticized their evil deeds:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness, meaning: because of their saying: (Indeed, we seek forgiveness while Muhammad is among us),
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them

, even if you are among them, and even if they seek forgiveness as they say, and they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque, meaning: whoever believes in God and worships Him, meaning: you and those who follow you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Al-Sabah Al-Bazzar told us...
m: he said, Abu Burdah told us, on the authority of Abu Musa, who said: There were two security matters before, his statement:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them

, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness, he said: As for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he has passed away, and as for seeking forgiveness, it will continue among you until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Yunus bin Abi Ishaq told us, on the authority of Amer Abi Al-Khattab Al-Thawri, he said:
m: I heard Abu Al-Ala’ say: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had two trusts, one of which was lost and the other remained:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, the verse.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them

, O Muhammad. And God would not punish the polytheists while they seek forgiveness, meaning: if they sought forgiveness. They said: And they were not seeking forgiveness, so God, the Most High, said since they were not seeking forgiveness:
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them
while they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque?
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness. He said: The people were not seeking forgiveness, and if they had sought forgiveness they would not have been punished.

x: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: They are two guarantees that God sent down: As for one of them, he has passed away, the Prophet of God. As for the other, God has kept him among you as a mercy, seeking forgiveness and repentance.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: God said to His Messenger:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them

, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness. He said: I would not punish them while they seek forgiveness, and if they had sought forgiveness and confessed their sins, they would have been believers. How could I not punish them while they do not seek forgiveness?
h
And why should God not punish them
while they prevent people from Muhammad and from the Sacred Mosque?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness, he said, he says: If they had sought forgiveness, I would not have punished them.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: And God would not punish them while they were Muslims. They said: And their repentance in this place was their Islam.
Who said that?

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Abdul Malik bin Al-Sabah told us, Imran bin Hudayr told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them

, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness, he said: They asked for punishment, so he said: He would not punish them while you are among them, and He would not punish them while they enter Islam.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: And you are among them, he said: among them, and his statement: And they seek forgiveness, he said: they submit.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, among them, And God would not punish them while they seek Surat al-Anfal 8:34
h
And why should God not punish them

while they prevent [people] from Al-Masjid Al-Haram, while they were not its guardians? Its guardians are none but the righteous, but most of them do not know. forgiveness, he said: while they submit,
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them
while they avert, Quraysh, from the Sacred Mosque.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, he said: among them,
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, he said: their entry into Islam.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Among them are those who have previously been granted entry into Islam by God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, meaning: God, the Exalted, would not punish a people while their prophets were among them until He brought them out. Then he said:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, meaning: And among them were those who had previously entered into faith from God, which is seeking forgiveness. Then he said:
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them
, so He punished them with the sword on the day of Badr.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: God would not punish them while they were praying.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, meaning: they pray, meaning by this the people of Mecca.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, he said, Hussain Al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness, he said: They pray.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Faraj
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say regarding His statement:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, meaning the people of Mecca. He said: I would not punish you while Muhammad is among you. Then he said:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, meaning: they believe and pray.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, he said: while they are praying.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And God would not punish the polytheists while they seek forgiveness. They said: Then this was abrogated by His statement:
h
And why should God not punish them while they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said:
m: He said in al-Anfal 8:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness, so the verse that follows it abrogated it:
h
And why should God not punish them
? until His saying: So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve, so they were fought in Mecca, and hunger and siege afflicted them there.

x: The most correct of these sayings in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: Its interpretation is:
h
And God would not punish them while you are among them
, O Muhammad, residing among them, until He expels you from among them, because I will not destroy a town while its prophet is in it,
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness

, for their sins and disbelief, but they do not seek forgiveness for that, rather they persist in it, so they deserve punishment, just as it is said: (I would not do good to you while you wrong me), meaning: I will not do good to you, if you wrong me, and if you wronged me I would not do good to you, but I do good to you because you do not wrong me. And likewise, then it was said:
h
And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them

while they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque, meaning: What is their business, and what prevents them from God punishing them while they do not seek forgiveness from God for their disbelief and believe in Him, while they prevent the believers in God and His Messenger from the Sacred Mosque?

We said: This statement is the most correct statement in this regard, because the people - I mean the polytheists of Mecca - had hastened the punishment, and said: O God, if what Muhammad brought is the truth, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. So God said to His Prophet: “I would not punish them while you are among them, and I would not punish them if they sought forgiveness. How could I not punish them after You have been expelled from them, and they prevent people from the Sacred Mosque?” So God, the Most High, informed him that the punishment they had hastened would befall them and would befall them, and He informed them of the moment when it would befall them, and that would be after He had expelled them from among them. There is no reason to threaten them with punishment in the Hereafter, while they were hastening it in this immediate matter, and there is no doubt that they will be punished in the Hereafter.
Rather, God’s hastening of it for them on the Day of Badr is clear evidence that what we have said is true. Likewise, there is no basis for the statement of those who attributed his statement:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness

, to the fact that it refers to the believers, and it is in the context of reporting about them and about what God will do to them. There is no evidence that the reporting about them has been completed, and therefore it is a metaphor for them, and that there is no disagreement among its people about its interpretation. Likewise, there is no basis for the statement of those who said: This was abrogated by His statement:
h
And why should God not punish them while they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque
, the verse, because His statement, may He be glorified and exalted:
h
And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness
, is a report, and it is not permissible for a report to contain abrogation.
Rather, abrogation is for a command or a prohibition. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the inclusion of an in his saying:
h
And why should God not punish them

? Some Basra grammarians said: It is redundant here, and it was used as la was used, which is redundant. It was mentioned in poetry: If Ghatafan had not committed any sins against me, their nobles would have blamed Amr. Some Arabists have denied this statement and said: An was only used for a correct meaning, because the meaning of and what is wrong with them is what prevents them from being punished. He said: An was used for this meaning, and it was excluded by la to show that it means denial, because prevention is denial. He said: And la in the verse is correct in meaning, because if denial is imposed on it, it becomes report. He said: “Don’t you see that you said: ‘Zaid is not standing’, for you have made standing obligatory?”
He said: And likewise la in this verse.”
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
And they were not his allies
His allies are only the righteous, but most of them do not know.”

God Almighty says: And what is the matter with these polytheists that God should not punish them while they prevent people from the Sacred Mosque, and they are not the allies of God? His allies means: God’s allies are only the righteous, meaning: those who fear God by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience, but most of them do not know, meaning: but most of the polytheists do not know that the righteous are the allies of God, rather they think that they are the allies of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they were not his allies
. His allies are only the righteous,” they are the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: His allies are none but the righteous, whoever they may be, and wherever they may be.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And they were not his allies

. His allies are only the righteous,” those who respect his sanctity and establish prayer near him, meaning: you - meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - and those who believe in you, but most of them do not know.

x: God Almighty says: And what is the matter with these polytheists that God should not punish them, while they prevent those who pray to God in it and worship Him from the Sacred Mosque, and they are not God’s guardians, but rather His guardians are those who prevent them from the Sacred Mosque, and they do not pray in the Sacred Mosque, And their prayer at the House, meaning the Ancient House of God, was nothing but whistling, which is whistling. It is said: (Maka yamku makwan wa makaan) and it has been said that (al-maku) is for a man to gather his hands, then put them in his mouth, then scream.

(Maka ast al-dabbah mukaan), if it blows with wind. It is said: (It does not yamku except with its ast uncovered), and for this reason al-ist is called (al-makwa), it was named thus, and from that is the saying of Antarah: And the wife of a prostitute left a braid, and she was bitten by its prey, like the cheek of a wise man. And Al-Tarmeh said: He leaned towards the first with a sharp stab, the sides of which were covered with ashes.

Meaning: vote. As for tasdiya, it is clapping. It is said: sada yasdi tasadayyan, clap, and safah, all meaning the same thing. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Musa bin Qais, on the authority of Hajar bin Anbas:
m: Except for whistling and clapping. He said: Whistling means whistling, and clap means clapping.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands
. “Whistling” means whistling, and clap of hands means clapping of hands.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands
, meaning: the prayer of the polytheists at the House was whistling, meaning whistling, and clapping, meaning clapping of hands.

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said, Fadil told us, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands
, he said: clapping and whistling.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Qura bin Khalid, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: Al-Maka’ means clapping, and Al-Tasdiyya means whistling. He said: Ibn Umar tilted his cheek to one side.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Qurra bin Khalid, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. He said: Whistling and clapping are whistling and clapping.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said,
m: I heard Muhammad bin Al-Hussein narrating, on the authority of Qura bin Khalid, on the authority of Atiya Al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Omar, he said: Al-Maka’ means whistling, and Al-Tasdiya means clapping.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Amir told us, he said, Qura told us, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands
, he said: Whistling is whistling, and clapping is clapping of hands. Qura said: Atiyah narrated to us what Ibn Umar did, so he whistled, tilted his cheek, and clapped his hands.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Bakr ibn Mudar told me, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Rabiʿah, he said:
m: I heard Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf say regarding the statement of God:
h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands
, Bakr said: So Jaʿfar brought his hands together for me, then blew into them whistling, as Abu Salamah had told him.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The ‘mukka’ is the whistle, and ‘tasdiya’ is the clapping. ... He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Salamah bin Sabur told us, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Omar: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping, he said: whistling and clapping. ... He said, Abu Ahmad told us, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Omar, the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Habawayh Abu Yazid told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The Quraysh used to circumambulate the House naked, whistling and clapping, so God revealed: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants?” (al-A’raf 7:32), so they were commanded to wear clothes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed, he said:
m: The Quraysh used to oppose the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the circumambulation, mocking him, whistling and clapping, so this verse was revealed:
h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Except for whistling, he said: They would blow into their hands, and tasdiya means clapping.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Except for whistling and clapping. He said: Whistling is putting their fingers in their mouths, and clap is clapping, they mix that up with the prayer of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: except that he did not say: his prayer.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Muka means putting their fingers in their mouths, and tasdiya means clapping. He said: A group of Banu Abd al-Dar used to mix all of these things with the blessings of Muhammad.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Talha bin Amr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands, he said: from between the fingers. Ahmad said: A letter fell on me, and I do not think it was anything but throwing, blowing and whistling from them, and Saeed bin Jubair showed me where they were whistling from the direction of Abu Qubays. Narrated to us, Al-Muthanna said, narrated to us, Ishaq bin Sulayman said, narrated to us, Talhah bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement:
h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands

, he said: The whistling means they would interlock their fingers and whistle with them, and that is the whistling. He said: And Saeed bin Jubair showed me the place where they used to whistle towards Abu Qubays.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Harb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman,
m: regarding his statement: whistling and clapping, he said: whistling is blowing - and he pointed with his hand before his mouth - and clapping is clapping.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: Al-Maka’ means whistling, and Al-Tasdiyya means clapping.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands
, he said: We were told that (whistling) was clapping of hands, and (clapping) was shouting with which they opposed the Qur’an.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Bell whistling and clapping. He said: Bell whistling is whistling, and clap clapping is clapping.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. And whistling is the whistling, like a white bird called maka that is found in the land of the Hijaz, and claps is clapping.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands

, he said: Whistling is a whistle that the people of the Age of Ignorance used to make loud noises. He said: And he also said regarding whistling: whistling in their hands and playing. It has been said about (tasddiyyah): It is (turning away from the Sacred House of God), and this is a baseless statement, because (tasddiyyah) is a noun derived from the saying: (I turned away, turning away). As for (sad), it is not said from it: (saddayt), rather it is said from it: (sadddat), and if you stress the dal from it to mean repeating the action, it is said: (sadddat tasidaydan). Unless the one who said this statement attributed (tasddiyyah) to it being from (sadddat), then one of its dals was changed to a ya, as it is said: (tazanayt) from (dhannat), and as the rajaz poet said: The falcon is killed if the falcon breaks Surat al-Anfal 8:35 And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and hand-clapping.
h
So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve
. Meaning: The falcon is biting, so one of its two letters, the letter Dhad was changed to a Ya, and this is a direction to which it is directed.

x: Mention of those who said what we mentioned in the interpretation of al-Tasdiyya.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told me, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Talha bin Amr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands
, turning them away from the Sacred House of God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Sulayman told us, he said, Talha bin Amr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And a siddiyah. He said: The siddiyah means the people prevented them from entering the Sacred House.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: And turning away, he said: turning away from the path of God, and turning them away from prayer and from the religion of God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands

, he said: Their prayer that they claim will ward off evil from them was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands, and that is what God does not like nor love, nor is it what He has made obligatory upon them, nor what He has commanded them to do. As for His statement: Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve, it means the punishment that He promised them with the sword on the day of Badr. He says to the polytheists who said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky verse, when He brought them the punishment they had hastened, Taste, meaning eat, and it is not a taste with the mouth, but rather a taste with the senses and the presence of the taste of His pain in the hearts. He says to them: So taste the punishment for what you used to deny that God will punish you with it for your denial of the Oneness of your Lord and the message of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve
, meaning: what God inflicted upon them on the day of Badr of killing.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve
, he said: These are the people of Badr, the day God punished them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve
, meaning the people of Badr. God punished them on the day of Badr by killing and taking them captive.

evidence.text: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Qurra bin Khalid, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His Messenger spend their wealth, giving it to their peers among the polytheists so that they may gain strength by it to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him, to turn the believers in God and His Messenger away from believing in God and His Messenger. So they will spend their wealth on that, and then their spending will be a regret for them. He says: It will become a cause of remorse for them, because their wealth will be lost, and they will not attain what they hoped for and coveted of extinguishing the light of God and raising the word of disbelief over the word of God, because God is the One who raises His word and makes the word of disbelief the lowest. Then the believers will overcome them, and God will gather those who disbelieved in Him and His Messenger to Hell, and they will be tormented therein.

So great is the regret and remorse therein for those of them who live and those who perish! As for the living, their wealth is spent in vain, without attaining any benefit, and they will return defeated, subdued, deprived, and robbed. As for the deceased, he was killed, robbed, and hastened to the fire of God to abide therein forever. We seek refuge in God from His wrath. The one who took charge of the expenses mentioned by God in this verse, among other things, was Abu Sufyan.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth and the verse, And those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell, he said: It was revealed about Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. On the day of Uhud, he hired two thousand Abyssinians from Banu Kinanah, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought with them. They are the ones about whom Kaʿb ibn Malik says: And we came to a wave of the sea in the midst of which were Abyssinians, some of them bareheaded and some masked. Three thousand, and we are three hundred, if they are more, then four Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Ya’qub al-Qummi, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Ibn Abza: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God, he said: It was revealed about Abu Sufyan: He hired two thousand men on the day of Uhud to fight with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in addition to those Arabs who sought help. ...He said, my father told us, on the authority of Khattab ibn Uthman al-Asfari, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Utaybah: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God. He said: It was revealed about Abu Sufyan. He spent on the polytheists on the day of Uhud forty ounces of gold, and an ounce at that time was forty-two mithqals.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God, the verse, when Abu Sufyan brought the caravan to Mecca, he stirred up the people and called them to fight, until the Prophet of God invaded the following year. And Badr was in Ramadan, on Friday morning, the seventeenth of Ramadan. And Uhud was in Shawwal, on Saturday, the eleventh of it, in the fourth year.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: God said about what the polytheists, including Abu Sufyan, were hiring men to fight Muhammad with: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they will spend it; then it will be a cause of regret for them, meaning remorse and woe on the Day of Resurrection, then they will be overcome.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: They spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God, the verse until His statement: Those are the losers, he said: Regarding Abu Sufyan’s spending on the infidels on the day of Uhud.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubayd God ibn Shihab al-Zuhri told us,
m: and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, and al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, and other scholars of ours told us, all of them narrated some hadith about the Day of Uhud. All their talk came together in what I have mentioned of the talk about the Day of Uhud. They said, or what was said by them: When some of the infidels of Quraysh from the companions of the well were killed on the day of Badr, and they returned to Mecca, and Abu Sufyan returned with his camel, Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Sufyan ibn Umayyah walked with men from Quraysh whose fathers, sons, and brothers had been killed at Badr. They spoke to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those of Quraysh who had business with that caravan, and said: O people of Quraysh, Muhammad has left you and killed your best, so help us with this money to fight him, so that we may take revenge on him for those of us who were killed! So they did. He said: It was about them, as mentioned by Ibn Abbas, that God revealed: Indeed, those who disbelieved spend their wealth until His saying:
h
And those who disbelieved will be gathered to Hell
b.via: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubayd God ibn Shihab al-Zuhri

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God, until His saying: will be gathered together, meaning the group who went to Abu Sufyan, and to whoever had wealth from Quraysh in that trade, and they asked them to strengthen them to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they did.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Saeed bin Abi Ayoub told me, on the authority of Ata bin Dinar,
m: regarding the statement of God: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth, the verse, it was revealed about Abu Sufyan bin Harb.

x: Some of them said: He meant the polytheists of Badr.
Mention of who said that:

c: Al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj told us, he said,
m: I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, he heard al-Dahhak say about His statement, Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God the verse, he said: They are the people of Badr.

x: “In my opinion, what is correct to say about this is what we have said, which is to say: God informed us about those who disbelieved in Him from the polytheists of Quraysh, that they spend their wealth to hinder people from the path of God. He did not tell us which of those He meant, but rather He made the statement “those who disbelieved” general. It is possible that He meant those who spent their wealth to fight the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions at Uhud, and it is possible that He meant those among them who spent that at Badr, and it is possible that He meant both groups. Since that is the case, then the correct thing to say about it is general, just as His praise made general those among Quraysh who disbelieved.”

The Almighty says: God will gather those who disbelieved in their Lord and spent their wealth to hinder people from the path of God, to Hell, to separate between them - they are the people of wickedness, as He said and called them the wicked, and between the believers in God and His Messenger, they are the good ones, as He called them, the Most High. So He, the Most High, distinguished between them by settling the people of faith in Him and His Messenger in His Gardens, and sending the people of disbelief into His Fire. God And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So that God may distinguish the wicked from the good
, so He distinguished the people of happiness from the people of misery.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: Then he mentioned the polytheists and what will be done to them on the Day of Resurrection, and he said:
h
So that God may distinguish the wicked from the good

, meaning: He will distinguish the believer from the disbeliever, and He will place some of the wicked upon others. And what He, the Most High, means by His saying: And He will put some of the wicked upon others, is that He will put some of the disbelievers on top of others, and will pile them all up, meaning that He will gather some of them together until they become numerous, as He, the Most High, said in describing the clouds: Then He will bring them together, then He will make them into a heap (al-Nur 24:43), meaning: a dense gathering, and as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
He will pile it all up
, he said: He will gather it all together, one on top of the other. And his saying:
h
He will put him in Hell
, meaning: He will put all the wicked people in Hell. So he made the report about them singular in order to make his saying:
h
So that God may distinguish the wicked

, singular. Then he said: Those are the losers, so he made it plural, and did not say: That is the loser, so he returned it to the beginning of the report. By those he means those who disbelieved, and its interpretation is: Those who spend their wealth to turn people away from the path of God are the losers. By his saying: the losers he means those whose deal was fruitful and whose trade was a loss. This is because they bought with their wealth the punishment of God in the Hereafter, and they hastened to spend it in what they spent in fighting the Prophet of God and the believers in him, disgrace and humiliation.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who disbelieve, from the polytheists of your people, if they desist, from what they are persisting in of their disbelief in God and His Messenger, and their fighting you and fighting the believers, and return to faith, God will forgive them for what has passed of their sins before their faith and their return to obeying God and His Messenger through their faith and repentance. And if they return, He says: And if these polytheists return to fighting you after the battle that You brought upon them on the Day of Badr, then My way has passed with the first of them at Badr, and with others of the past generations, when they transgressed and denied My messengers and did not accept their advice, of bringing down immediate punishment upon them. So if they return to fighting and waging war against you, then bring down upon these people what You brought down upon them.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: The precedent of the ancients has passed, in the Quraysh on the day of Badr, and other nations before that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The way of the ancients has passed, he said: in Quraysh and other nations before that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said
m: regarding His statement: Say to those who disbelieve, if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them, but if they return to fighting, “then the precedent of the former peoples has already passed,” meaning: whoever among them was killed on the day of Badr.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And if they return, to fighting you, then the precedent of the former peoples has passed, of the people of Badr.

x: God Almighty says to those who believe in Him and His Messenger: “And if these people prepare to fight you, you have seen My way with those of them who fought you on the Day of Badr, and I will return with the same with those of them who fought you, so fight them until there is no more polytheism, and no one is worshipped except God alone, with no partner for Him, and the affliction is lifted from the servants of God on earth - which is (the trial) - and “the religion will be entirely for God,” meaning: until all obedience and worship will be purely for God and no one else. God And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, meaning: until there is no more polytheism.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, he said: Persecution means polytheism.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And fight them until there is no more persecution

, meaning: Fight them until there is no more polytheism, and religion is all for God, until it is said: There is no god but God, for which the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought, and to which he called.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, he said: until there is no more polytheism.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, he said: until there is no more calamity.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
and religion is all for God, meaning: no believer is tempted away from his religion, and monotheism is purely for God, with no partner in it, and he rejects all rivals to Him.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, he said: until there is no more disbelief, and the religion is all for God, there is no more disbelief with your religion.

c: Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, Aban Al-Attar told us, he said, Hisham bin Urwa told us, on the authority of his father:
m: That Abdul Malik bin Marwan wrote to him asking him about some things, so Urwa wrote to him: ((Peace be upon you, for I praise God, there is no god but Him. As for what follows, you wrote to me asking me about the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca, and I will inform you about it, and there is no power or strength except with God. The reason for the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca was that God gave him prophethood, what an excellent prophet! What an excellent master! What an excellent clan! May God reward him with good, and may we know his face in Paradise, and may He make us live upon his religion and cause us to die upon it. And when he called his people to what God had sent him of guidance and light which He had sent down upon him, they did not turn away from him at the beginning of what he called them to, and they almost listened to him, until he mentioned their tyrants. Then some people from Taif from Quraysh came, and they had wealth, and some people denied that and were harsh with him, and they hated what he said, and they tempted those who obeyed them with it, The common people turned away from him and abandoned him, except for those whom God preserved from among them, and they were few. He remained like that for as long as God had willed, then their leaders conspired to tempt those who followed him from the religion of God, from their sons, brothers and tribes. It was a severe tribulation. Those who were tempted were tempted, and God protected whomever He wished from among them. When he had done that to the Muslims, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to go to the land of Abyssinia. In Abyssinia there was a righteous king called the Negus, who did not wrong anyone in his land. He was also praised for his righteousness. Abyssinia was a market place for the Quraysh, where they traded and where their merchants lived, finding comfort, security and good trade. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to go there, and most of them went there when they were defeated in Makkah, and he feared for them the tribulations. He himself stayed and did not leave. This continued for years, oppressing those among them who had converted to Islam. Then Islam spread there, and some of their noblest and most powerful men entered it. When they saw that, they relaxed regarding the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and his companions. The first trial was when those companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) left before Abyssinia, fearing it and fleeing from the trials and earthquakes they were experiencing. When they relaxed, and those who entered Islam entered, they talked about their relaxation. This reached those companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) who were in Abyssinia, that those of them who were in Mecca had relaxed, and that they would not be tempted. So they returned to Mecca, and they were almost safe there, and they began to increase in number and multiply. Many of the Ansar in Medina converted to Islam, and Islam spread in Medina, and the people of Medina began to visit the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in Mecca. When the Quraysh saw that, they conspired to tempt them and be harsh with them. They seized them and were keen to tempt them, so they suffered great hardship. And that was the last trial. There were two tribulations: a tribulation that drove those who had gone to Abyssinia, when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to do so and gave them permission to go there; and a tribulation when they returned and saw those from Medina who were coming to them. Then seventy leaders came from Medina, the leaders of those who had converted to Islam, and they met him for the Hajj. They pledged allegiance to him at Al-Aqabah and gave him their pledge that we are from you and you are from us, and that whoever of your companions comes or you come to us, we will protect you as we protect ourselves. The Quraysh became violent towards them at that time. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered his companions to go out to Medina. This was the last tribulation in which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent out his companions, and he himself went out. It was the one about which God revealed:
h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
and religion is all for God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr:
m: That he wrote to al-Walid: ((As for what follows, you wrote to me asking me about the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca, and I have, praise be to God, knowledge of everything that you wrote asking me about, and I will inform you, God willing, and there is no power or strength except with God)), then he mentioned something similar.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Qais told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, he said: (Yasaf) and (Na’ila), two idols that were worshipped. As for his statement:
h
If they desist
, its meaning is:
h
If they desist

from temptation, which is associating partners with God, and turn to the true religion with you, then indeed, God is Seeing of what they do, meaning: God is not hidden from what they do of abandoning disbelief and entering the religion of Islam, because He sees them and sees your deeds, and all things are manifest to Him, nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing is hidden from Him, not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller or greater than that, except that it is in a clear book.

x: Some of them said: The meaning of this is that if they stop fighting.
What we said about this is more correct, because even if the polytheists stopped fighting, it was obligatory for the believers to fight them until they submitted.

God Almighty says: And if these polytheists turn away from what you have called them to, O believers, of believing in God and His Messenger, and abandoning fighting you because of their disbelief, and they refuse except to persist in disbelief and fighting you, then fight them, and be certain that God is your helper and supporter against them. What an excellent protector, He is for you, meaning: What an excellent supporter for you and His friends, and what an excellent helper, and He is the supporter.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And if they turn away, from your command to what they are upon of their disbelief, then God is your Master who honored you and gave you victory over them on the day of Badr, despite their great number and your small number. What an excellent Master and what an excellent Helper! Part 9 of Volume 6 is done. Followed by, God willing, the tenth part of the sixth volume. The first: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And know that whatever you obtain of anything (al-Anfal 8:41)

x: This is a teaching from God Almighty to the believers regarding the division of their spoils if they acquire them. God Almighty says: And know, O believers, that whatever you acquire as spoils. Scholars differed about the meaning of booty and spoils of war.
Some of them said: There are two meanings in them, each one of them is different from the other.
Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ narrated that Hameed bin Abdul Rahman narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saleh that he said: I asked Ata’ Al-Sa’ib about this verse:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of spoils

- indeed, God has a fifth of it, and this verse: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger (al-Hashr 59:7). I said: What is the spoils of war and what is the spoils of war? He said: The Muslims gained victory over the polytheists and over their land and took them by force, so whatever money they took over which they gained victory was the spoils of war, but as for the land, it is the spoils of war in our black land.
Others said: Spoils are what is taken by force, and booty is what is obtained through a peace treaty.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, he said:
m: Ghanima is what the Muslims took by force through fighting, in which one-fifth is due, and four-fifths of it is for those who witnessed it. Fay is what they agreed upon without fighting, in which there is no one-fifth, it is for those whom God has named.”

x: Others said: Ghanima and Fay’ have the same meaning. They said: This verse in Al-Anfal abrogates His statement:
h
Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God and to the Messenger (al-Hashr 59
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns is for God and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the
orphans and the needy and the traveler (al-Hashr 59:7), he said: The spoils of war were for these people, then Surat al-Anfal was abrogated in that regard, and He said:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of anything

- a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the traveler (al-Hashr 59:7). So this abrogated what was before it in Surat al-Anfal. And He made the fifth for whoever had the spoils of war in Surat al-Hashr, and the rest of that for whoever fought for it. We have previously explained spoils of war and that it is money that is delivered to him from the money of the one whose money God has given to the people of his religion, by overpowering him and subduing him through fighting. As for al-Fay’, it is what God bestowed upon the Muslims from the wealth of the polytheists, which is what He returned to them through a peace treaty without sending horses or camels. It may be permissible to call what He returned to them from it, their swords, spears, and other weapons, al-Fay’, because al-Fay’ is a verbal noun derived from the saying: The thing returned, and God returned it. However, what God has rejected regarding the spoils of war by His ruling in Surat al-Hashr is only what was described as spoils of war, not what was driven upon by horses and riders, for reasons I have explained in the book: A Delicate Book of Sayings on the Rulings of the Laws of Religion, and we will also explain it in the interpretation of Surat al-Hashr, if we reach it, God willing. As for the statement of those who said: The verse in Surat Al-Anfal abrogates the verse in Surat Al-Hashr, this is meaningless, since there is no meaning in one of the two verses that negates the ruling of the other. We have explained the meaning of abrogation, which is the negation of a ruling that has been established by a ruling that contradicts it, in more than one place, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. Surat al-Anfal 8:41 And know that whatever you gain of anything, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger
h
and for the near of kin
and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer,
h
if you have believed in God and in what We revealed to Our Servant on the Day of Criterion

, the day the two armies met. And God is over all things competent. As for his saying: Of anything, what is meant by it is: everything that the name thing applies to, from what God has granted to the believers of the wealth of those polytheists whose wealth they have overcome, from what the division has applied to, even the thread and needle, such as:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of anything
, he said: The sewn part of thing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim Al-Fadl told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
Then a fifth of it is for God
, and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives, and the orphans, and the needy, and the wayfarer.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said that his saying:
h
Then a fifth of it belongs to God is the key to the statement
, and to God belongs the world and the hereafter and what is in them, but the meaning of the statement is: The Messenger has a fifth of it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim, he said:
m: I asked al-Hasan about the statement of God:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of anything
- a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger, he said: This is the key to the statement, to God belongs this world and the hereafter.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, he said:
m: I asked Al-Hasan bin Muhammad about his statement:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of anything

, a fifth of it belongs to God, he said: This is the key to the statement, to God belongs this world and the hereafter. Abu Kuraib narrated, Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated, Abu Shihab narrated, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Nahshal, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out an expedition and they captured spoils, he would give one-fifth of the spoils, and he would multiply that fifth by five. Then he recited:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of spoils
h
then a fifth of it is for God
and for the Messenger. He said: His statement:
h
then a fifth of it is for God
, is a key to the statement. To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, so God made the share of God and the share of the Messenger one.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheera, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: Then a fifth of it belongs to God, he said: Everything belongs to God.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of anything
, a fifth of it is for God, he said: Everything is for God, and a fifth is for God and His Messenger, and everything else is divided into four shares.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: The spoils of war were divided into five fifths, four fifths for those who fought over them, and the remaining fifth was divided into five fifths, one fifth for God and the Messenger.

c: Imran bin Musa told us, he said, Abdul Warith told us, he said, Aban told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, recommended a fifth of his money, and he said: Should I not be satisfied with my money with what God is satisfied with for Himself?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’:
m: And know that whatever you gain of anything, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger. He said: The fifth of God and the fifth of His Messenger are one. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would carry some of it and put in it whatever he wanted.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of his companions, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And know that whatever you gain, a fifth of it belongs to God, he said: Everything belongs to God, the fifth is for the Messenger, the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: A fifth of it is for the House of God and for the Messenger.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakiʿ ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah al-Riyahi, who said:
m: The spoils of war would be brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would divide them into five parts, four-fifths of which would go to those who witnessed them. Then he would take one-fifth and strike it with his hand, and take from it what he had grasped and give it to the Kaʿbah, and it was the share of God. Then he would divide what remained into five parts, one part for the Messenger, one part for the near of kin, one part for the orphans, one part for the poor, and one part for the wayfarer. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated that Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi narrated on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of spoils

, a fifth of it belongs to God, to the end of the verse. He said: The spoils would be brought and placed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would divide them into five shares, giving four to the people and taking one share. Then he would strike with his hand all of that share, and whatever he took of it he would give to the Kaʿbah, and it is that which was named for God. Do not assign a share to God, for God belongs this world and the Hereafter. Then he would divide the rest into five shares: a share for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a share for the near of kin, a share for the orphans, a share for the needy, and a share for the wayfarer.

x: Others said: What was named for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is only meant as his kinship, and neither God nor His Messenger have anything to do with it.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The spoils of war were divided into five fifths, four of which were for those who fought over it, and one fifth was divided into four: a quarter for God, the Messenger, and the near of kin - meaning the relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - so whatever was for God and the Messenger was for the relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not take anything from the fifth. The second quarter was for the orphans, the third quarter was for the poor, and the fourth quarter was for the wayfarer.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: His saying:
h
Then a fifth of it belongs to God opening of a discussion

, and that is due to the consensus of the proof that the fifth cannot be divided into six shares. If God had a share in it, as Abu al-ʿAliyah said, then a fifth of the spoils would have to be divided into six shares.

The scholars differed only on dividing it into five or less, but as for more than that, we do not know of anyone who said it other than the one we mentioned from the report on Abu al-ʿAliyah. And in the consensus of those I mentioned, there is clear evidence of the correctness of what we have chosen. As for the one who said: The Messenger’s share is for the relatives, he has made a share obligatory for the Messenger, even though he, may God bless him and grant him peace, spent it on his relatives, so it did not come out of the division being five shares, and: Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of spoils

, a fifth of it is for God, the verse, he said: When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gained spoils, he would divide them into fifths. One fifth was for God and His Messenger, and the Muslims would divide what remained.

The one fifth that was assigned to God and His Messenger was for His Messenger, relatives, orphans, the needy, and wayfarers. So this one fifth was five fifths: one fifth for God and His Messenger, one fifth for relatives, one fifth for orphans, one fifth for the needy, and one fifth for wayfarers.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha, he said:
m: I asked Yahya ibn al-Jazzar about the share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: It is one-fifth of one-fifth.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah and Jarir told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha, on the authority of Yahya ibn al-Jazzar,
m: the same.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Then a fifth of it belongs to God, he said: Four fifths are for those who are present at the battle, and the remaining fifth is for God and the Messenger, a fifth of it is placed where he sees fit, a fifth of it is for relatives, a fifth of it is for orphans, a fifth of it is for the poor, and a fifth is for the wayfarer. As for his saying:
h
And for the near of kin
, the people of interpretation differed about them.

x: Some of them said: They are relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Banu Hashim.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were not permitted to take charity, so he made one-fifth of the fifth for them.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his family did not eat charity, so he made one-fifth of the fifth for them.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Abd al-Salam told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: God knew that there were poor people among the Banu Hashim, so He made the fifth for them in place of the charity.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said, Ismail bin Abaan told us, he said, Al-Sabah bin Yahya Al-Muzni told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Al-Daylam, he said,
m: Ali bin Al-Hussein, may God have mercy on him, said to a man from the people of Ash-Sham: Haven’t you read in (Al-Anfal):
h
And know that whatever you obtain of anything
- a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger the verse? He said: Yes! He said: Then you are them? He said: Yes!

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said,
m: Surat al-Anfal 8:41 And know that whatever you gain of anything, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger
h
and for the near of kin
and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer,
h
if you have believed in God and in what We revealed to Our Servant on the Day of Criterion
, the day the two armies met. And God is over all things competent.

c: Israel told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: These are the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for whom charity is not permissible.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Najdah wrote to him asking him about his relatives, so he wrote him a letter: We claim that we are them, but our people refused that to us. ... He said: Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
h
Then a fifth of it is for God

, he said: Four fifths are for those who are present at the battle, and the remaining fifth is for God and the Messenger, a fifth of it is placed where he sees fit, a fifth for relatives, a fifth for orphans, a fifth for the poor, and a fifth for the wayfarer.

x: Others said: Rather, they are all Quraysh.
Who said that?

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Abdullah bin Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, he said:
m: Najdah wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about the relatives. He said: So Ibn Abbas wrote to him: ((We used to say: We are them, but our people refused that to us, and they said: All of Quraysh are relatives.))

x: Others said: The share of the people of the villages was for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then it became for the ruler after him.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He was asked about the share of the relatives. He said: It was food for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was alive. Then, when he died, it was given to the ruler after him.

x: Others said: Rather, the share of the relatives was for Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib in particular.

Among those who said this was Al-Shafi’i, and his reason for that was: Abu Kuraib narrated, Yunus bin Bakir narrated, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated, Az-Zuhri narrated, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Jubayr bin Al-Mut'im, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the share of the relatives from Khaybar among Banu Hashim and Banu Al-Muttalib, I walked with Uthman bin Affan, may God have mercy on him, and we said: O Messenger of God, these are your brothers, Banu Hashim. We do not deny their virtue, because of the position that God has placed you in among them. What do you think of our brothers, Banu Al-Muttalib? You have given to them and left us, and we and they are of the same status to you? He said: They did not leave us in ignorance or Islam. Banu Hashim and Banu Al-Muttalib are one thing! Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, clasped his hands together.

The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: “The share of the relatives was for the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Banu Hashim and their allies from Banu al-Muttalib,” because the allies of the people were from them, and because of the authenticity of the report that we mentioned about that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Scholars differed regarding the ruling on these two shares - I mean the share of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the share of the relatives - after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Some of them said: They are spent to help Islam and its people.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ahmad bin Yunus told us, he said, Abu Shihab told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Nahshal, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He made the share of God and the share of the Messenger one,
h
and for the near of kin
, so he made these two shares for horses and weapons. And he made the share for orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer, and no one else is given it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim, who said:
m: I asked al-Hasan about the statement of God:
h
And know that whatever you obtain of spoils

- indeed, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger and for the near relatives. He said: This is the key to the statement: God has this world and the Hereafter. Then the people differed about these two shares after the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Some said: The share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is for the relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Others said: The share of the relatives is the caliph. They agreed that these two shares should be for horses and equipment in the way of God, and they were like that during the caliphates of Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, who said:
m: I asked Al-Hasan bin Muhammad, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Omar bin Obaid told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Abu Bakr and Omar, may God be pleased with them, used to put the Prophet’s share in the forelegs and weapons. So I said to Ibrahim: What did Ali, may God be pleased with him, say about it? He said: Ali was the most severe of them about it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils - a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy Al-Ayah. Ibn Abbas said: So the spoils were divided into five fifths: four among those who fought over it, and one fifth was divided among four: for God, the Messenger, and the near relatives - the relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So whatever was for God and the Messenger was for the relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not take anything from the fifth. Then when God took His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, restored the share of the relatives among the Muslims, and he began to carry it in the way of God, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We do not inherit, what we leave behind is charity.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He was asked about the share of the relatives, so he said: It was food for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he died, Abu Bakr and Umar carried it in the way of God, as charity for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said: The share of the relatives after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is with the share of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the guardian of the Muslims.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Amr bin Thabit told us, on the authority of Imran bin Dhibyan, on the authority of Hakim bin Saad, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: Every person is given his share of the fifth, and the share of God and His Messenger is next to the imam.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He was asked about the share of relatives, so he said: It was food for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was alive, and when he died, it was given to the ruler after him.

x: Others said: The share of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is returned in the fifth, and the fifth is divided into three shares: for orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer. This is the opinion of a group of the people of Iraq.
Others said: The entire fifth is for the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abdul Ghaffar told us, he said, Abdul Ghaffar told us, he said, Al-Munhal bin Amr told us, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Ali and Ali bin Al-Hussein about the fifth and they said: It is for us. So I said to Ali: God says: And the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, and they said: Our orphans and our needy.

x: The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is that the share of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is returned in the fifth, and the fifth is divided into four shares, according to what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: a share for the relatives, a share for the orphans, a share for the poor, and a share for the wayfarer, because God made the fifth obligatory for people described by certain characteristics, just as He made the four fifths obligatory for others. They agreed that no one else deserves the right of the four-fifths, and likewise no one else deserves the right of the people of the fifth. It is not permissible for it to go from them to others, just as it is not permissible for some of the shares that God has made for those He has named in His Book to go, due to the absence of some of those who deserve it, to other than the people of the other two shares.
As for orphans, they are Muslim children whose fathers have died. The poor are the needy and destitute Muslims.
