And the wayfarer is the one who has traveled a long journey, such as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The fourth fifth is for the wayfarer, who is the weak and poor person who stays with the Muslims.

x: The statement in the interpretation of His saying: “
h
If you have believed in God and in what We revealed to Our Servant on the Day of Criterion
, the day the two armies met.
And God is over all things competent.”

God Almighty says: Be certain, O believers, that whatever you gain is already divided according to the portion I have explained and you have believed in it, if you have acknowledged the oneness of God and what God revealed to His servant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day He distinguished between truth and falsehood at Badr, and revealed the victory of the believers and their supremacy over their enemy. That was the day the two armies met, the group of believers and the group of polytheists. God is Powerful to destroy disbelief and humiliate them at the hands of the believers, and to do other things that He wills. Nothing He wills is impossible for Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: The Day of Surat al-Anfal 8:41 And know that whatever you gain of anything, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger
h
and for the near of kin
and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer,
h
if you have believed in God and in what We revealed to Our Servant on the Day of Criterion
, the day the two armies met. And God is over all things competent. Discrimination, he means: by Discrimination, the Day of Badr, on which God distinguished between truth and falsehood.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr - and Ishaq
m: said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr - one of them adds more than the other, in his saying:
h
The Day of Discrimination

, the day God distinguished between truth and falsehood, and it is the Day of Badr, and it is the first battle witnessed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The leader of the polytheists was Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, so they met on Friday, nineteen nights before the end of the month of Ramadan, and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were three hundred and some men, and the polytheists were between one thousand and nine hundred. So God defeated the polytheists that day, and killed more than seventy of them, and took a similar number of them captive.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Muqsim:
m: h
The Day of Discrimination
, he said: The Day of Badr, God distinguished between truth and falsehood.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Uthman al-Jazari, on the authority of Muqsim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Day of Discrimination
, he said: On the day of Badr, God distinguished between truth and falsehood.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
The Day of Discrimination is the day the two armies met
, the Day of Badr, and Badr is between Medina and Mecca.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Yahya bin Yaqub Abu Talib told me, on the authority of Abu Awn Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Salami,
m: Abdullah bin Habib said, Al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: The night of Al-Furqan, the day the two armies met, was the seventeenth of the month of Ramadan.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The day the two armies met, Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Kathir said: The day of Badr.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And We did not send down to Our servant
h
the Day of Discrimination
, the day the two armies met, meaning the day I distinguished between truth and falsehood with My power, the day the two armies met, from you and from them.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We did not send down to Our servant on
h
the Day of Discrimination
, and that was the Day of Badr, the day God distinguished between truth and falsehood.

x: God Almighty says: Be certain, O believers: and know that the division of the spoils is according to what your Lord has made clear to you, if you believe in God and what was revealed to His servant on the day of Badr, when He distinguished between truth and falsehood in the victory of His Messenger, when you were, then, on the lower slope, meaning: on the edge of the valley closest to Medina, and they were on the farthest slope, meaning: and your enemy from the polytheists was descending on the edge of the farthest valley to Mecca, and the caravan was below you, meaning: and the caravan in it was Abu Sufyan and his companions in a place lower than you to the seashore. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: When you were on the lower slope, he said: the edge of the lower valley, and they were on the edge of the farthest valley, and the caravan was below you, he said: Abu Sufyan and his companions, below them.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When you were on the lower slope and they were on the farthest slope

, meaning the edge of the valley. The Prophet of God was at the top of the valley, and the polytheists were at the bottom, and the caravan was below you, meaning Abu Sufyan, who took the camel down on his estate until he arrived in Mecca with it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: When you were on the lower side of the valley and they were on the farthest side, from the valley to Mecca, and the caravan was below you, meaning: the caravan of Abu Sufyan that you went out to take and they went out to protect it, without an appointment from you or them.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the caravan is lower than you

, he said: Abu Sufyan and his companions were coming from Ash-Sham as traders. They did not know the people of Badr, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know the infidels of Quraysh, nor the infidels of Quraysh knew Muhammad and his companions, until the one who would water them all met at the water of Badr. Then they fought, and the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated them and took them prisoner.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: He mentioned the dwellings of the people and the caravan, so he said: When you were on the lower slope and they were on the farther slope and the caravan, he is Abu Sufyan, was below you, on the shore of the sea. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: When you were on the enemy. This was read by most of the Medinan and Kufan readers: By the enemy, with a damma on the ‘ayn. Some Meccans and Basrans read it as: By the enemy, with a kasra on the ‘ayn.

x: They are two well-known languages with one meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.

i: He recites the verse of Al-Ra’i: And red eyes, their sockets as the eyes of the enemy, the root With the breaking of the letter ‘ayn from al-‘adwa, and the verse of Aws bin Hajar is also recited:
x: A knight, if the horses were to attack him, would quickly turn away and not intend to advance.

Surat al-Anfal 8:42 When you were on the near slope and they were on the farthest slope and the caravan was below you. If you had made an appointment, you would have differed concerning the appointment. But that God might accomplish a matter which was to be done, that he who perished might perish on the basis of clear evidence and he who lived might live on the basis of clear evidence. And indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And if you had made an appointment
, you would have differed concerning the appointment, but that God might accomplish a matter which was to be done.

God Almighty means: If your gathering in the place where you gathered, you believers and your enemy from the polytheists, had been based on an appointment between you and them, you would have differed about the appointment, due to the large number of your enemy and the small number of you. But God gathered you without an appointment between you and them, so that God may accomplish a matter that was to be done, and that judgment is from God.
His victory was for His friends from the believers in God and His Messenger, and the destruction of His enemies and their enemies at Badr by killing and captivity, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And if you had made an appointment

, you would have differed in the appointment, and if that had been about an appointment between you and them, and then you were informed of their great number and your small number, you would not have met them, but that God may accomplish a matter which was to be accomplished, meaning: that God may accomplish what He willed with His power, of honoring Islam and its people, and humiliating polytheism and its people, without your permission, so He did what He willed of that with His kindness.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik told me: Abdullah ibn Kaʿb said: I heard Kaʿb ibn Malik say in the Battle of Badr: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims went out only to seek the caravan of Quraysh, until God brought them together with their enemy without an appointment.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Umair ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: Abu Sufyan came with the caravan from Ash-Sham, and Abu Jahl went out to protect him from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. So they met at Badr, and these did not know those, nor those knew those, until the water-carriers met. He said: And the people warned one another.

x: The statement in the interpretation of His saying: “So that he who is to perish will perish with clear evidence, and he who lives will live with clear evidence.
And indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.”

God Almighty says: But God gathered them there, to carry out a matter that was to be done, so that he who was to perish would perish with clear evidence. This lam in his saying: So that he may perish is repeated on the lam in his saying: So that he may decide, as if he said: But so that he who perishes may perish with clear evidence, he gathered you. What he means by his saying: So that he who perishes will perish with clear evidence, is that he who dies from among His creation will die with a proof from God that has been established for him and cut off his excuse, and a lesson that he has witnessed and seen. And he who lives will live with clear evidence, meaning: And he who lives from among them will live with a proof from God that has been established for him and appeared to his eye so that he knows it. We will gather you and your enemy there.
Ibn Ishaq said about this:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: So that he who is destroyed will perish on the basis of clear evidence, meaning that he who disbelieved after the proof will disbelieve, because of what he saw of the sign and the lesson, and he who believed will believe on the basis of something similar. As for His statement: And indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, its meaning is: And indeed, God, O believers, is All-Hearing, of what you say and what others say, when God sees His Prophet in his sleep and shows you, your enemy in your eyes as few while they are many, and your enemy sees you in their eyes as few, All-Knowing, of what your souls conceal and your hearts contain, at that time and in every situation. God Almighty says to them and to His servants: So fear your Lord, O people, in your speech: lest you speak without truth, and in your hearts: lest you believe in them other than what is right, for nothing, outward or inward, is hidden from God.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: When you were on the enemy.
This was read by most of the Medinan and Kufan readers: By the enemy, with a damma on the ‘ayn.
Some Meccans and Basrans read it as: By the enemy, with a kasra on the ‘ayn.

He recites the verse of Al-Ra’i: And red eyes, their sockets as the eyes of the enemy, the root With the breaking of the letter ‘ayn from al-‘adwa, and the verse of Aws bin Hajar is also recited: A knight, if the horses were to attack him, would quickly turn away and not intend to advance.

x: God Almighty says: And God, O Muhammad, is All-Hearing of what your companions say, All-Knowing of what they conceal, when God shows you your enemy and their enemy: in your sleep, a little, meaning: He shows them to you in your sleep, a little, so you inform them of that, until their hearts become strong, and they dare to fight their enemy. And if your Lord had shown you your enemy and their enemy as many, your companions would have failed, become cowardly and weak, and would not have been able to fight the people, and they would have disputed about that.
h
But God saved
them from that by what He showed you in your sleep of the vision. He is All-Knowing of what the hearts conceal, nothing that the hearts conceal is hidden from Him.
Some of them claimed that the meaning of his saying:
h
When God shows them to you in your dream

, little by little, is: in the eye with which you sleep, so the dream became the eye, as if he meant: When God shows them to you in your eye, little by little. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: When God showed them to you in your dream as few, he said: God showed them to him in his dream as few, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed his companions of that, and it was a confirmation for them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. ...and he said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Abu Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: When God showed them to you in your dream, but little, the verse. So the first thing that he showed them was a blessing from His blessings upon them, with which He encouraged them against their enemy, and with which He kept from them what He feared for them of their weakness, because of His knowledge of what was in them.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying:
h
But God saved
Some of them said: Its meaning is: But God granted the believers their affair, until He made them victorious over their enemy.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But God made them safe
, meaning: God made their matter safe for them until He made them victorious over their enemy.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: But God made His command regarding them sound.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
But God made them safe
, he said: He made His command regarding them safe.

x: The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is what Ibn ʿAbbas said, which is that God saved the people - by what He showed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his dream - from failure and dispute, until their hearts became strong and they dared to fight their enemy. This is because His statement,
h
But God saved

, follows His statement, And if He had shown you them in large numbers, you would have lost heart and would have disputed over the matter, so what is more deserving of the report is that He saved them from Him, may His praise be glorified, which would have been feared if His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had not seen the small number of people in his dream.

God Almighty says: And indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, when God shows His Prophet in his dream the polytheists as few, and when God shows them the believers when they meet them as few in their eyes while they are many in number, and He makes the believers seem small in their eyes, so that they stop preparing for them, and their strength becomes easy for the believers, as:

c: Ibn Buzayʿ al-Baghdadi told me, he said, Ishaq ibn Mansur told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: They seemed small in our eyes on the day of Badr, until I said to a man next to me: Do you think they are seventy? He said: I think they are a hundred! He said: So we captured one of them and we said: How many are they? He said: A thousand.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, Ibn Masoud said: They were few in our eyes, until I said to a man: Do you think they would be a hundred?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: Some of the polytheists said:
m: The caravan has turned back, so go back. Abu Jahl said: Now that Muhammad and his companions have come out to you! Do not go back until you have exterminated them. He said: O people, do not kill them with weapons, but seize them by force, and tie them up with ropes! He said this out of his own power. And His saying: That God may accomplish a matter which was to be done, the Most High says: I have made you, O believers, few in the eyes of the polytheists, and have made them appear to you as few in your eyes, until God has accomplished between you what He has accomplished of fighting one another, and has made you, O believers, victorious over your enemies among the polytheists and triumphed over them, so that the word of God may be supreme, and the word of those who disbelieve may be inferior. And that is a matter which God will do and will accomplish His command in it, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: So that God may carry out a matter that was to be done, meaning: to unite them for war, to take revenge on whoever He wanted to take revenge on, and to bestow favors on whoever He wanted to complete the favor on from among the people of his authority. And to God all matters return, says the Most High: All matters will return to Him in the Hereafter, and He will reward those who deserve them according to what they deserve, the good-doer for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil.

x: This is a definition from God, the Most High, to the people of faith in Him, the conduct in the war against His enemies from among the people of disbelief in Him, and the actions that are hoped for them to use when they meet them, victory over them and triumph over them. Then He, the Most High, says to them:
h
O you who have believed

, believe in God and His Messenger, if you meet a group of the people of disbelief in God for war and fighting, then stand firm to fight them, and do not flee from them or turn your backs to them, except to divert from fighting or to join a group of you, and remember God often, meaning: and call upon God for victory over them and triumph over them, and make your hearts and tongues feel His remembrance, that you may succeed, meaning: so that you may succeed and triumph over your enemy, and God may grant you victory and triumph over them, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
, when you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much that you may be successful, God has made it obligatory to remember Him when you are most occupied, when fighting with swords.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
O you who have believed

, when you meet a company, fighting you in the way of God, then stand firm and remember God much, remember God to whom you have sacrificed yourselves and fulfill what you have given of your pledge, that you may be successful.

x: God Almighty says to those who believe in Him: Obey, O believers, your Lord and His Messenger in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, and do not disobey them in anything, and do not dispute and lose courage, meaning: do not differ and become divided and your hearts differ, and lose courage, meaning: become weak and avoid, and your strength departs. This is a proverb. It is said to a man if he is facing something he loves and is pleased with: The wind is facing him, meaning what he loves. An example of this is the saying of Ubayd ibn al-Abrash: As We protected you on the Day of Nafs from the blows and the favor of the people from the wind and from the number Meaning: from strength and abundance. What is meant here is: Your strength and power will be lost, you will become weak, and weakness and dysfunction will enter you. And be patient, meaning: Be patient with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when you meet your enemy, and do not flee from him and abandon him.
Indeed, God is with the patient, meaning: Be patient, for I am with you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And your strength will depart
, he said: Your victory. He said: And the strength of the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, departed when they disputed with him on the day of Uhud.

c: Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And your scent will depart, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar, except that he said: The scent of Muhammad’s companions when they left him on the day of Uhud.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And do not dispute and [thus] lose courage
and your strength departs, he said: Your limit and your seriousness.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And your wind will depart
, he said: The wind of war.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And your wind will depart
, he said: The wind is victory. There has never been victory except by a wind that God sends to strike the faces of the enemy, and if that happens, they will have no strength.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And do not dispute and lose courage, meaning: do not differ and your matter becomes divided, and your strength departs, meaning: your limit is lost, and be patient, for God is with the patient, meaning: I am with you if you do that.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And do not dispute and [thus] lose courage
, he said: Failure is weakness in fighting one’s enemy and being defeated by them, so that is (failure).

x: This is an advance from God, the Most High, to the believers in Him and His Messenger, that they should not do any work except for God alone, and to seek what is with Him, not to show off to people, as the polytheists did on their way to Badr, seeking to show off to people. That is because they were informed that the caravan of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions had missed, and it was said to them: (Go back, for the caravan that you came to support has been saved!), but they refused and said: (We will go to Badr and drink wine there, and the female singers will play for us, and the Arabs will talk about us there), so they were given cups of death instead of wine, as:

c: Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Abaan told us, he said, Hisham bin Urwah told us, on the authority of Urwah, he said:
m: Before the Quraysh met the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr, a rider from Abu Sufyan and the caravan who were with him came to them and said: We have passed the people, so go back. Then the caravan that Abu Sufyan had sent to order the Quraysh to go back to Al-Juhfah came and said: ((By God, we will not go back until we camp at Badr and stay there for three nights, and those of the people of Hijaz who attacked us will see us, for no one from the Arabs will see us and what we have gathered and fight us.)) They are the ones about whom God said: Those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people, and they and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, feared God, so God granted victory to His Messenger, and disgraced the leaders of disbelief, and healed the hearts of the believers among them. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, Ibn Ishaq narrated - in a hadith he mentioned - he narrated, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Asim ibn Umar, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, and Yazid ibn Ruman narrated, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and other scholars of ours, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When Abu Sufyan saw that he had secured his caravan, he sent word to the Quraysh 106:You only came out to protect your caravan, your men, and your wealth, but God has saved them, so go back! Abu Jahl ibn Hisham said: By God, we will not go back until we return to Badr - and Badr was a season of the Arabs, where they held a market every year - and we will stay there for three days, slaughter camels, feed the poor, and drink wine, and the female singers will play for us, and the Arabs will hear about us, and they will continue to fear us forever, so go on. Ibn Humayd said: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq said: And do not be like those who left their homes in arrogance and to be seen by people, meaning: Do not be like Abu Jahl and his companions who said: We will not return until we reach Badr, slaughter camels, and drink wine there, and the female singers play for us, and the Arabs hear about us, and they will not cease to fear us, meaning: Do not let your affair be for show or reputation, or seeking what people have, and be sincere in your intention and calculation for God in supporting your religion and assisting your Prophet, meaning: Do not work except for God, and do not seek anyone other than Him.

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said, Israel told us, and Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Those who left their homes insolently
and to be seen by people, he said: The companions of Badr.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Insolently and to show off to people
, he said: Abu Jahl and his companions on the day of Badr.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. Ibn Jurayj said, and Abdullah bin Kathir said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh, and that was their going out to Badr.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people, meaning: the polytheists who fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They left their homes in arrogance and to be seen by people. He said: They are Quraysh, Abu Jahl and his companions, who left on the day of Badr.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “And be not like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people and avert [people] from the way of God. And God encompasses what they do.” He said: “The polytheists of Quraysh who fought the Prophet of God on the day of Badr went forth with transgression and pride. And it was said to them on that day: ‘Go back, for your caravan has set out and you have been victorious.’ They said: ‘No, by God, not until the people of Hijaz speak of our march and our numbers!’” He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on that day: ‘O God, Quraysh has come forth with its pride and arrogance to challenge You and Your Messenger!’”

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: He mentioned the polytheists and what they eat on the waters, so he said: Do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people and to hinder [people] from the way of God.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Those who left their homes insolently
, he said: They are the polytheists, who went out to Badr insolently and insolently.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi, he said:
m: When the Quraysh left Mecca for Badr, they went out with the singing girls and the tambourines, so God revealed: “And be not like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people and to avert [people] from the way of God. And God encompasses what they do.”

x: The interpretation of the statement then is: O believers in God and His Messenger, do not act for show and reputation, and do not sincerely work for God and expect reward for it, like the army of the disbelievers in God and His Messenger who left their homes in arrogance and showing off to people with their clothing, their wealth, their large numbers and the strength of their entourage, and hinder [people] from the way of God, meaning: and they prevent people from the religion of God and from entering Islam, by fighting them and torturing those they can of the people of faith in God, and God encompasses what they do, of showing off and hindering people from the way of God, and other than that of their actions, and God is All-Knowing, meaning: He knows all of that, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and that is because all things are manifest to Him, nothing of them is hidden from Him, so He is their successor and punisher for them.
God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And when Satan made their deeds seem good to them
h
and when Satan made their deeds seem good to them
, and his making that seem good to them, was like:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Iblis came on the day of Badr with an army of devils, with his banner, in the form of a man from Banu Mudlij, and the devil was in the form of Suraqah bin Malik bin Ju’sham. The devil said to the polytheists: No one from among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector. When the people lined up, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a handful of dirt and threw it in the faces of the polytheists, and they turned away. Gabriel came to Iblis, and when he saw him, and his hand was in the hand of a man from among the polytheists, Iblis pulled his hand away and turned away, he and his followers. The man said: O Suraqah, do you claim that you are our protector? He said: “Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear God, and God is severe in penalty.” That was when he saw the angels.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Satan came to the polytheists in the form of Suraqah bin Malik bin Ja’sham Al-Kinani, the poet, then Al-Mudlaji. He came on a horse and said to the polytheists: No one from among the people will defeat you today! They said: And who are you? He said: I am your neighbor Suraqah, and these are Kinanah who have come to you!

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us, Yazid ibn Ruman told me, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said:
m: When the Quraysh decided to march, they remembered what had happened between them and Banu Ka’b - meaning the war - and that almost made them stop. Then Satan appeared to them in the form of Suraqa [bin Malik] ibn Ja’sham al-Mudlaji, who was one of the nobles of Banu Kinanah, and he said: I will protect you from Kinanah coming to you from behind you with something you dislike! So they set out quickly.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them

and said, ‘No one from among mankind can overcome you this Day, and indeed, I am your protector,’ then He mentioned Satan’s luring them and his imitation of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ja’sham to them when they mentioned what was between them and Banu Bakr ibn Abd Manat ibn Kinanah in the war that had taken place between them. God says: So when the two armies saw each other, and the enemy of God looked at the soldiers of God from the angels with whom God had supported His Messenger and the believers against their enemy, “he turned back on his heels and said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I see what you do not see.’” And the enemy of God was truthful, for he saw what they did not see, and he said, Indeed, I fear God, and God is severe in penalty, so he brought them in and then surrendered them. He said: It was mentioned to me that they used to see him in every house in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ja’sham and they did not deny him. Even when it was the day of Badr and the two armies met, the one who saw him when he retreated was either Al-Harith bin Hisham or Umair bin Wahb Al-Jumahi. He mentioned one of them and said: Where, O Suraaq! And he represented the enemy of God and left.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them

, until his statement: severe in penalty, he said: It was mentioned to us that it was Gabriel with whom the angels descend, so the enemy of God claimed that he had no hand in the angels, and he said: “Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear God,” and by God, the enemy of God lied, he had no fear of God, but he knew that he had no strength or protection, and that is the habit of the enemy of God for those who obey him and seek his revenge, until when truth and falsehood meet, he surrenders to them as the worst of Muslims, and disavows them at that time.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them

, the verse, he said: When the day of Badr came, Satan marched with his banner and his soldiers with the polytheists, and he cast into the hearts of the polytheists: No one will defeat you, and I am your protector! So when they met, and Satan Surat al-Anfal 8:48 And when Satan made their deeds pleasing to them and said, "No one can overcome you today from among the people, and indeed, I am your protector." But when the two companies saw each other, he turned back on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear God, and God is severe in penalty." looked at the reinforcements of the angels, he turned back on his heels - he said: he retreated - and said: Indeed, I see what you do not see, the verse.

c: Ahmad ibn al-Faraj told us, Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Majshun told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, on the authority of Talha ibn Ubayd God ibn Kurayz:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Iblis has never been seen on a day when he is smaller, more contemptible, more defeated, or more angry than on the Day of Arafah. This is because of what he sees of the sending down of mercy and forgiveness of sins, except what he saw on the Day of Badr!’ They said: ‘O Messenger of God, what did he see on the Day of Badr?’ He said: ‘He saw Gabriel commanding the angels.’”
b.via: Talha ibn Ubayd God ibn Kurayz

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sulayman bin al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Hamid bin Hilal, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, I see what you do not see, he said: He saw Gabriel wrapped in a cloak, walking in front of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in his hand was the bridle, and he did not ride. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, Hashim ibn Al-Qasim narrated, Sulayman ibn Al-Mugheerah narrated, on the authority of Humayd ibn Hilal, who said: Al-Hasan said, reciting this verse: And when Satan made their deeds pleasing to them Al-Baqarah 2:17, he said: Iblis marched with the polytheists at Badr with his banner and his soldiers, and he cast into the hearts of the polytheists that no one will defeat you while you are fighting for the religion of your fathers, and you will never be defeated by numbers! So when they met, he turned back on his heels - he said: he retreated - and said: “Indeed, I am innocent of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see,” meaning the angels.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb, he said:
m: When the Quraysh decided to march, they said: We only fear Banu Bakr! Then Satan said to them, in the form of Suraqa bin Malik bin Jaʿsham: I am your protector from Banu Bakr, and no one from among the people can defeat you today.

x: The interpretation of the statement: And indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing is in these circumstances, and when Satan made their coming out to you, O believers, to fight and fight you seem attractive to them and urged them against you, and said to them: No one from the children of Adam can overcome you today, so be reassured and be glad, And indeed, I am your protector, from Kinanah lest they come to you from behind you, so I will protect you, I will shelter you and I will protect you from them, so do not fear them, and make your punishment and your might upon Muhammad and his companions, So when the two armies saw one another, meaning: when the soldiers of God from the believers and the soldiers of Satan from the polytheists advanced, and some of them looked at each other, he turned back on his heels, meaning: he retreated backwards on his back, fleeing.

(He turned back, he turned back, he turned back a turning back), and from it is the saying of Zuhair: They beat your white fox, if they catch up they do not retreat, if they are attacked and protected He said to the polytheists: “I am innocent of you. I see what you do not see.”
He meant that he sees the angels whom God sent to support the believers, but the polytheists do not see them. I fear God’s punishment, and the enemy of God lied. And God is severe in penalty.
God Almighty says: And indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, in these circumstances, And
h
when the hypocrites say
, and he repeated his statement:
h
When the hypocrites say

, on his statement: When God showed them to you in your dream, little, “And those in whose hearts is disease,” meaning: doubt in Islam, their certainty was not sound, and their chests were not opened to faith, These people were deceived by their religion, meaning: these people who fight the polytheists from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were deceived by their religion, and that is Islam. He mentioned that those who said this statement were a group of polytheists from Quraysh who had spoken about Islam, but Islam had not yet taken root in their hearts.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer,
m: regarding this verse:
h
When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say

, ‘These people have been deceived by their religion,’ he said: There were people from Mecca who spoke about Islam, so they went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr. When they saw the small number of Muslims, they said, These people have been deceived by their religion.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told me, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer,
m: the same.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Yahya bin Zakariya told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said

, ‘These people have been deceived by their religion,’ he said: A group of Quraysh 106:Abu Qais bin Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, Abu Qais bin Al-Fakih bin Al-Mughira, Al-Harith bin Zama’ah bin Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib, Ali bin Umayya bin Khalaf, and Al-Asi bin Munabbih bin Al-Hajjaj, left Mecca with Quraysh while they were in doubt, but their doubt held them back. When they saw the small number of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said, These people have been deceived by their religion, until they proceeded as they proceeded, despite their small number and the large number of their enemy, and those behind them were scattered by them.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say

, ‘These people have been deceived by their religion,’ he said: They are people who did not witness the fighting on the day of Badr, so they were called hypocrites. Muammar said: Some of them said: They were people who had acknowledged Islam while they were in Mecca, so they went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr, and when they saw the small number of Muslims, they said, These people have been deceived by their religion.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said

, until his statement: Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise, he said: They saw a group of believers scattered for the sake of God. And it was mentioned to us that when Abu Jahl, the enemy of God, looked down upon Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, he said: By God, God will not be worshipped after today! out of cruelty and arrogance.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said
m: regarding His statement:
h
When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say
, Surat al-Anfal 8:49
h
When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say

, “These people have been deluded by their religion.” But whoever relies upon God - then indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise. he said: There were people from the hypocrites in Mecca who said it on the day of Badr, and they were three hundred and some men that day. ... He said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding His statement:
h
When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said

, he said: When the people drew near to one another, God made the Muslims few in the eyes of the polytheists, and made the polytheists few in the eyes of the Muslims, the polytheists said: These people have been deceived by their religion, and they only said that because they were few in their eyes, and they thought that they would defeat them, and they had no doubt about that, so God said:
h
And whoever relies upon God
- then indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise. As for his saying:
h
And whoever relies upon God

, its meaning is: And whoever submits his affair to God, trusts in Him, and is satisfied with His judgment, then God will protect and support him, because He is Mighty, nothing can overcome Him, and no one can subdue Him. His neighbor is impregnable, and whoever relies upon Him is sufficient. This is an order from God, the Most High, to the believers in Him from the companions of the Messenger of God and others, that they should entrust their affairs to Him and submit to His judgment, so that He may suffice them against their enemies and not humiliate them from those who oppose them, because He is Mighty and not defeated, so His neighbor is not subjugated, Wise, meaning that He is Wise in what He manages of the affairs of His creation, and no defect enters into His management.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you could see, O Muhammad, when the angels take the souls of the infidels, and extract them from their bodies, they strike their faces and buttocks, and say to them: Taste the torment of the fire that will burn you on the day you enter Hell. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved
h
they strike their faces and their backs
, he said: On the day of Badr.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Saleem told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They strike their faces and their backsides, he said: And their buttocks, but God is generous and uses euphemisms.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They strike their faces and their backs
, he said: And their backsides, but he is generous and uses a euphemism.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Wahb ibn Jarir told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Yaʿla ibn Muslim, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They strike their faces and their backs
, he said: God used a metaphor, and if He had wanted, He would have said: their backsides, but what He meant by their backsides was their backsides.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: He struck them on the day of Badr. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: When the polytheists turned their faces toward the Muslims, they struck their faces with swords. And when they turned away, the angels caught up with them and struck their backsides.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Ibad bin Rashid told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: “A man said: O Messenger of God, I saw something like a strap on Abu Jahl’s back! He said: What is that? He said: The angels’ beating.”

c: Muhammad told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “A man said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I attacked a polytheist and went to strike him, but his head fell off. He said: The king got to him before you.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Harmalah told me:
m: He heard Umar, the freed slave of Ghafra, say: When you hear God say:
h
They strike their faces and their backs
, he means: their buttocks.

x: There is an omission in the speech, and the apparent meaning of it sufficed without mentioning it, which is His statement: (And they say), Taste the punishment of the burning fire. (They say) was omitted, just as it was omitted from His statement: ((And if you could but see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, Our Lord, we have seen and heard (al-Sajdah 32:21)), meaning: they say: Our Lord, we have seen.

God Almighty says, informing about what the angels said to these polytheists who were killed at Badr, that they said to them while they were striking their faces and backs: (Taste the punishment of God which burns you), this punishment is for you, for what your hands have put forth, meaning: for what your hands have earned of sins and burdens, and what you have committed of disobedience to God during the days of your life, so taste the punishment today, and in your return there is the punishment of burning, and that is for you because God is not unjust to His servants, He does not punish anyone of His creation except for a crime he has committed, and He does not punish him except for his disobedience to Him, because injustice cannot be from Him. In the opening of that in his saying: and that God there are two aspects of parsing: One of them: the accusative, which is for the purpose of connecting with what in His statement: because of what you have put forward, meaning: that is because of what your hands have put forward, and that God is not unjust to the servants, according to the statement of some of them, and the genitive, according to the statement of some. The other: raising, on that is because of what you have presented, and that is because God.

God Almighty says: The actions of these polytheists from Quraysh who were killed at Badr were like the custom of the people of Pharaoh, their actions and deeds, and the actions of those who denied the proofs of God and His messengers from the nations before them, so we did to them as we did to those. We have previously explained that habit is the affair and habit, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told me, he said, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer,
m: Mujahid, and Ata’: Like the way of Pharaoh’s family, like the actions of Pharaoh’s family, like the customs of Pharaoh’s family. And His statement:
h
So God seized them for their sins

, meaning: God punished them for their denial of His proofs and His messengers, and their disobedience to their Lord, just as He punished their peers and the nations before them. Indeed, God is Powerful, no one can overcome Him, and no one can repel His judgment. He executes His command, and His judgment is carried out among His creation. His punishment is severe for whoever disbelieves in God and rejects His proofs.

x: God Almighty says: And We seized those who disbelieved in Our signs from the polytheists of Quraysh at Badr for their sins, and We did that to them, because they changed the blessing that God had bestowed upon them by sending His Messenger from among them and among them, by expelling him from among them, denying him, and waging war against him, so We changed Our blessing upon them by destroying them, as We did that to those who came before them from among those who rebelled against Us and disobeyed Our command. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: That is because God will not change a blessing which He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is within themselves. He says: The blessing of God, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, bestowed it upon the Quraysh, and they disbelieved, so he conveyed it to the Ansar. And His statement: And that God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, means: Nothing of the speech of His creation is hidden from Him. He hears the speech of every speaker among them, whether good or evil. All-Knowing, of what their hearts conceal, and He will reward and recompense them for what they say and do, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

x: God Almighty says: Other than these polytheists who were killed by God, who were killed at Badr, the blessing of their Lord that He bestowed upon them, by sending Muhammad from among them and among them, calling them to guidance, by their denial of him and their war against him, like the way of the people of Pharaoh, like the way of the people of Pharaoh and their custom and their actions with Moses, the Prophet of God, in their denial of him and their intention to war against him, and the custom of the nations before them who denied their messengers and their actions, so We destroyed them for their sins, some by the earthquake, some by the sinking, and some by the wind, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh, in the sea, and all of them were wrongdoers, meaning: All of these nations that We destroyed were doing what they should not have done, by their denial of the messengers of God and their denial of His signs. Thus We destroyed those whom We destroyed at Badr, when they changed the favor of God upon them, by killing with the sword, and We humiliated some of them by captivity and captivity.

God Almighty says: The worst of what has crawled on the earth in the sight of God are those who disbelieved in their Lord, denied His oneness, and worshipped other than Him. They do not believe, meaning: they do not believe in God’s messengers, nor do they acknowledge His revelation and sending down.

God Almighty says: Indeed, the worst of beasts in the sight of God are those who disbelieve, “those of whom you have made a covenant,” O Muhammad, meaning: You have taken their covenants and pledges that they will not fight you, nor support one another against you in fighting you, like the Qurayza and their peers, between whom and you there was a covenant and agreement, then they break, their covenants and pledges, whenever they have made a covenant with you and trusted you, they fight you and support one another against you, and they do not fear God, nor do they fear in doing that that He will bring upon them a battle that will overwhelm them and destroy them, like the one who:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Those of them with whom you made a treaty, then they break their treaty, he said: Qurayza, they plotted against Muhammad on the day of the Trench, his enemies.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you encounter in war those with whom you have made a covenant time after time from Qurayza, and you take them prisoner, then disperse with them those behind them, meaning: Do to them an act that will disperse those behind them who are their peers, those with whom you have a covenant and agreement. Displacement means expulsion, dispersion and separation. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ordered to do this to the one who broke the covenant between him and them if he had power over them, an act that would frighten those behind them, those with whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a covenant, so that they would not dare to do what these people, whom God described in this verse as breaking the covenant, dared to do. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if you catch them in war
, disperse by them those behind them, meaning: punish them after them.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And He scattered them from behind them, meaning: He tormented them from behind them.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: But if you catch up with them in war, disperse through them those behind them, meaning: Admonish others from among the people through them.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But if you catch them in war
, scatter them from those behind them, meaning: punish them from those behind them, from the enemy after them, so that they may beware of breaking their oath and you may do the same to them.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: And he dispersed with them those behind them, he said: He warned with them those behind them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: They were punished by those behind them, after them. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Kathir said: They were punished by those behind them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: But if you overtake them in war, disperse them from behind so that they may remember, meaning: torment them from behind so that they may understand.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim say regarding His statement:
h
And He scattered with them those who came after them
, meaning: He punished them after them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the statement of God: But if you overtake them in war, disperse with them those behind them, he said: Hide them by what you do to these people. And he recited: “And others besides them whom you do not know. God knows them” (al-Anfal 8:60). As for his saying: Perhaps they will remember, its meaning is: So that they may learn a lesson from what you did to those whose characteristics you described, so that they may beware of breaking the covenant between you and them, for fear that what happened to these people will happen to them if they break it.

x: God Almighty says: And if you fear, O Muhammad, an enemy with whom you have a covenant and agreement, that he will break his covenant, violate his contract, and betray you, and that is (treachery) and treachery,
h
then throw back to them on equal terms

, meaning: fight them in war, and inform them before you fight them that you have abrogated the covenant between you and them, because of what they had shown of signs of treachery and betrayal, so that you and they will be on equal terms in knowing that you are fighting them, so they will take up the tools of war, and you will be free from treachery. Indeed, God does not love the treacherous, those who betray someone with whom he had a safe haven and a covenant between him and that he will betray him and fight him, before informing him that there is no war and that he has broken the covenant.
How is it permissible to break a covenant out of fear of betrayal, when fear is suspicion, not certainty?

The matter is different from what you have said, but rather its meaning is: If signs of treachery appear from your enemy, and you fear that they will attack you, then give them the reins of peace and declare war on them. This is like what happened with Banu Qurayzah when they responded to Abu Sufyan and the polytheists who were with him to support them against the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and fight them with them, after the covenant they had made with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) to be peaceful and not fight the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). Their response to that caused the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) to fear treachery against him and his companions from them. This is the ruling of every people who have a truce with the believers, and the Imam of the Muslims has seen signs of treachery from them like what appeared to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and his companions from Qurayzah, so it is the duty of the Imam of the Muslims to denounce them equally and declare war on them. The meaning of his saying: on an equal footing is: until your knowledge and their knowledge are equal that each group of you is at war with the other, not at peace.
It was said: The verse was revealed about Qurayza.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then throw back to them equally, he said: Qurayza.

x: Some of them used to say: The equal in this context means the grace period.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said:
m: It has become clear to us that his statement,
h
Then throw back to them on equal terms

, means: slowly, as Bakir told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, regarding the statement of God, “A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty. So travel freely throughout the land for four months,” (al-Tawbah 9:1-2). As for the people who know the Arabic language, they differ on its meaning.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: So, throw it to them in justice, meaning: until your knowledge and their knowledge of what you are doing to each other in terms of fighting each other are equal. And they cited as evidence for their saying that the words of the rajaz poet: Strike the faces of your treacherous enemies until they respond to you in the same way.

Others said: It means: the middle, from the saying of Hassan: Woe to the supporters of the Messenger and his family after sunset in the midst of the atheists Meaning: in the middle of the grave. Likewise, these meanings are close, because justice is a middle ground that does not rise above the truth nor fall short of it. Likewise, the middle ground is justice, and the equality of the two parties’ knowledge regarding what they owe each other after the truce is justice from the verb and the middle ground. As for what Al-Walid bin Muslim said, that its meaning is respite, I do not know of any basis for it in the speech of the Arabs. Surat al-Anfal 8:58 And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them upon equity. Indeed, God does not like traitors.

The readings differed in the reading of that. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as: “And never think that those who disbelieve have outstripped us. Indeed, they have outstripped us with their own souls,” with a kasra on the alif of that they are, and with a ta’ in to think, meaning: And never think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieved have outstripped us and have evaded us with their own souls. Then the report of God’s power over them began, and it was said: Indeed, these disbelievers are not able to defeat their Lord, if He seeks them and wants to punish and destroy them, with their own souls, so that they evade Him with them.

Some of the readers of Medina and Kufa read it as: And let not those who disbelieve think, with the letter ya in yasibna and the letter alif in inhanma being broken. This is an unfavorable reading for two reasons: one of them is that it is outside the reading of the Qur’an and is an anomaly of it, and the other is that it is far from the eloquent speech of the Arabs. This is because in the speech of the Arabs, the word yasb is used in the accusative case and its predicate, as in the saying: Abdullah yasbun ‘akhik qaymun and yaqūm and qām he stood up. So the reciter of this reading made yasb the predicate of something not mentioned. Rather, what he meant, I think, was: “And let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped Us. Indeed, they cannot outstrip Us.” So he did not think about the correctness or weakness of the way the speech was pronounced, and he used in his reading that as well what appeared to him from the meaning of the speech.

I think that what prompted him to do that was the consideration of the reading of Abdullah. This is because what is mentioned in the Mushaf of Abdullah is: “And let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped Us. Indeed, they cannot outstrip Us.” This is eloquent and correct, if you include anhum in the speech, because yasbun is the operator of anhum, and if there is no anhum in the speech, it is devoid of a noun that operates on it. For the one who reads this from the reading, there are two aspects in the speech of the Arabs, even if they are far from their eloquent speech: One of them: that what was meant by it is: And let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped, or that they have outstripped, then (that) and (that they) were deleted, as God Almighty said: And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, [causing] fear and hope, (al-Rum 30:24), meaning: that He shows you, and a verse of Dhu al-Rummah may be recited in something similar to that: I think Ibn Tarthouth Otaiba is going with my habit of lying and making up stories Meaning: I think Ibn Tarthouth will go with my habit of lying and making up stories?

And likewise the reading of the one who reads that with the letter ya’, directs sabaqoo to sabiqeen in this meaning. The second aspect is that he intended it to be accusative with he thinks, as if he said: And let not those who disbelieve think that they will outstrip you, then he deleted that they and implied it.
Some of them have interpreted the meaning of his statement: It is only Satan who frightens his allies
r
(Al Imran 3:175)

as: It is only Satan who frightens the believer from his allies, and that the mention of the believer is implied in his statement: frightens, since Satan, according to him, does not frighten his allies.

Some of the people of Ash-Sham read it as: And do not think that those who disbelieve with the ta’ of tahsabna “have outstripped them that they will not be unable” with the fatha of the alif of that they will be unable, meaning: And do not think that those who disbelieve will not be unable.

There is no rational basis for this reading, unless the reader intended by la in yaʿjizun “la” which enters into the speech as a filler and a link, so the meaning of the speech then would be: And do not think that those who disbelieve have outstripped that they will be unable. There is no basis for directing a letter in the Book of God to lengthening, without an argument that must be accepted, and it has a way out in the correctness.

The correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read: (And do not think), with a taʿ, (those who disbelieved have outstripped us), with a kasra on the alif of (innahum), (they are not incapable), meaning: And do not think, O Muhammad, that those who denied the proofs of God and belied them, have outstripped us by themselves and have outstripped us, they are not incapable of us, meaning: they will outstrip us by themselves, and they are not able to escape from us, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “And let not those who disbelieve think that they will outstrip. Indeed, they will not escape.” He said: They will not escape. Surat al-Anfal 8:59 And let not those who disbelieve think that they will outstrip Us. Indeed, they will not cause failure.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as: “And never think that those who disbelieve have outstripped us.
Some of the readers of Medina and Kufa read it as: And let not those who disbelieve think, with the letter ya in yasibna and the letter alif in inhanma being broken.

This is an unfavorable reading for two reasons: one of them is that it is outside the reading of the Qur’an and is an anomaly of it, and the other is that it is far from the eloquent speech of the Arabs.
So the reciter of this reading made yasb the predicate of something not mentioned.
So he did not think about the correctness or weakness of the way the speech was pronounced, and he used in his reading that as well what appeared to him from the meaning of the speech.
I think that what prompted him to do that was the consideration of the reading of Abdullah.

For the one who reads this from the reading, there are two aspects in the speech of the Arabs, even if they are far from their eloquent speech: One of them: that what was meant by it is: And let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped, or that they have outstripped, then (that) and (that they) were deleted, as God Almighty said: And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, [causing] fear and hope, (al-Rum 30:24), meaning: that He shows you, and a verse of Dhu al-Rummah may be recited in something similar to that: I think Ibn Tarthouth Otaiba is going with my habit of lying and making up stories Meaning: I think Ibn Tarthouth will go with my habit of lying and making up stories?
And likewise the reading of the one who reads that with the letter ya’, directs sabaqoo to sabiqeen in this meaning.

Some of the people of Ash-Sham read it as: And do not think that those who disbelieve with the ta’ of tahsabna “have outstripped them that they will not be unable” with the fatha of the alif of that they will be unable, meaning: And do not think that those who disbelieve will not be unable.

Abu Jaʿfar said: There is no rational basis for this reading, unless the reader intended by la in yaʿjizun “la” which enters into the speech as a filler and a link, so the meaning of the speech then would be: And do not think that those who disbelieve have outstripped that they will be unable.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read: (And do not think), with a taʿ, (those who disbelieved have outstripped us), with a kasra on the alif of (innahum), (they are not incapable), meaning: And do not think, O Muhammad, that those who denied the proofs of God and belied them, have outstripped us by themselves and have outstripped us, they are not incapable of us, meaning: they will outstrip us by themselves, and they are not able to escape from us, as:

x: God Almighty says: And prepare, for those who disbelieved in their Lord, with whom you have a treaty, if you fear their treachery and deceit, O believers in God and His Messenger, whatever you are able of power, meaning: whatever you are able to prepare of the tools that will be a force for you against them, of weapons and horses, to terrify thereby the enemy of God and your enemy, meaning: you terrify by your preparation the enemy of God and your enemy from the polytheists. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Usama bin Zaid, on the authority of Salih bin Kaysan, on the authority of a man from Juhayna, tracing the hadith back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
And prepare against them whatever you are able of power
. Beware, archery is power. Beware, archery is power.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Saeed bin Sharhabil told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib,
m: and Abdul Karim bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abu Ali Al-Hamadani: “He heard Uqbah bin Amir on the pulpit saying: God said: ‘
h
And prepare against them whatever you are able of power
and of steeds of war.’ Beware, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the pulpit: God said: ‘
h
And prepare against them whatever you are able of power
.’ Beware, power is archery. Beware, power is archery, three times.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said,
m: Mahbub, Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn, Wakiʿ, Abu Usamah, and Abu Naʿim told us, on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd, on the authority of Salih ibn Kaysan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir al-Juhani, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited on the pulpit: ‘
h
And prepare against them whatever you are able of power
and of steeds of war. ’ Then he said: ‘Beware, power is archery, beware, power is archery,’ three times.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, on the authority of Salih bin Kaysan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir:
m: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse on the pulpit, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Usama bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Salih bin Kaysan, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of his brother,
m: Muhammad bin Ubaidah, on the authority of his brother Abdullah bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement:
h
And prepare against them whatever you are able of power
, beware, power is archery.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Shu’bah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And prepare against them whatever you are able of power
, he said: fortresses, and of steeds of war, he said: females.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Damrah bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Raja’ bin Abi Salamah, who said:
m: A man met Mujahid in Mecca, and Mujahid had some saddles with him. Mujahid said: This is from strength! And Mujahid was preparing for battle.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And prepare against them whatever you are able of power

, of weapons. As for his saying: You will terrorize the enemy of God and your enemy with it. Ibn Wakee' said: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Mughirah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: With it you terrify the enemy of God and your enemy, he said: With it you disgrace the enemy of God and your enemy.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Uthman, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah and Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And with it you terrify the enemy of God and your enemy, you humiliate with it Surat al-Anfal 8:60
h
And prepare against them whatever you are able of power
and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of God and your enemy
h
and others besides them whom you do not know

but God knows them. And whatever you spend in the cause of God will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged. the enemy of God and your enemy. And this is how he used to read it: (You humiliate).

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Abdul Aziz told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Mughira,
m: and Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: You will be terrified by it, meaning you will be disgraced by it.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same. It is said: I terrified the enemy, and I terrified him, so I terrify him and I terrify him, terrorizing and intimidating, which is fear and terror. And from it is the saying of Tufail al-Ghanawi: Woe to you, O mother of the living, you have driven the Banu Kalb into their throats in the morning of terror and fear.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And others besides them whom you do not know
, but God knows them.
The people of interpretation differed regarding these others. Who are they, and what are they?
Some of them said: They are Banu Qurayza.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hussein,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And others besides them, meaning: from Banu Qurayza.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
