m: And others besides them, he said: Qurayza.

x: Others said: From Persia.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And others besides them whom you do not know
, but God knows them. These are the people of Persia.

x: Others said: They are every enemy of the Muslims, except those whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered to be dispersed from behind them. They said: They are the hypocrites.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God: But if you overtake them in war, disperse with them those behind them, he said: Make them afraid of them, because of what you do to these people. And he recited: “
h
And others besides them whom you do not know
. God knows them.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And others besides them whom you do not know
, but God knows them, he said: These are the hypocrites, you do not know them because they are with you, they say: There is no god but God, and they fight with you.

x: Others said: They are a people of jinn.

The correct thing to say about this is that God commanded the believers to prepare for jihad and the tools of war and what would strengthen them to fight the enemy and their enemy from the polytheists, from weapons and archery and other things, and tethering horses. There is no reason to say: He meant by strength a meaning other than one of the meanings of strength, and God has made the command general.
The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made it clear that this was meant specifically by his saying: Behold, strength is archery?

Even though the report came with that, there is nothing in the report that indicates that it is intended to mean throwing specifically, without the other meanings of power over them, because throwing is one of the meanings of power, because it was only said in al-Naba 78:Behold, power is throwing, and it did not say: without anything else. And from power also is the sword, the spear, the javelin, and everything that was an aid in fighting the polytheists, such as the aid of throwing or more effective than throwing at them and in harming them. This is despite the weakness of the chain of transmission of the report on that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for his statement:
h
And others besides them whom you do not know

, the statement of those who said that it refers to the jinn is closer and more likely to be correct, because God, the Most High, has included in His statement: And of the tethering of horses by which you terrify the enemy of God and your enemy, the command to associate with good in order to terrify every enemy of God and of the believers whom they know. There is no doubt that the believers were aware of the enmity of Qurayzah and Persia towards them, because they knew that they were polytheists and that they were at war with them.
There is no meaning in saying, while they knew that they were enemies to them:
h
And others besides them whom you do not know

, but the meaning of that, God willing, is: You terrify, O believers, by your association with horses, the enemy of God and your enemies from the children of Adam whose enmity towards you you know, because of their disbelief in God and His Messenger, and you terrify with that another race other than the children of Adam, whose locations and conditions you do not know, God knows them but you do not, because the children of Adam do not see them. It was said: The neighing of horses terrifies the jinn, and that the jinn do not come near a house in which there is a horse.
The believers knew what the hypocrites were doing, so why do you deny that I meant the hypocrites?

The hypocrites were not terrified by the horses or weapons of the Muslims, but what terrified them was that the Muslims would reveal their secrets of disbelief, which they used to hide. The believers were ordered to prepare the force to terrify the enemy. As for the one who was not terrified by that, he is not included in the meaning of the one for whom the believers were ordered to prepare that.

It was said: You do not know them, so it was sufficient for knowledge with one accusative in this place, because what was meant was: You do not know them, as the poet said: God knows me and Habban and we will both meet him The statement in the interpretation of His saying:
h
And whatever you spend in the way of God will be fully repaid to you
, and you will not be wronged.

God Almighty says: Whatever you spend, O believers, in purchasing war equipment such as weapons, spears, hooves, or other expenses in the struggle against the polytheist enemies of God, God will replace it for you in this world, and He will give you your rewards for that with Him until He pays them to you on the Day of Resurrection, and you will not be wronged. He says: Your Lord will do that to you, and He will not waste your rewards on Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: h
And whatever you spend in the way of God will be fully repaid to you
, and you will not be wronged, meaning: Your reward with God in the Hereafter will not be lost, and He will replace it in this world.

evidence.text: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, on the authority of Salih bin Kaysan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse on the pulpit, and he mentioned something similar.
And this is how he used to read it: (You humiliate).

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And if you fear treachery and betrayal from a people, then denounce them on equal terms and declare war on them. “
h
But if they incline to peace

, then incline to it.” And if they incline to making peace with you and refraining from war with you, either by entering Islam, or by paying the jizya, or by a truce, or something similar to that of the causes of peace and reconciliation, then incline to it. He says: So incline toward it and offer them whatever they incline toward and ask you for. It is said: (The man inclined towards such-and-such with inclination), and it is from Tamim and Qais, according to what was mentioned about them. You say: (Yajhnh), with a damma on the noon, and others say: (Yajhnh) with a kasra on the noon, and that is if he leans, and from it is the saying of Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan: Jawah has become certain that if the two armies meet, his tribe will be the first to prevail. (wings), habitats.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if they incline to peace
,” he said: to reconciliation, and it was abrogated by His statement:
h
Kill the polytheists wherever you find them
, (al-Tawbah 9:5).

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And if they incline to peace

,” meaning to make peace, then incline to it, he said: This was before Bara’ah, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would make peace treaties with people for a period of time, so either they would submit or he would fight them. Then that was abrogated later in Bara’ah, so He said:
h
Kill the polytheists wherever you find them

, and He said: Fight the polytheists altogether, (al-Tawbah 9:36), and He abandoned the treaty with everyone with whom a treaty had been made, and He ordered him to fight them until they said, There is no god but God, and submitted, and that nothing would be accepted from them except that. And every treaty that was in this surah and in others, and every peace treaty by which the Muslims reconcile with the polytheists and make peace with them, then Bara’ah came to abrogate that, so He ordered fighting them in every case until they said, There is no god but God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Hussein, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said:
m: h
And if they incline to peace
, then incline to it,” was abrogated by the verse in (Al-Bara’ah), in which He says: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, to His saying: while they are subdued (al-Tawbah 9:29).

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And if they incline to peace
, then incline to it,” he says: And if they want peace, then reject it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And if they incline to peace
, then incline to it,” meaning: If they invite you to peace - to Islam - then make peace with them on it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “
h
And if they incline to peace
, then incline to it,” he said: So make peace with them. He said: And this was abrogated by jihad.

x: As for what he said and those who said the same, that this verse was abrogated, this is a statement for which there is no evidence from the Book, the Sunnah, or the innate nature of reason. We have demonstrated in more than one place in this book and others that the abrogating verse can only be that which negates the ruling of the abrogated verse in every respect. As for that which is contrary to that, it cannot be abrogating. And God’s statement in Bara’ah:
h
Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9
:5) does not negate the ruling of His statement: “
h
But if they incline to peace
, then incline to it,” because His statement: “
h
But if they incline to peace

,” only meant Banu Qurayzah, who were Jews and People of the Book. God, may He be glorified, permitted the believers to make peace with the People of the Book and to forsake war on them in exchange for taking the jizyah from them.
As for his saying:
h
Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9

:5), what he meant by it was the polytheists of the Arabs who worshipped idols, from whom it is not permissible to accept the jizya. So neither of the two verses negates the ruling of the other, rather each one of them is decisive in what it was revealed about.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And if they incline to peace
,” he said: Qurayza. As for his saying:
h
And put your trust in God
, he says: O Muhammad, entrust your matter to God, and be content with Him, trusting in Him that He will suffice you, like the one who:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And trust in God, God is sufficient for you. And His saying: He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, means by that: God, in whom you rely, is All-Hearing, of what you and those with whom you make peace and leave war, from the enemies of God and your enemies, say when you make peace between you and Him, and what each party of you stipulates for the other of conditions, All-Knowing, of what each party of you conceals for the other party of fulfilling what he has contracted with, and of what is concealed from you in his heart, and what is concealed from his companion.

x: God Almighty says: And if, O Muhammad, these people whom I have commanded you to throw aside all hostility to, if you fear treachery from them, and to make peace with them if they incline to peace, deceive you and plot against you, then sufficient for you is God, meaning: God will suffice you against them and will suffice you against their deception of you, because He is responsible for making your religion prevail over all religions, and He will make His word supreme and the word of His enemies the lowest, He is the One who supported you with His victory, meaning: God who strengthened you with His victory over His enemies, and with the believers, meaning: with the helpers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And if they intend to deceive you, he said: Qurayza.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is God, he is behind that.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: It is He who supported you with His victory, he said: with the Ansar.

x: By His saying:
h
And He united their hearts

, He meant that He united the hearts of the believers from the Aws and Khazraj, after their division and dispersion, upon His true religion, and made them all together after they had been scattered, and brothers after they had been enemies. And His statement:
h
If you spent all that is on the earth

, you could not bring their hearts together, the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you spent, O Muhammad, all that is on the earth of gold, silver and goods, you could not bring their hearts together with your tricks, but God brought them together on guidance, so they came together and gathered, as a strengthening from God for you, support from Him and assistance against your enemy. The Almighty says: The One who did that and caused it for you until they became your helpers and supporters and one hand against whoever seeks to harm you, is the One who, if an enemy seeks to harm you, He will suffice you against his plot and grant you victory over him.
So go ahead with His command and put your trust in Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And He brought their hearts together, he said: These are the Ansar, He brought their hearts together after the war that had been between them.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Bashir ibn Thabit,
m: a man from the Ansar, that he said about this verse: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together, meaning: the Ansar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And He brought their hearts together, on the guidance with which He sent you to them, “If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together. But God brought them together,” on His religion upon which He united them, meaning the Aws and the Khazraj.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Khawzi, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Abi Mughis, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: If two Muslims meet and shake hands, they will be forgiven. He said, I said to Mujahid: Will they be forgiven for shaking hands? Mujahid said: Haven’t you heard him say: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together? Al-Walid said to Mujahid: You know better than me.

c: Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told us, he said, Al-Walid told me, on the authority of Abu Amr, he said, Abdah bin Abi Lubabah told me, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: and I met him and he took my hand and said: When two people who love each other for the sake of God see each other, and one of them takes the hand of the other and smiles at him, their sins fall away like the leaves of a tree. Abdah said: So I said to him: This is easy! He said: Do not say that, for God says: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together! Abdah said: Then I knew that he was more knowledgeable than me.

c: Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, Abdullah bin Musa told us, Fadil bin Ghazwan told us:
m: I came to Abu Ishaq and greeted him and said: Do you know me? Fadil said: Yes! If it were not for shyness, I would have kissed you.

c: Abu Al-Ahwas told me, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: This verse was revealed about those who love one another for the sake of God: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Umair ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: We used to say that the first thing to be removed from people - or he said: from people - is familiarity.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ayoub bin Suwaid told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, he said, Abda bin Abi Lubaba told me, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Al-Walid.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said,
m: Abu Usamah, Ibn Numayr, and Hafs ibn Ghayath told us, on the authority of Fadil ibn Ghazwan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, he said: I heard Abdullah say: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together the verse, he said: They are those who love each other for the sake of God. And His statement:
h
He is Exalted in Might and Wise

, means: God, who united the hearts of the Aws and Khazraj after their word had been scattered and they had become hostile, and made them your supporters, is Exalted in Might. Nothing can defeat Him, and no one can reverse His judgment, but He executes His judgment on His creation. He says: So rely on Him, and trust in Him. He is Wise in the management of His creation.

x: God Almighty says to the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet,
h
God is sufficient for you

, and God is sufficient for those believers who follow you. God Almighty says to them: Confront your enemy, for God will suffice you against them, and do not be frightened by their great number and your small number, for God will support you with His victory. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil bin Ismail told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Shawdhab Abu Muadh, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers, he said:
h
God is sufficient for you
, and God is sufficient for those who follow you among the believers.

c: Ahmad bin Othman bin Hakim Al-Awdi told me, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Shawdhab, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you of the believers, he said:
h
God is sufficient for you
, and He is sufficient for those with you.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Shawdhab, on the authority of Amer,
m: in a similar manner, except that he said:
h
God is sufficient for you
, and He is sufficient for those who testified with you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Ibn Zayd,
m: regarding his statement: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers, he said: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers, for sufficient for you and for them is God. So (man) in his statement: and whoever follows you from the believers, according to this interpretation that we mentioned from Al-Sha’bi, is in the accusative case, in apposition to the meaning of (kaf) in his statement:
h
God is sufficient for you
, not according to its wording, because it is in the accusative case apparently, and in the accusative case in meaning. Because the meaning of the statement is:
h
God is sufficient for you
, and He is sufficient for whoever follows you from the believers. Some Arabists have said about min that it is in the nominative case in apposition to the name God, as if he said:
h
God is sufficient for you
and those believers who follow you in the jihad against the enemy, not those who sit back from you. He cited as evidence for the correctness of his statement his saying:
h
He urged the believers to fight

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet, urge the believers to fight, urging your followers and those who believe in what you have brought them of the truth, to fight those of the polytheists who have turned away and turned away from the truth, If there are twenty of you, "patient, when meeting the enemy, and who seek reward for themselves and stand firm against their enemy, they will overcome two hundred, of their enemy and subdue them, and if there are a hundred of you, then they will overcome, of them a thousand, because they are a people who do not understand," He says: Because the polytheists are a people who fight without hope of reward, nor seeking reward or seeking reward, because they do not understand that God requires of those who fight seeking reward and seeking God's promise at the appointed time, what He promised to the mujahideen in His cause, so they do not stand firm if they are truthful in the encounter, for fear that they will fight and their world will be lost.
Then the Almighty made things easier for the believers, since He knew their weakness, and said to them:
h
Now God has lightened your burden
h
and He knows that there is weakness in you

, meaning that there is weakness in one of them when facing ten of their enemy. So if there are a hundred of you, patient, when facing them to stand firm for them, they will overcome two hundred of them. And if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand of them, by God’s permission, meaning by God’s leaving them alone for their defeat and His assistance to them.
h
And God is with the patient

, against their enemy and the enemy of God, seeking reward in his patience and seeking a great reward from his Lord, through His assistance to him and victory over him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Muhibb told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If there are twenty among you
, patient, they will overcome two hundred, he said: One was for ten, then it was made two, and he should not flee from them.

c: Saeed bin Yahya told us, my father told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: He imposed on the Muslims ten men per man from the infidels, and said:
h
If there are twenty among you
, patient, they will overcome two hundred, so he made that easier for them, and made two men per man. Ibn Abbas said: So I do not like people to know that this was made easier for them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, Abdullah ibn Abi Nujayh al-Makki told me, on the authority of Ata ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said:
m: When this verse was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, and they thought it too great that twenty could fight two hundred, and one hundred thousand, so God made it easier for them. Then He abrogated it with the other verse, saying: “
h
Now God has lightened your burden
h
and He knows that there is weakness in you

. So if there are a hundred of you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand.” He said: And if they were half of their enemy, it was not appropriate for them to flee from them. But if they were less than that, it was not obligatory for them to fight, and it was permissible for them to avoid them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If there are twenty among you
, patient, they will overcome two hundred, he said: Every Muslim man had ten, and he should not flee from them. And they were like that until God revealed: “
h
Now God has lightened your burden
h
and He knows that there is weakness in you

. So if there are a hundred among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred,” so He mobilized for every Muslim man two men from the polytheists, thus abrogating the first order, and He said again in His statement:
h
If there are twenty among you

, patient, they will overcome two hundred, so God commanded the man from the believers to fight ten of the infidels, and that was difficult for the believers, and God had mercy on them, so He said: “If there are a hundred among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, and if there are a thousand among you, they will overcome two thousand by God’s permission.
h
And God is with the patient
,” so God commanded the man from the believers to fight two men from the infidels.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: O Prophet, urge the believers to fight, until his statement:
h
because they are a people who do not understand

, that is, he had made it obligatory for every Muslim man to have ten of the enemy to tempt them - meaning to tempt them - with that, so that they would prepare themselves for the invasion, and that God would support them against the enemy. It was not something that God had determined for them or made obligatory, but it was an incitement and a commandment that God commanded His Prophet to do. Then He made it easier for them and said:
h
Now God has lightened your burden

and knows that there is weakness in you, so He made it obligatory for every man to have two men after that, as a relief, so that the believers would know that God is merciful to them, so they put their trust in God and were patient and truthful. If it had been obligatory for them, they would have disbelieved. So every Muslim man refrained from fighting whoever he encountered from the disbelievers if they were more than them and did not fight them. So do not be deceived by the words of men! For I have heard men say: It is not proper for a Muslim man to fight until there are two men on every man, and until there are four on every two men, and then according to that calculation. And they claimed that they would disobey God if they fought until they reached that number, and that there is no blame on them if they do not fight until they reach the number of two men on every man, and four on every two men, and God said: “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And God is Kind to His servants.” (al-Baqarah 2:207) And God said: “So fight in the cause of God. You are not charged except with yourself. And urge the believers.”
r
(An-Nisa’: 84)
This is the urge that God revealed to them in Al-Anfal. So do not be helpless, so fight, for there have fallen among my people as God wills them to be.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Hussain, on the authority of Zaid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan, they said,
m: he said in Surat al-Anfal 8:“
h
If there are twenty among you
, patient, they will overcome two hundred.
h
And if there are a hundred among you
, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve
h
because they are a people who do not understand
.” Then he abrogated and said:
h
Now God has lightened your burden
h
and He knows that there is weakness in you
, until His saying:
h
And God is with the patient

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If there are twenty among you
, patient, he said: One Muslim and ten polytheists. Then He made it easier for them, and made it obligatory for them that no man should flee from two men.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If there are twenty among you
, patient, to his statement:
h
And if there are a hundred among you

, he said: This is for the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr. He made it obligatory for each one of them to fight ten of the infidels, and they were upset by that, so he made it obligatory for each man to fight two men, as a relief from God.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibrahim bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar and Abu Ma’bad, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: A man was only commanded to be patient with himself for ten, and ten for one hundred, because the Muslims were few. But when the Muslims became many, God made it easier for them. So a man was commanded to be patient with two men, and ten for twenty, and one hundred for two hundred.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh:
m: h
If there are twenty among you

, patient, they will overcome two hundred, he said: It was obligatory upon them if twenty met two hundred that they should not flee, because if they did not flee they would be defeated. Then God made it easier for them and said: If there are a hundred among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, and if there are a thousand among you, they will overcome two thousand, so He said: It is not appropriate for a thousand to flee from two thousand, because if they are patient with them, they will overcome them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Now God has lightened your burden
h
and He knows that there is weakness in you

. So if there are a hundred of you, patient, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand,” God made every man responsible for two men, after there had been ten for every man. This hadith is on the authority of Ibn Abbas.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, on the authority of Az-Zubayr bin Al-Kharit, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: It was obligatory upon the believers that each one of them should fight ten of the polytheists, as God says: “
h
If there are twenty among you
, patient, they will overcome two hundred.
h
And if there are a hundred among you

, they will overcome a thousand.” This was difficult for them, so God revealed the alleviation, and made it obligatory upon each man to fight two men, as God says: If there are a hundred among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred. So God made it easy for them, and they were reduced from victory by that amount.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
If there are twenty among you

, patient, they will overcome two hundred, he said: They will fight two hundred, but they were weaker than that, so God abrogated it for them, and made it lighter and said: If there are one hundred among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, so He made the first time one man equal to ten, then He made the man equal to two.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If there are twenty among you

, patient, they will overcome two hundred, he said: It was obligatory upon them if twenty met two hundred that they should not flee, because if they did not flee they would be defeated. Then God made it easier for them and said: “If there are a hundred among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are a thousand among you, they will overcome two thousand by permission of God,” so He says: It is not appropriate for a thousand to flee from two thousand, because if they are patient with them, they will overcome them.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, he said:
m: This was Surat al-Anfal 8:66
h
Now God has lightened your burden
h
and He knows that there is weakness in you
. So if there are a hundred of you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand, by God's permission.
h
And God is with the patient
. obligatory: that not one out of ten should flee. And he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Ata’, something similar. As for his saying:
h
Because they are a people who do not understand
, we have explained its interpretation. Ibn Ishaq used to say about this:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: They are a people who do not understand, meaning: they do not fight with good intentions or right, and they do not know good or evil.

x: This verse - I mean His statement:
h
If there are twenty among you
, patient, they will overcome two hundred - even if it is a statement, its meaning is a command. This is indicated by His statement:
h
Now God has lightened your burden

, for lightening was only after the burden was made heavy. If the ten of them standing firm against the one hundred of their enemy had not been obligatory upon them before the lightening, but rather it was recommended, there would have been no justification for lightening, because lightening is only a concession for one of the Muslims not to stand firm against the ten of the enemy. If the severity had not preceded it, there would have been no justification for lightening, since the understanding of lightening was only after the severity. Since that is the case, it is known that the ruling of His statement:
h
Now God has lightened your burden
h
and He knows that there is weakness in you
, abrogates the ruling of His statement: “
h
If there are twenty among you
, patient, they will overcome two hundred.

And if there are one hundred among you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve.” We have explained in our book, The Book of Explanation of the Principles of Rulings, that every piece of report from God in which He promises a servant a reward and recompense for an action, and a punishment and torment for leaving it, even if it does not appear to be an order, is in the meaning of an order, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
And He knows that there is weakness in you

Some of the Medinans and some of the Basrans read it as (and he knew that there was weakness among you), with a damma on the (Ḍād) throughout the Qur’an, and a tanween on the (weakness), as a source from (the man became weak, weakness). The majority of the Kufians read it as: And he knew that there was weakness among you, with the letter Ḍād open, also as a source of weakness.
Some of the Medinans read it as weak, assuming that fa’alaa is the plural of weak as weak, just as shareek is pluralized as shareek, and ar-Raheem is pluralized as rahima’.

The most correct of the readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads it: And He knows that there is weakness among you, and weakness, with the opening of the letter Ḍād or its closing, because they are the two well-known readings, and they are two well-known dialects in the speech of the Arabs, and they are eloquent with one meaning, so whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct. As for the reading of the one who reads it: weak ones, it is an anomalous reading of the reading, even if it has a correct way out, so I do not like the reader to read it with it.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And He knows that there is weakness in you.

Some of the Medinans and some of the Basrans read it as (and he knew that there was weakness among you), with a damma on the (Ḍād) throughout the Qur’an, and a tanween on the (weakness), as a source from (the man became weak, weakness).
The majority of the Kufians read it as: And he knew that there was weakness among you, with the letter Ḍād open, also as a source of weakness.
Some of the Medinans read it as weak, assuming that fa’alaa is the plural of weak as weak, just as shareek is pluralized as shareek, and ar-Raheem is pluralized as rahima’.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads it: And He knows that there is weakness among you, and weakness, with the opening of the letter Ḍād or its closing, because they are the two well-known readings, and they are two well-known dialects in the speech of the Arabs, and they are eloquent with one meaning, so whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct.
As for the reading of the one who reads it: weak ones, it is an anomalous reading of the reading, even if it has a correct way out, so I do not like the reader to read it with it.

x: God Almighty says: It is not for a prophet to detain an unbeliever who is in his power and who is in his hand from among the idol worshippers for ransom or as a favor. And (captivity) in the speech of the Arabs means imprisonment. It is said from it: (captive), meaning: imprisoned. And it is heard from them: (May God make him imprisoned). God Almighty said this to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform him that killing the polytheists whom he, may God bless him and grant him peace, had taken prisoner on the day of Badr and then ransomed them was more correct than taking ransom from them and releasing them. And his saying: Until he makes a great slaughter in the land, means: until he exaggerates in killing the polytheists in it, and subdues them by force and coercion. It is said: So-and-so went to extremes in this matter, if he exaggerated in it.

It was also said: I killed him with knowledge, meaning: I killed him with knowledge. You want, he says to the believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: You want, O believers, the worldly goods, by capturing the polytheists, which is what a person is offered of wealth and goods. He says: You want, by taking ransom from the polytheists, the worldly goods and taste. And God wants the Hereafter, he says: And God wants for you the adornment of the Hereafter and what He has prepared for the believers and the people of His allegiance in His gardens, by killing them and causing you great destruction on earth. He says to them: So seek what God wants for you and work for Him, not what your own desires call you to of desiring the world and its causes. And God is Exalted in Might, he says: If you want the Hereafter, your enemy will not overcome you, because God is Exalted in Might and cannot be defeated, and He is Wise in His management of the affairs of His creation.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a slaughter in the land

, and that was on the day of Badr, and the Muslims at that time were few. Then when they became numerous and their power became strong, God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed after this regarding the captives: Then either a favor afterward or ransom [them],
r
(Muhammad 47:4)

, so God gave the Prophet and the believers the choice in the matter of the captives. If they wanted to, they could kill them, if they wanted to, they could enslave them, and if they wanted, they could ransom them.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a slaughter on the land

. You desire the goods of this world,” the verse, he said: The companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted ransom on the day of Badr, so they ransomed them with four thousand, four thousand. By my life, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not inflict a slaughter on that day! It was the first battle he fought against the polytheists.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us,
m: on the

x: God Almighty says to the people of Badr who took spoils and ransom from the captives:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

, meaning: Had it not been for a decree from God that preceded you from the people of Badr in the Preserved Tablet, that God had made the spoils available to you, and that God had decreed among what He had decreed that He would not lead a people astray after He had guided them until He had made clear to them what they should avoid, and that He would not punish anyone who had witnessed the scene that you witnessed at Badr with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, supporting the religion of God, you would have been afflicted by God, for taking the spoils and ransom, with a great punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Adi told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

, the verse, he said: God had fed this nation the spoils, and they had taken ransom from the prisoners of Badr before they were commanded to do so. He said: God rebuked them for that, then God permitted it.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzayʿ told us, he said, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

, the verse, and that was on the day of Badr, and the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the spoils and prisoners before they were commanded to do so, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, had written in the Mother of the Book: The spoils and the prisoners are lawful for Muhammad and his nation, and He had not made it lawful for a nation before them, and they took the spoils and took the prisoners before it was revealed to them about that, God said:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, meaning in the first book, that the spoils and prisoners are lawful for you, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God the verse

, and the spoils were before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, among the nations, if they acquired spoils they would make them an offering, and God forbade them from eating from it, little or much. He forbade that to every prophet and his nation, so they would not eat from it, nor would they steal from it, nor would they take from it, little or much, except that God would punish them for it. And God had forbidden it to them with a strict prohibition, so He did not make it permissible for any prophet except Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God had already decreed that the spoils were lawful for him and his nation, so that is what He said on the day of Badr, regarding taking ransom from the prisoners:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, he said: God was going to give this nation the spoils, and they did what they did before the spoils were permissible.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Al-A’mash said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, he said: God had previously made the spoils permissible for them.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila told us, on the authority of Bashir bin Maimun, he said:
m: I heard Saeed narrating, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: He recited this verse:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took. He said: Meaning: Had it not been foreordained in my knowledge that I would make the spoils permissible, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took of the captives.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, and Abu Muawiyah told us
m: something similar, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Spoils of war were not made lawful for any of the black-headed people before you. Fire used to come down from the sky and consume them, until the day of Badr, and the people fell into spoils of war, so God revealed: ‘
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
that would have touched you,’ until he reached, ‘lawful and good.’”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. He said: When the day of Badr came, the people rushed to the spoils.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Suwar, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, who said:
m: “The Muslims took seventy polytheists prisoner and killed seventy. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Choose between taking ransom from them and strengthening yourself against your enemy, and if you accept it, seventy of you will be killed, or you will kill them! They said: Rather, we will take ransom from them, and seventy of them were killed. Ubaydah said: They sought both options.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ubaidah, he said:
m: The ransom for the prisoners of Badr was one hundred ounces, and an ounce was forty dirhams, and six dinars.

c: Abu Kuraib and Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us, they said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah,
m: “He said regarding the prisoners of Badr: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you wish, you may kill them, and if you wish, you may ransom them and some of you may be martyred according to their number! They said: Yes, we will take the ransom and enjoy it, and some of us may be martyred according to their number.”

c: Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Tusi told me, he said: Abd al-Samad bin Abd al-Warith told us, he said: Hammam bin Yahya told us, he said: Ata bin al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, he said:
m: Umar, may God have mercy on him, ordered the killing of the prisoners, so God revealed:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

, that spoils of war were forbidden to every prophet and his nation, and whenever they gained spoils of war, they would make the spoils of war an offering to God that would be consumed by the fire. And it was previously in the decree and knowledge of God that spoils of war would be made lawful for this nation, and they would eat them in their stomachs.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding the statement of God: Had Surat al-Anfal 8:68
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took. it not been for a previous decree from God, you would have been afflicted, he said: God knew that the spoils would be permissible for them, so He said:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, that He had made the spoils permissible for you, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: If it were not for a previous decree from God for the people of Badr, that He would not punish them, a great punishment would have befallen them.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, he said: for the people of Badr, from happiness.

c: Ibn Kayʿ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqaʿ, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, for the people of Badr, their scene.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, he said: A previous decree from God was good for the people of Badr.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took, God had previously bestowed upon them good, and He had made the spoils permissible for them.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abdul Warith bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Amr bin Ubaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, he said: preceded, that no one from the people of Badr would be punished.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, for the people of Badr and their witnessing it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told me, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took, he afflicted you for what you took of the spoils on the day of Badr before I made it lawful for you. So he said: It was previously from God that He forgave them and had mercy on them. It was previously that He would not punish the believers, because He does not punish His Messenger and those who believed in him and migrated with him and supported him.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, that no one would be held accountable for an action he did out of ignorance, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his saying:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God
, for the people of Badr and their witnessing it, he said: A decree that preceded, because of His saying:
h
And God would not lead a people astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid (al-Tawbah 9

:115), that preceded, and it preceded that He would not hold people accountable for doing something out of ignorance, for what you have taken, Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: for what you have taken, of what you have taken as captives. Then He said after that: So eat of what you have taken as spoils.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: He rebuked him regarding the prisoners and taking the spoils, and no prophet before him had eaten spoils from his enemy. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad, who said:

c: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAli ibn Abi Talib narrated to me:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been aided by terror, and the earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me, and I have been given comprehensive words, and spoils of war have been made lawful for me, which were not made lawful for any prophet before me, and I have been given intercession, five things that were not given to any prophet before me.” Muhammad said: Then he said: It is not for a prophet, meaning before you, to have captives, until His saying:
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

, you would have been afflicted with a great punishment for what you took, meaning the captives and spoils, a great punishment, meaning: Had it not been decreed from me that I would not punish except after forbidding you, and I had not forbidden you, I would have punished you for what you did. Then He made it lawful for him and for them as mercy, favor, and a reward from the Most Gracious, Most Merciful.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is what we have explained before. That is because his statement,
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

, is a general report that is not limited to one meaning rather than another. All of these meanings that I have mentioned about those I have mentioned are what has been mentioned in the Book of God that this nation will not be held accountable for anything of them, and that is: what they did out of ignorance, and the permissibility of the spoils, and forgiveness for the people of Badr, and all of that which was written for them. Since that is the case, there is no reason to single out one meaning rather than another, and God has made the report general with all of that, without any indication that necessitates the correctness of the statement regarding it specifically.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: “There was no believer among those who were aided who did not love the spoils, except for Umar ibn al-Khattab. He would not meet a prisoner without striking his neck, and he said: O Messenger of God, what do we have to do with the spoils? We are a people who fight in the religion of God until God is worshipped! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If we were punished for this matter, O Umar, no one would be saved except you! God said: Do not return to making things permissible before I make them permissible for you.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq said:
m: “When the verse: ‘
h
Had it not been for a previous decree from God

,’ was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a punishment were to descend from the sky, none would be saved from it except Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, because he said: O Prophet of God, killing in great numbers is more beloved to me than keeping men alive.”

evidence.text: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila told us, on the authority of Bashir bin Maimun, he said: I heard Saeed narrating, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: He recited this verse: Had it not been for a previous decree from God, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took.

x: God Almighty says to the believers from the people of Badr: So eat, O believers, of what you have taken as spoils, of the wealth of the polytheists, lawful, by His making it lawful for you, good and fear God, meaning: And fear God lest you return, that you do something in your religion after this before it was entrusted to you, as you did in taking ransom and eating the spoils, and you took them before it was lawful for you, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. This is from the deferred meaning of the presentation, and the interpretation of the words: So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good, “Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful,” And fear God. What he means by his saying: God is Forgiving of the sins of the faithful among His servants, Merciful towards them, that He will punish them after they repent from them.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet, say to those in your hands and in the hands of your companions from the prisoners of the polytheists from whom He took ransom what He took: If God knows in your hearts any good, meaning: If God knows in your hearts any Islam, He will give you better than what was taken from you, of ransom, and forgive you, meaning: He will pardon you for the punishment of your crime that you committed by fighting the Prophet of God and his companions and your disbelief in God, and God is Forgiving, of the sins of His servants if they repent, Merciful, to them, that He will not punish them for them after their repentance. It was mentioned that Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib used to say: This verse was revealed about me.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Abbas said:
m: “It was revealed about me: ‘It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has made slaughter in the land. ’ So I informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of my conversion to Islam, and I asked him to account for the twenty ounces that he had taken from me, but he refused, so God replaced them with twenty slaves, all of them merchants, and my money was in his hands.” And: This hadith was narrated to us by Humayd, who said:

c: Salamah narrated to us,
m: who said: Muhammad narrated to me, Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Ri’ab, who said: Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib used to say: By God, it was revealed about me, when I mentioned my Islam to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Wakee’.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Say to those of the captives who are in your hands

, the verse, he said: It was mentioned to us that when the wealth of Bahrain, eighty thousand, was presented to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he had performed ablution for the noon prayer, but he did not give to anyone who complained that day, nor did he deprive anyone who asked, and he did not pray that day until he distributed it, and he ordered Al-Abbas to take from it and scoop it up, so he took. He said: Al-Abbas used to say: This is better than what was taken from us, and I hope for forgiveness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: O Prophet, say to those who are in your hands of captives, the verse. Al-Abbas had been taken prisoner on the day of Badr, so he ransomed himself with forty ounces of gold. Al-Abbas said when this verse was revealed: God has given me two qualities, and I would not like to have the world for them: I was taken prisoner on the day of Badr, so I ransomed myself with forty ounces, so He gave me forty slaves, and I hope for the forgiveness that God has promised us.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement: O Prophet, say to those who are in your hands of captives, until his statement:
h
And God is Forgiving and Merciful

, meaning by that: those who were taken captive on the day of Badr. He says: If you act in obedience to Me and give sincere advice to My Messenger, I will give you better than what was taken from you, and I will forgive you.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: O Prophet,
h
say to those of the captives who are in your hands

, meaning Abbas and his companions. He said: They said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We believe in what you have brought, and we bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. We will advise you regarding our people. Then this verse was revealed: If God knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you, faith and belief, He will replace for you better than what was afflicted from you, and forgive you, the polytheism that you were upon. He said: Al-Abbas used to say: I would not like this verse not to be revealed about us, and that I should have the world. He said: He will give you better than what was taken from you, so He gave me better than what was taken from me a hundred times, and He Surat al-Anfal 8:70 O Prophet, say to those captives in your hands, "If God knows any good in your hearts, He will give you something better than what was taken from you and forgive you. And God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful." said: He will forgive you, and I hope that He has forgiven me.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about the verse: O Prophet, say to those who are in your hands of the captives, meaning Al-Abbas and his companions, who were taken captive on the day of Badr. God says: If you act in obedience to Me and advise Me and My Messenger, I will give you better than what was taken from you and forgive you. Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib used to say: God has given us two qualities, nothing is better than them: twenty slaves. As for the second, we are in the promise of the Truthful One awaiting forgiveness from God, the Exalted.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet: And if these captives in your hands intend to betray you, meaning to betray you, deceive you, and trick you, by showing you in words that are contrary to what is in their hearts, they have already betrayed God before, meaning: they disobeyed God’s command before the Battle of Badr, and He enabled the believers to defeat them at Badr, and God is Knowing, of what they say with their tongues and conceal in their hearts, Wise, in their management and the management of the affairs of His creation other than them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And if they intend to betray you

, meaning Abbas and his companions in their saying: (We believe in what you have brought, and we bear witness that you are the Messenger of God, we will advise you against our people), he says: If their saying was betrayal, they betrayed God before, so He gave you power over them, he says: They disbelieved and fought you, so God gave you power over them.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if they intend to betray you

, the verse, he said: It was mentioned to us that “a man wrote for the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then deliberately became a hypocrite, and joined the polytheists in Mecca, then said: (Muhammad only writes what you wish)! When a man from the Ansar heard that, he vowed that if God gave him power over him, he would strike him with the sword. So when the day of the conquest came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave security to the people except for Abdullah bin Saad bin Abi Sarh, Muqays bin Subaba, Ibn Khatal, and a woman who used to pray against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, every morning. Then Uthman bin Abi Sarh came, and he was his foster brother - or: his foster brother - and said: O Messenger of God, this is so-and-so who has come repentant and regretful! So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away. When the Ansari heard about him, he came, slung over his sword, and surrounded him, and kept looking at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to nod to him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came forward. He took his hand and pledged allegiance to him. He said: By God, I blamed you for it so that you would fulfill your vow! He said: O Prophet of God, I have given you my allegiance, so why didn’t you nod to me? He said: It is not appropriate for a prophet to nod.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And if they intend to betray you
, they have already betrayed God before, and He gave them power over you,” meaning: They disbelieved in God and broke His covenant, so He gave them power over you at Badr.

x: God Almighty says: Those who believed in God and His Messenger. And they emigrated, meaning they emigrated from their people, clan, and homes, meaning they left them and went out from them, and their people and clan abandoned them, and strove in the cause of God, meaning they went to great lengths to exhaust themselves and their souls in war against the enemies of God from the infidels, in the cause of God, meaning in the religion of God which He made a path to His mercy and salvation from His punishment, and those who gave shelter and aided, meaning: those who gave shelter to the Messenger of God and the emigrants with him, meaning: they made for them a shelter to which they would take refuge, which is the abode and dwelling, meaning: they housed them, and made for them dwellings from their homes when their people expelled them from their homes, and aided, meaning: and aided them against their enemies and the enemies of God from the polytheists, those are allies of one another, meaning: these two groups, meaning the emigrants and the helpers, some of them are supporters of others, and helpers against those other than them from the polytheists, and their hands are one against those who disbelieve in God, and some of them are brothers to others without…” Their infidel relatives.

It has been said: What is meant by that is that some of them are more deserving of the inheritance of others, and that God inherited some of them from others through migration and support, not through kinship and blood relations, and that God later abrogated that by saying: And those of kinship are more deserving of one another in the Book of God (al-Anfal 8:75) (al-Ahzab 33:6).
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And those who believed and emigrated and fought in the cause of God and those who gave shelter and aided - those are the believers
, truly, means: in inheritance, he made the inheritance for the emigrants and the helpers, not the relatives. God said: And those who believed and did not emigrate -
h
you have no share in their guardianship until they emigrate
, meaning: you have no share in their inheritance. And they used to do that until God revealed this verse:
h
And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God
(al-Anfal 8:75, al-Ahzab 33:6), in inheritance, so it abrogated the previous one, and the inheritance became for the relatives.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: Indeed,
h
those who believed and emigrated

and fought with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God, he says: There is no emigration after the conquest, rather it is martyrdom after that, and those who gave shelter and aided - those are allies of one another, until his statement: until they emigrate, and that is because the believers were in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in three ranks: among them is the believer and the emigrant who separated himself from his people in emigration, he went out to a people of believers in their homes, their property and their wealth, they gave shelter and aided, and they declared what the emigrants declared, and they brandished swords against those who lied and denied, so these two are believers, God made some of them allies of others, so they would inherit from one another, if the believing emigrant died, the Ansar inherited him by guardianship in religion. And the one who believed but did not emigrate would not inherit because he did not emigrate or support them, so God absolved the believing emigrants from their inheritance, which is the guardianship that God said: You have no right to their guardianship until they emigrate. And it was the right of the believers who gave shelter and support, if they sought their support in religion, to support them if they fought, unless they sought support against a people between whom and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) there was a covenant, in which case they would have no support against them, except against an enemy with whom there was no covenant. Then God revealed after that that He would join every relative with his relative from the believers who emigrated and those who believed but did not emigrate. So He made for every person among the believers a prescribed share by His saying: “
h
And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God
. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things” (al-Anfal 8:75) and by His saying: And the believing men and Surat al-Anfal 8:72 Indeed,
h
those who believed and emigrated
and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God, and those who gave shelter and aided - those are allies of one another.
h
And those who believed but did not emigrate - you have no guardianship over them at all until they emigrate

. But if they seek aid of you in religion, then it is your duty to aid them. Except for a people between whom and you there is a treaty. And God is Seeing of what you do. believing women are allies of one another (al-Tawbah 9:71).

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The three verses are the last of Al-Anfal, in which there is mention of what happened regarding the guardianship of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, between the Muslim immigrants and the Ansar in inheritance, then that was abrogated by the last of them: “
h
And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God
. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things” (al-Anfal 8:75).

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Kathir,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
those who believed and emigrated

and fought steadfastly, to His statement: He is Seeing of what you do, he said: We have been informed that it was in regard to inheritance, that the believers who emigrated and the believers who did not emigrate do not inherit from each other. He said: Then after that was revealed: “And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the decree of God. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things” (al-Anfal 8:75). So they inherited from each other and did not emigrate, Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: The last three verses of Al-Anfal mention what was between the Muslim emigrants and the Ansar in inheritance, then that was abrogated by the last: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the decree of God (al-Anfal 8:75 - al-Ahzab 33:6).

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And
h
those who believed and emigrated
and fought in the cause of God, and those who gave shelter and aided until His saying:
h
You have no right to be their guardian until they emigrate

, he said: The Muslims remained for a period of time inheriting from one another through emigration, and the Muslim Bedouin did not inherit anything from the emigrant, then that was abrogated after that, and God added: “
h
And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God

. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things” (al-Ahzab 33:6), meaning: from the people of polytheism, so the will was permitted, and they had no inheritance, and inheritance became by religions, and the Muslims inherit from one another from the emigrants and the believers, and the people of two religions do not inherit.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadheeh told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan, they said:
m: (Indeed,
h
those who believed and emigrated
and fought in the cause of God) until His saying:
h
You have no share in their guardianship until they emigrate
, the Bedouin did not inherit from the emigrant, nor did the emigrant inherit from him, so He abrogated it and said: “
h
And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God
. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things” (al-Anfal 8:75).

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: Indeed,
h
those who believed and emigrated

and fought in the cause of God and those who gave shelter and aided - those are allies of one another, in inheritance. And those who believed but did not emigrate, those are the Bedouins, you have no part in their guardianship, in inheritance. And if they seek help of you in religion, he says: that they are Muslims, then you are responsible for help except against a people between whom and you there is a treaty. “And those who disbelieve are allies of one another,” in inheritance. And those who believed afterward and emigrated and fought with you - those are from you, then the obligations and inheritance abrogated it. And those of kinship, those who inherited through emigration, are more worthy of one another in the Book of God, so the Bedouins and the emigrants inherited.

x: The statement in the interpretation of His saying: “
h
And those who believed but did not emigrate - you have no guardianship over them at all until they emigrate
And if they seek help of you in religion, then you must help them, except against a people between whom and you there is a treaty. And God is Seeing of what you do.”

What is meant by the words of God Almighty: And those who believed, those who believed in God and His Messenger, and did not emigrate, their people the infidels, and did not leave the land of infidelity for the land of Islam, what is [the matter] with you, O believers in God and His Messenger, the emigrants from their people the polytheists and the land of war, of their guardianship, meaning: of their support and their inheritance. I mentioned the statement of some who said: The meaning of guardianship here is inheritance, and I will mention, God willing, whoever I remember mentioned it later. From anything until they emigrate, their people and their homes, from the abode of war to the abode of Islam, and if they seek your aid in religion, meaning: if these who believed and did not emigrate seek your aid, in religion, meaning: because they are from the people of your religion against your enemies and their enemies from the polytheists, then upon you, O believers from the emigrants and the helpers, is aid, “unless” they seek your aid, against a people between whom and you there is a treaty, meaning: a covenant that some of you have trusted with one another that they will not fight him, and God is Seeing of what you do, meaning: God is Seeing of what you do in what He has commanded you and forbidden you from the guardianship of one another, O emigrants and helpers, and leaving the guardianship of those who have not emigrated and your aid to them when you seek their aid in religion, and other than that of the obligations of God that He has imposed upon you, is Seeing, He sees it and perceives it, so nothing of that or anything else is hidden from Him.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
You have no right to be their guardian until they emigrate

. He said: The Muslims used to inherit from one another through emigration, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, established brotherhood between them, so they used to inherit from one another through Islam and emigration. A man would convert to Islam but not emigrate, so he would not inherit from his brother. This was abrogated by His statement:
h
And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the decree of God than the believers and the emigrants (al-Ahzab 33

c: Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a man who had entered Islam and said: You establish prayer, pay zakat, perform Hajj to the House, and fast Ramadan, and you will not see the fire of a polytheist except that you are at war.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if they seek your help in religion
, meaning: If the Muslim Bedouins seek your help, O Muhajireen and Ansar, against your enemy, then you must help them, except against a people between you and whom there is a covenant.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, left the people on the day he died in four categories: a believing emigrant, the Ansar, and a believing Bedouin who did not emigrate. If the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sought his help, he would help him, and if he left him, it was his permission. If the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sought his help in religion, it was his right to help him, and that is what He said:
h
And if they seek your help in religion
, then it is your duty to help them. The fourth category: those who follow them in righteousness.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Those who believed and emigrated

, to the end of the surah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and left people in four categories: a believing emigrant, a Muslim Bedouin, those who gave shelter and aided, and those who followed in righteousness.
